# M2 live report: real Claude on the walkthrough and the demo (turn 13)

*Written 2026-11-13 (turn 15) about the work of turn 13, 2026-11-10. During turn 13 you asked to skip the write-ups until the demo worked; this is that write-up. Times are UTC (the machine's clock runs at UTC−8). The code described is the working tree of 2026-11-13: turn 13's changes, uncommitted, on top of your commit "initial generation" of 2026-11-05. The project report (`docs/project-report.md`) is updated to match.*

## In brief

- **The real-Claude walkthrough of `docs/m2-plan.md` §12 passed both readings** on a copy of the Spyro sample. Normative: two questions, proved in round 1, Accept made the goal a Derivation. Literal: one question, not proved, Claude suggested the missing premise, the scripted user adopted it, and round 2 proved the goal.
- **The demo passed twice, live, through the real extension UI** in your own snap VS Code (1.145.2), each on a fresh empty folder: "Socrates is mortal" (proved in round 1) and "Tweety can fly" (not proved, with the suggested premise "All penguins are birds"; adopted; proved in round 2). In both, Claude built the vocabulary from nothing.
- **Every one of the 6 rounds passed telelean's gate at its first attempt.** The four sessions took 35 requests and about 4 minutes of wall time, and Claude Code estimated $0.63 at API list prices. The plan had estimated 30–55 requests and 10–30 minutes for the walkthrough alone.
- **Turn 13 also fixed what the Spyro sample could not reveal** (section 5), found by testing the demo's path, a freshly typed model, with a scripted Claude: Accept refused cards typed while Claude worked; Lean's index hides some declarations, which the gate then refused; a misleading message for a blank line; four lines of the system prompt; a run could start Claude where Lean's sandbox cannot run; and wrong advice after a conflict.
- **The machine matters** (section 6): on this Ubuntu, Lean's sandbox works only inside the VS Code snap, a fresh folder must be trusted, and the demo belongs in a new window.
- **What this does not show** (section 4): that the formalisations say what the sentences mean. The penguin run is the plain example: the gate certified "Tweety can fly" from "All birds can fly", read with no exceptions. It also does not show the paths that never came up live (failed checks, Feedback, Cancel, resume), and it is one run per example.

## 1. Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Model and effort | `claude-opus-5-5` (Opus 5.5), effort high: the extension's defaults. Caps at their defaults (per round: 25 Lean checks, 80 turns, 20 minutes, 3 check attempts) |
| Claude Code | 2.1.322, the binary of the VS Code Claude Code extension (`~/.vscode/extensions/anthropic.claude-code-2.1.322-linux-x64/resources/native-binary/claude`), logged in with your claude.ai subscription |
| Lean | `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0`, every job sandboxed as always |
| Machine | Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`. The runs were started from the main session's shell, which runs inside the snap VS Code, so they had its AppArmor label `snap.code.code (complain)` (section 6) |
| Walkthrough | `scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --live` (both opt-ins: `--live` and `TELELEAN_WALKTHROUGH_LIVE=yes`), one reading per invocation. Each reading gets its own copy of `mental_model/` with its own git repository; the script drives the RunManager directly, without VS Code |
| Demo | `packages/extension/scripts/demo-driver.mjs --live --vscode snap` (both opt-ins: `--live` and `TELELEAN_DEMO_LIVE=yes`). It starts your installed snap VS Code 1.145.2 (snap revision 278) through the snap's own `electron-launch`, headless under xvfb, with telelean loaded from `packages/extension`. VS Code's user data, extensions, XDG folders and the snap's per-user folders stay in the run's work folder; HOME is the real one, because Claude Code's login lives there. The driver then works the UI like a user: a fresh empty folder, **telelean: Initialize Model Here** through the Command Palette (subject `Demo`), the cards typed in the A\|D\|G box, the selection, **These suffice ▶**, the real consent dialog, the review, Accept, and a wait for Lean's check of the accepted files |

**Pre-checks, before anything spent quota:**
- the two runner test files that spawn the live scripts to show that live mode refuses (`walkthroughScript.test.ts`, `smokeScript.test.ts`): 11/11 passed;
- `walkthrough-claude.mjs --dry-run`: both readings passed with the FakeBackend and real Lean;
- `--dry-run --binary-check`: it found Claude Code 2.1.322, and every command-line flag telelean passes was still valid on it.

**Order (2026-11-10, UTC).** The walkthrough ran on the code as it was; the fixes of section 5 came after it; the demo ran on the rebuilt extension, which had all of them.

| Time | What |
|---|---|
| 16:38 | turn 13 starts: "a minimal prototype for demo purposes with a real Claude backend as soon as possible" |
| 16:41–16:42 | walkthrough, normative reading (live) |
| 16:42 | the demo-readiness workflow starts, with no real Claude: three agents in parallel (fresh-model, snap-vscode, demo-driver), then an integrator |
| 16:43–16:44 | walkthrough, literal reading (live) |
| 17:09–18:03 | the fixes of section 5 land in the sources |
| 18:05 | the integrator rebuilds the extension bundle that VS Code loads |
| 18:35 | the workflow ends; every suite passes (section 7) |
| 18:36 | live demo: Socrates |
| 18:37–18:38 | live demo: the penguin |

## 2. Results

### 2.1 The four runs

| Run | Rounds | Questions | Gate | Requests | Cache read | Cache write | Output tokens | CLI cost estimate | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Walkthrough, normative | 1: proved | 2 | passed at attempt 1 | 8 | 76,240 | 13,686 | 2,924 | $0.183 | 46 s |
| Walkthrough, literal | 2: not proved; suggestion adopted; proved | 1 | passed at attempt 1, both rounds | 11 | 128,804 | 7,510 | 3,886 | $0.164 | 61 s |
| Demo, Socrates | 1: proved | 0 | passed at attempt 1 | 6 | 47,221 | 11,704 | 1,913 | $0.141 | ~52 s |
| Demo, penguin | 2: not proved; suggestion adopted; proved | 0 | passed at attempt 1, both rounds | 10 | 102,775 | 6,848 | 3,388 | $0.143 | ~76 s |
| **All four** | 6 | 3 | 6 of 6 at the first attempt | **35** | 355,040 | 39,748 | 12,111 | **$0.632** | ~4 min |

- **Where the numbers come from.** Tokens, requests and cost are from Claude Code's own record of each session (uncached input was 74 tokens in all). The cost is the CLI's estimate at API list prices; a subscription is not billed per token, but the runs use the plan's usage.
- **Wall time.** For the walkthrough, the script's time per reading: copy, Lean refresh, run, Accept and the final refresh. For the demo, the driver's time from VS Code's start to Lean's check after Accept.
- **Rate limits.** Both scripts cancel a run at the first usage-limit status that is not "allowed"; none was cancelled. The plan's 7-day window showed 4% used after the walkthrough and 7% after the demo. That figure covers everything the plan did in the window, including the Claude Code sessions that did the work, not only these runs.

### 2.2 Walkthrough, normative reading

The selection is the sample's: target "Cynder would not be a good addition to the new Spyro game", premises "PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts" (no Lean yet, stance *rule*), "Cynder is a character who has a dark past" and "The new Spyro game is PG".

1. **Question 1** (tag *word-sense*): *"In "PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts", what does "cannot have" mean for the goal about Cynder being a good addition?"* The options were "Such a character would not be a good addition" (the goal then follows) and "Such a character is never actually in the game" (a new "appears in" relation; the goal would need a further premise). The script answers every question that mentions "cannot" in its own words: *"I mean it as a rule: PG games should not include characters with dark pasts. I do not mean it is impossible for a PG game to contain one."*
2. **Question 2** (tag *enthymeme*): *"Should "PG games should not include characters with dark pasts" be read as saying such a character would not be a good addition to a PG game?"* (options "Yes, same thing" / "No, 'should not include' is separate"). The script answers every other question with **Decide for me**. Claude chose "Yes" and listed that choice under "assumed without asking".
3. **Formalisation**, directly below the rule's block in `Main.lean`:

   ```lean
   /-- PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts -/
   abbrev pg_no_dark_past : Prop :=
     ∀ (c : Character) (g : Game), IsPG g → HasDarkPast c → ¬ GoodAddition c g
   axiom pg_no_dark_past.holds : pg_no_dark_past
   ```

   One `check_lean` passed; `freeze_statements` returned 13 permitted names, the same set as the scripted run of project-report §3.8.
4. **Proof**, after the freeze; `check_lean` reported its footprint, the same 11 names as the scripted run:

   ```lean
   theorem cynder_not_good.holds : cynder_not_good :=
     pg_no_dark_past.holds cynder newSpyro new_spyro_pg.holds cynder_dark_past.holds
   ```
5. **`finish(proved)`**; the gate passed at attempt 1. The script accepted with the recommended "Make Derivation". After Accept the copy's refresh showed the goal proved, a DERIVATION, resting on the three premises plus the presuppositions `Spyro.Character.exists` and `Spyro.Game.exists`. These are exactly the pass criteria of m2-plan §12.2 step 4.

### 2.3 Walkthrough, literal reading

1. **Question** (tag *word-sense*): *"In "PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts", what does "have" mean?"*, with the options "Feature in the game" and "Not a good addition". The scripted answer: *"I mean it literally: a PG game cannot contain a character with a dark past at all."*
2. **Formalisation.** One new relation in `Vocabulary.lean`, then the rule:

   ```lean
   /-- can contain (the game is allowed to contain the character) -/
   axiom CanContain : Game → Character → Prop
   ```
   ```lean
   /-- PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts -/
   abbrev pg_no_dark_past : Prop :=
     ∀ (g : Game) (c : Character), IsPG g → HasDarkPast c → ¬ CanContain g c
   axiom pg_no_dark_past.holds : pg_no_dark_past
   ```

   The freeze returned 14 permitted names (`CanContain` joins the signature).
3. **Suggested premise** (`propose_assumption`): *"A character can only be a good addition to a game that can contain them"*, `∀ (c : Character) (g : Game), GoodAddition c g → CanContain g c`, with the gap proof `fun h hg => pg_no_dark_past.holds newSpyro cynder new_spyro_pg.holds cynder_dark_past.holds (h cynder newSpyro hg)`. telelean's scratch check confirmed that it closes the gap; its Lean name, derived from the sentence, is `a_character_can_only_be_a`.
4. **`finish(not_proved)`** with the gap *"Nothing links what a game can contain with which characters would be good additions to it."* The gate passed.
5. **Adoption.** The script pressed the equivalent of **I hold this** ("it seems obvious to me"). telelean wrote the card into the working copy before the target's block, worded by Claude, declared it on the target and froze again. Round 2's proof:

   ```lean
   theorem cynder_not_good.holds : cynder_not_good := fun hg =>
     pg_no_dark_past.holds newSpyro cynder new_spyro_pg.holds cynder_dark_past.holds
       (a_character_can_only_be_a.holds cynder newSpyro hg)
   ```

   Its footprint is 13 names: the normative 11, plus `CanContain` and the adopted card's `.holds`. The gate passed at attempt 1; after Accept the goal was proved and a DERIVATION, and the adopted card an Assumption worded by Claude (m2-plan §12.2 step 5).

### 2.4 Demo: Socrates, on a fresh folder

The driver typed A "All humans are mortal", A "Socrates is a human" and G "Socrates is mortal" into a model just made by Initialize (no vocabulary at all), selected all three and pressed **These suffice ▶**.

- **No question.** Claude read "All humans are mortal" as a rule without exceptions and said so under "assumed without asking", together with its choice of one sort for everything.
- **Vocabulary, created from nothing** (`Model/Demo/Vocabulary.lean`):

  ```lean
  /-- Beings (things that may be human or mortal). -/
  axiom Being : Type
  axiom Being.exists : Nonempty Being
  instance : Nonempty Being := Being.exists

  /-- `Human x`: x is a human. -/
  axiom Human : Being → Prop
  /-- `Mortal x`: x is mortal. -/
  axiom Mortal : Being → Prop

  /-- Socrates. -/
  noncomputable opaque socrates : Being
  ```
- **Statements and proof** (`Model/Demo/Inbox.lean`, each directly below its card's block):

  ```lean
  abbrev all_humans_are_mortal : Prop := ∀ x : Being, Human x → Mortal x
  axiom all_humans_are_mortal.holds : all_humans_are_mortal
  abbrev socrates_is_a_human : Prop := Human socrates
  axiom socrates_is_a_human.holds : socrates_is_a_human
  abbrev socrates_is_mortal : Prop := Mortal socrates
  theorem socrates_is_mortal.holds : socrates_is_mortal :=
    all_humans_are_mortal.holds socrates socrates_is_a_human.holds
  ```
- **The checks.** The freeze permitted 9 names; the proof rests on the two premises and the presupposition `Demo.Being.exists`. The gate passed at attempt 1 and flagged `Demo.Being.exists` as the one definition question; the driver answered **Yes, I endorse it** (its default). After Accept, Lean re-checked the files and the goal was proved.

### 2.5 Demo: the penguin

A "All birds can fly", A "Tweety is a penguin", G "Tweety can fly", in a fresh folder.

- **No question.** Claude again chose the strict reading of "All birds can fly" and listed it under "assumed without asking", with "penguin" as its own predicate, because no card says penguins are birds.
- **Vocabulary:** `axiom Animal : Type` with `Animal.exists` and its instance; `Bird`, `Penguin`, `CanFly : Animal → Prop`; `noncomputable opaque tweety : Animal`.
- **Statements:** `all_birds_can_fly := ∀ x : Animal, Bird x → CanFly x` and `tweety_is_a_penguin := Penguin tweety`, each with its `.holds`, and `tweety_can_fly := CanFly tweety`.
- **Round 1: not proved.** Gap: *"Nothing in the premises says Tweety is a bird."* Suggested premise: *"All penguins are birds"*, `∀ x : Animal, Penguin x → Bird x` (Lean name `all_penguins_are_birds`, gap proof `fun h => all_birds_can_fly.holds tweety (h tweety tweety_is_a_penguin.holds)`), checked by telelean to close the gap.
- **Round 2,** after **I hold this**:

  ```lean
  theorem tweety_can_fly.holds : tweety_can_fly :=
    all_birds_can_fly.holds tweety (all_penguins_are_birds.holds tweety tweety_is_a_penguin.holds)
  ```

  The footprint is the three cards plus `Demo.Animal.exists`. The gate passed at attempt 1 in both rounds; the driver endorsed `Demo.Animal.exists` and accepted, and Lean re-checked the files with the goal proved.
- **Claude's own warning,** in its summary: *"Under that reading the cards conclude that a penguin can fly, which isn't true of real penguins. If you meant "birds typically fly", that card would need to be weaker."*

### 2.6 Against the plan's estimate

m2-plan §12.3 estimated the walkthrough before anything had been measured.

| Both readings together | Estimate | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Requests | 10–20 (normative) and 20–35 (literal) | 8 and 11 |
| Cache-read tokens | 0.5–1.5 M | 205,044 |
| Cache-write tokens | 50–150 k | 21,196 |
| Output tokens | 20–60 k | 6,810 |
| Wall time per reading | 5–15 minutes | 46 s and 61 s |

## 3. What the runs show

- **The harness works with the real CLI.** telelean's way of driving Claude Code (stream-json, its MCP tool server, the path guard, the subscription and hook checks before the first prompt) carried four complete sessions on Claude Code 2.1.322. Until turn 13 it had met only a node test double and M0's eight-request smoke test.
- **The protocol works with a real model.** Claude used the tools as the system prompt asks: questions before formalising (walkthrough), `check_lean`, one freeze per round, proofs only after it, `propose_assumption` with a gap proof, and `finish` with an honest status. All of it was accepted at the first attempt.
- **A fresh model works.** On an empty folder Claude created sorts with their existence presupposition and instance, predicates and opaque constants exactly in the shapes the gate accepts, and put the statements directly below the cards' blocks in `Inbox.lean`.
- **The suggestion path works end to end:** the suggestion, telelean's scratch check, adoption, the second freeze and the round-2 proof, twice.
- **The extension's live path works in your own VS Code:** Initialize on an empty folder (palette, subject input, git dialog), typed cards, the consent dialog, finding Claude Code, the preflight (including turn 13's sandbox probe), the run panel, the review with a definition approval, I hold this, Accept and Lean's re-check.
- **It is cheap and quick:** about $0.14–$0.18 per run at API list prices, under a minute and a half each.

## 4. What the runs do not show

- **That the formalisations are faithful.** The gate certifies "proved from the selected premises *as formalised*" (project report §3.7 item 1); the runs show its limits:
  - **The penguin.** Read with no exceptions, "All birds can fly" plus the adopted "All penguins are birds" proves "Tweety can fly", which is false of real penguins. The proof is valid; the premise, as formalised, is what is wrong. Claude said so in its summary and under "assumed without asking"; nothing else in telelean would have.
  - **No questions in the demo.** In both demo runs Claude asked nothing: it chose the strict reading of "All …" and listed it under "assumed without asking". The dry run's scripted Claude asks a genericity question here, so the dry run is no guide to when the real one asks.
  - **The literal reading.** The scripted answer said a PG game *cannot contain* such a character *at all*. Claude glossed its new relation as permission ("the game is allowed to contain the character") and listed "'cannot have' as 'is not allowed to contain'" under "assumed without asking". Nothing checks that a formalisation follows an answer (§3.6, "Questions and decisions").
- **A human's review.** Every answer, every definition approval, every adoption and every Accept came from a script: the walkthrough's fixed answers, and the driver's defaults (option 1, **Yes, I endorse it**, **I hold this**, Accept). Nobody read the statements before accepting.
- **Paths that never came up live:**
  - the gate failing, Claude retrying, the give-up and the revert (every round passed at its first attempt);
  - Feedback, Cancel, a window reload and `--resume`, usage-limit warnings;
  - a real model attempting any of the cheats (the cheat catalogue is played by the FakeBackend only);
  - the board-edit merge, the `.ilean` fix and the blank-line findings of section 5 (none was needed in these runs);
  - the "Self-evident?" button, "Leave it open", and a "No" to a definition;
  - other models or efforts, larger models, and the 1.140.0 test build (the live demo ran in the snap).
- **Repeatability.** Each example ran once, and model behaviour varies from run to run.
- **The walkthrough ran on the code before turn 13's fixes;** it bundles the runner from the sources when it starts. It did not need any of them. The demo ran with all of them.

**Smaller observations from the transcripts.**
- In the Socrates run Claude rewrote `Inbox.lean` and `Vocabulary.lean` whole with Write instead of editing them. It reproduced every block byte for byte, so the markup rule (G5) passed. That rule, not the choice of tool, is what protects your words.
- The first message's example of a presupposition is the fixed text "there is at least one character" in every run, also for a model about humans or animals. This is cosmetic; it confused nothing.

## 5. Turn 13's fixes

All were found without real Claude. The fresh-model agent wrote FakeBackend scripts in which a well-behaved Claude follows the system prompt on a freshly initialised model with typed cards: the demo's path, which the Spyro sample never takes. They ran against the real RunManager, gate (with sandboxed Lean), proposal service and Accept. The snap agent ran the VS Code suites in your snap VS Code. The integrator applied the reports, rebuilt and re-ran everything.

### 5.1 Lean's index hides some declarations: a false rejection

- **Symptom.** Lean 4.35's `.ilean` index leaves some top-level declarations whose source mentions no constant out of its declaration table (`decls`). Examples: `abbrev two_plus_two_is_four : Prop := 2 + 2 = 4`, `theorem t : 2 + 2 = 4 := by decide`, and `theorem plain_mp : ∀ (p q : Prop), p → (p → q) → q := …`. Yet `abbrev q : Prop := True` and `axiom P0 : Prop` are listed, so the exact rule is unknown. telelean's facts then lacked these declarations, and check, freeze and the gate refused them fail-closed: *"Lean reported nothing about …"*. Arithmetic or purely logical examples, and generic helper lemmas, could not pass.
- **Change.** Such a declaration still has a `references` entry for itself whose definition has no parent. Runner `semantic/ilean.ts` now reports it as `unlisted`, skipping `example` (`<namespace>._example`) and private names. `semantic/refresh.ts` (`declDrafts`) takes its full range, docstring and keyword from core's declaration scanner, the one the board uses. It keeps the declaration only when the source declares that name, so a name Lean generates (for example by `deriving`) never appears. From then on the check file probes it like any other declaration.
- **Why this is safe.** The facts (type, kind, value, axioms) still come from Lean's own `#check`, `#print` and `#print axioms`; only the source range comes from telelean's scanner. The recorded Spyro and extras facts did not change.
- **Tests.** Two new cases in `ilean.test.ts` on an `.ilean` recorded from Lean 4.35 (`test-fixtures/semantic/recorded/unlisted-Inbox.*`). Fresh scenario (g), `arith.json`, fails without the fix ("Lean reported nothing about Demo.two_plus_two_is_four") and passes with it.

### 5.2 Accept refused cards typed during a run (demo-breaking)

- **Symptom.** Accept merges Claude's changes onto your current files with a 3-line-context patch and no fuzz, so an edit of yours within 3 lines of one of Claude's is a conflict. On a freshly typed `Inbox.lean` every card sits within 3 lines of Claude's formalisation. A card added with the A|D|G box, or a reason written on a card, while Claude worked therefore refused the Accept. The board does not lock editing during a run, and it asks for a reason on every assumption. All three exploratory cases were conflicts.
- **Change** (runner `proposal/files.ts`: `mergeFile`, new `boardEditsOf`). When the plain patch cannot be placed, the board's own edits are taken out of your text:
  - **added cards:** a run of new comment-only blocks (an id the base does not have, `id:` written, no `lean:`, bound to nothing) that ends the file's namespace, which is where the A|D|G box puts them;
  - **reasons:** `rationale:` written, changed or removed on an existing card, where the block reads exactly as at the start once its rationale is set back.

  Claude's patch is applied to the rest, and the edits are put back by card id: reasons with the field editor, cards at the end of the namespace. The result must read exactly as you wrote it, or it is a conflict. **Every other edit within 3 lines is still a conflict**, above all a changed sentence next to Claude's formalisation of it. As before, Accept then normalises, re-freezes and re-runs the gate on the merged files, with your files at Accept as the base.
- **Tests.** `boardEdits.test.ts` (6 tests). Fresh scenario (b) adds a card and a reason while Claude works, and Accept keeps both. The existing conflict tests of `accept.test.ts` still pass.

### 5.3 A misleading message for a blank line

- **Symptom.** If Claude's statement is separated from a selected card's block by one blank line, the block binds nothing (TL013). check and freeze then called the assumption's `.holds` *"a Prop-valued axiom (a belief) … propose a missing premise with propose_assumption instead"*, and the card one that *"has no Lean statement"*. Claude could have deleted the very axiom it needed.
- **Change** (core `gate/rules.ts`, `gate/describe.ts`). A chosen card left without code only by such a gap now gets `new-axiom` and `not-formalised` findings with the token `detached`. They say to remove the blank line and keep the axiom; the board's sentence is *"it left a blank line between “…” and its Lean statement"*. The codes and the verdicts are unchanged.
- **Tests.** Core `rules.test.ts` and `describe.test.ts`. Fresh scenario (h), `variants.json`, makes the mistake on purpose: one failed check and one refused freeze, both naming the blank line, then fixed.

### 5.4 The system prompt disagreed with the gate in four places

The four lines (runner `run/systemPrompt.ts` and `docs/m2-plan.md` §5.1, which a test keeps identical):
1. **Step 3** now says where typed cards are: *"cards typed on the board sit in the subject's Inbox.lean: formalise them there"*.
2. **Step 3** also says how a selected Goal or Derivation premise without Lean is used: *"may be formalised the same way (no `.holds` axiom) and proved after the freeze"*. The gate already accepted that.
3. **Step 5** allows the proof *"(or lower in the file, below everything it uses)"*. When the goal is typed before its premises, a proof "right after the target's statement" does not build, because the premises' `.holds` come later in the file; that cost a check.
4. **The vocabulary rule** lists propositions `axiom P : Prop`, which the gate accepts. It says *"The person confirms each new `T.exists`"*, and that only *other* definitions and instances are questions. The old line said every `instance` is a question, which contradicted the required presupposition instance.

### 5.5 A run could start Claude where Lean's sandbox cannot run

- **Symptom** (snap agent). This kernel restricts unprivileged user namespaces through AppArmor. An unconfined `bwrap` fails with *"setting up uid map: Permission denied"* (and *"loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted"*). The preflight only checked that the programs exist, so outside the snap VS Code a run would pass it, start Claude (spending quota), and then fail at its first Lean job.
- **Change** (runner `lean/runLean.ts`, `run/preflight.ts`).
  - `checkUserNamespaces()` runs `bwrap` once, with the real profile's namespace flags and system mounts, on `/usr/bin/true`. It runs straight from the extension host, whose AppArmor label a run's `bwrap` inherits, and caches a success.
  - The run preflight calls it after the tools check. A failure refuses the run before anything is sent: *"Lean's sandbox is not available, so telelean cannot check Claude's work: bwrap cannot set up the sandbox here (…)"*. When the sysctl is 1 it adds: *"this kernel lets only some programs create user namespaces (AppArmor: kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1): run telelean in the VS Code snap, whose processes may create them, or give bwrap an AppArmor profile that allows it"*.
  - The same sentence is appended when any Lean job's `bwrap` fails that way, so the board's "Lean: off" reason ("sandbox unavailable: …") explains it too.
- **Tests.** `userns.test.ts` (6 tests), and the host-environment suite asserts the probe in the snap and in the test build.

### 5.6 Wrong advice after a conflict

- **Symptom.** Both Accept refusals, an overlap and a failed re-check after drift, advised *"Discard, or Feedback to redo it on your current files"*. Feedback continues on Claude's working copy; it never moves onto your files, so the next Accept met the same conflict.
- **Change.** *"…; Discard, or undo those edits and Accept again."* (`proposal/files.ts`) and *"… Discard, or undo your edits since the run started and Accept again."* (`run/manager.ts`). The test, the user guide, the plan's §7.1 and the project report say the same. Feedback itself still does not rebase (section 9).

### 5.7 New: the demo, its driver and `npm run demo`

- **`docs/DEMO.md`:** the five-minute demo with your own example (new window, fresh trusted folder, Initialize, typing cards, These suffice, answering, the review, Accept or I hold this), what to expect with measured timings, tips for good examples, and troubleshooting.
- **`packages/extension/scripts/demo-driver.mjs`** (with `demo-ui.mjs` for the workbench and board over the DevTools protocol, and `demo-vscode.mjs` for the isolated instance) plays the whole demo in a separate VS Code window. It prints a JSON summary (verdicts, questions and answers, suggestions, the final Lean, statuses after Accept, times, usage) and saves screenshots. Its modes:
  - `--dry-run` (the default): VS Code's Test mode, the only mode in which a backend other than the real Claude can be installed. An agent inside VS Code (`test/demo/agent.ts`) installs a scripted "Claude" (`test/demo/demoClaude.ts`), answers in advance the git and consent questions Test mode never shows, and runs Initialize with arguments, since Test mode has no folder picker. Everything else goes through the board. The scripted Claude handles syllogisms and chains, with a genericity question whose answer changes the result, and anything else as whole sentences joined by a linking premise; real Lean and the real gate judge its work.
  - `--rehearse`: the exact live path in Development mode (palette, folder pick, subject input, git dialog, the real consent dialog) up to the run's start, which the quota tripwire must then refuse before any Claude binary is looked up.
  - `--live`: the same, then the real run. It needs both `--live` and `TELELEAN_DEMO_LIVE=yes`, refuses while `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE` is armed, uses the real HOME (Claude Code's login), and cancels at the first usage-limit warning unless `--continue-on-rate-warning`.
- **Defaults:** option 1 for each question; **Yes, I endorse it** for definitions (`--no-approve-definitions` stops instead); **I hold this** on a gap-closing suggestion (`--no-adopt`); Accept (`--end discard`). `--vscode test-build|snap|<binary>` chooses the VS Code.
- **`npm run demo`** (in `packages/extension`) runs the driver.

### 5.8 New: the VS Code suites in your own snap VS Code

- **`npm run test:smoke:snap`** (`scripts/smoke.mjs --snap`, with `scripts/snap-env.mjs`) runs the smoke and end-to-end instances in your installed snap VS Code instead of the downloaded 1.140.0 build. It starts the snap through its own `electron-launch` with the variables `snap run` sets, and keeps the snap's per-user folders in the isolated HOME. Running `snap run` itself would always use the real `~/snap/code`, because snapd takes the home folder from the password database.
- **New host-environment suite** (`test/suite/hostEnv.test.ts`, in both modes). It records what the extension host inherited, then checks the Lean sandbox (tools, the userns probe, a sandboxed `lean --version`), that Claude's cleaned environment keeps no snap variable or path, and the path guard's self-test under the chosen hook runtime and under the Electron-as-Node fallback.
- **`smoke.mjs`** now reports the AppArmor label and cgroup it ran under, warns when it runs unconfined on a userns-restricted kernel, watches `~/.vscode` and (snap mode) `~/snap/code` as well, and removes a Chromium shared-memory file its own instance left in `/dev/shm` that no process uses.
- **A harness leak, fixed.** The test instances inherited the variables of a Claude Code session that started them (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, a messaging socket and token, …); they now drop every `CLAUDE*`, `MCP_*` and `AI_AGENT` variable.
- No snap-specific failure needed a fix in the extension itself.

### 5.9 New: nine fresh-model scenarios

`packages/runner/test/run/fresh.e2e.test.ts` plays `test-fixtures/fresh/*.json`. Each starts from an empty folder: Initialize, the board's own add-card actions, These suffice, the real RunManager and gate with sandboxed Lean, Accept, a refresh and the board's statuses.
- (a) Socrates, with Undo and Redo, then Plato in the same model;
- (b) a chain with a named lemma and a tactic proof, plus a card and a reason typed while Claude works;
- (c) the penguin, with a question, a suggestion and adoption;
- (d) "Self-evident?" that is not;
- (e) the goal typed first;
- (f) a propositional example with a Derivation target;
- (g) arithmetic, self-evident;
- (h) honest variants a real Claude may write;
- (i) an intermediate step typed as a Derivation and selected.

A well-behaved Claude is never refused, apart from the mistakes the scripts make on purpose.

## 6. Environment findings

1. **Lean's sandbox works only inside the VS Code snap on this machine.** With `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1` (Ubuntu 24.04), `bwrap` may create its user namespaces only under an AppArmor profile that allows it. The snap VS Code's processes, and everything they start, run as `snap.code.code (complain)`, which does. A VS Code started any other way, a script from GNOME Terminal or over ssh, or a transient systemd service fails. The preflight now says so before a run starts (5.5); the board's checks have always failed closed ("Lean: off").
2. **A fresh folder must be trusted.** telelean does not run in Restricted Mode (`untrustedWorkspaces.supported: false`), so its commands are missing until you trust the folder. The test instances run with workspace trust off, so no automated test covers this; the demo driver's `--rehearse` and `--live` do.
3. **Open the demo in a new window** (File → New Window). **Developer: Reload Window** also restarts everything else running in that window, including a Claude Code session there.
4. **Your VS Code is the snap 1.145.2** (Electron 43.8.3, revision 278), newer than the 1.140.0 test build; both pass every suite. The extension host's environment holds the snap's variables (`SNAP*`, `GTK_*`, `GDK_*`, `LOCPATH`, `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, …). telelean's cleaning removes all of them from Claude Code's environment, and the hook runtime it picks there is `~/.local/bin/node`.
5. **Claude Code** was 2.1.322 for every run. As of 2026-11-13 2.1.323 is installed as well; telelean takes the newest extension binary and requires only 2.1.295 or newer.
6. **Harmless noise:** VS Code 1.145.2 prints an "InstantiationService has been disposed" stack when the raw-diff tab closes (VS Code's own bug). Once, a test instance left a Chromium file in `/dev/shm` at shutdown; `smoke.mjs` now cleans that up (5.8).

Lean's `.ilean` index adds positions and the references between declarations.

**Declarations the index leaves out (turn 13).** Lean 4.35's `.ilean` leaves some top-level declarations out of its declaration table (`decls`) when their source mentions no constant: `abbrev two_plus_two_is_four : Prop := 2 + 2 = 4`, `theorem t : 2 + 2 = 4 := by decide`, `theorem plain_mp : ∀ (p q : Prop), p → (p → q) → q := …`. Yet `abbrev q : Prop := True` and `axiom P0 : Prop` are listed, so the exact rule is unknown. Such a declaration still has a `references` entry for itself whose definition has no parent. telelean now reports it as an *unlisted* declaration (never an `example`, never a private name), takes its full range from its own declaration scanner (the one the board uses), and keeps it only when the source declares that name. The check file then probes it like any other declaration. Before this fix these declarations had no facts, so check, freeze and the gate refused them fail-closed ("Lean reported nothing about …"). The facts themselves still come from Lean; only the source range comes from the scanner.

## 32. Turn 13: the real-Claude walkthrough, the live demo, and the fixes and tools they needed (2026-11-10)

Turn 13's request was "a minimal prototype for demo purposes with a real Claude backend as soon as possible", with logging and write-ups skipped until the demo worked (they were done in turn 15). Sources: fresh-model, snap, demo driver and int are the four agents of the demo-readiness workflow (their reports: `verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_13/subagent_reports/demo_readiness_workflow/`); main is the main session. The results and every fix in detail: `docs/m2-live-report.md`.

- **Real Claude first on the code as it was (the m2-plan §12 walkthrough, both readings), then a quota-free workflow for the demo's path, then live runs of typed-in examples through the extension.** The walkthrough showed the Spyro path works with the real Claude. The demo's path is a fresh model with typed cards and no vocabulary, which the sample never exercises, so it was played first with scripted Claudes against the real gate. Every live run was announced first and run one at a time. *(main)*
- **Declarations that Lean 4.35 leaves out of the `.ilean` declaration table are recovered from their own reference entry (a definition with no parent), with the full range from telelean's own declaration scanner, and kept only when the source declares that name.** Such declarations (source without any constant: `2 + 2 = 4`, a lemma over plain `Prop`s) had no facts, so check, freeze and the gate refused them fail-closed. The facts still come from Lean's own probes of the name; only the source range comes from the scanner. `example` and private names are skipped, as before. The exact rule Lean follows is unknown (`axiom P0 : Prop` and `abbrev q : Prop := True` are listed). *(fresh-model)*
- **When Accept's 3-line patch cannot be placed, the board's own edits are taken out, the patch is applied to the rest, and they are put back by card id.** On a freshly typed Inbox every card sits within 3 lines of Claude's formalisation, so a card added or a reason written while Claude worked made every such Accept a conflict. Yet the board does not lock editing during a run and asks for a reason on every assumption. The merged files are still normalised, re-frozen and re-gated with the person's files at Accept as the base. *(fresh-model)*
- **Only two kinds of edit count as the board's own: new comment-only blocks that end a namespace (where add-node puts them) and `rationale:` changes; everything else keeps the 3-line rule.** Neither kind has a formal effect. A sentence changed next to Claude's formalisation of it must stay a conflict: the formalisation may no longer fit it. The put-back result must reproduce the edits exactly, or it is a conflict. *(fresh-model)*
- **A blank line between a chosen card's block and its statement gets findings with the token `detached`, which name the blank line; the codes and verdicts are unchanged.** The old findings called the assumption's `.holds` a belief and told Claude to remove it (and to use `propose_assumption`), which would have deleted the very axiom it needed. *(fresh-model)*
- **The system prompt was changed in four lines to teach exactly what the gate accepts.** Typed cards are in `Inbox.lean`. A selected Goal or Derivation premise without Lean is formalised without `.holds` and proved after the freeze. The proof may sit lower in the file. Propositions `axiom P : Prop` are vocabulary. The person confirms each new `T.exists`, and only *other* definitions and instances are questions. The old text called every instance a question, which contradicted the required presupposition instance, and its "right after the target's statement" does not build when the goal was typed first. *(fresh-model)*
- **No change to the vocabulary shape rule (D-3) or to the `T.exists` question.** Vocabulary over built-in types (`Person → Nat`) stays refused, and every new sort's existence presupposition still needs the person's Yes before Accept. Both are by design; the demo guide says so instead. *(fresh-model, int)*
- **After a conflict at Accept, the advice is now "Discard, or undo those edits and Accept again" (and, for a failed re-check, "… undo your edits since the run started …"); Feedback is no longer offered.** Feedback continues on the run's working copy and never rebases onto the person's files, so it met the same conflict. Making Feedback rebase was the alternative; it is left for later. *(int, from fresh-model's finding)*
- **The run preflight probes `bwrap` once, straight from the extension host, before anything is sent to Claude; a success is cached.** On a kernel with AppArmor's user-namespace restriction (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, this Ubuntu), `bwrap` works only under a profile that allows it, such as the VS Code snap's. A run elsewhere used to pass the preflight, start Claude (spending quota) and fail at its first Lean job. The probe runs from the extension host because a run's `bwrap` inherits that process's AppArmor label. It uses the real profile's namespace flags and system mounts on `/usr/bin/true`. *(int, from snap's suggestion)*
- **The same plain hint is appended to any Lean job's "bwrap could not set up the sandbox" reason when that sysctl is 1.** The board's "Lean: off … sandbox unavailable" then explains itself. *(int)*
- **The VS Code suites can run in the user's own snap VS Code (`npm run test:smoke:snap`), started through the snap's `electron-launch` with the variables `snap run` sets, not through `snap run`.** `snap run` always uses the real `~/snap/code/<rev>` (snapd takes the home folder from the password database), and the snap's CLI detaches VS Code, so the test runner would lose the exit code. The snap's per-user folders go into the isolated HOME, and the real `~/snap/code` is watched, mtimes and ctimes included. *(snap)*
- **The VS Code test instances drop every `CLAUDE*`, `MCP_*` and `AI_AGENT` variable.** Run from a Claude Code session, they had inherited its session variables, a messaging token among them; the user's own VS Code has none. *(snap)*
- **`smoke.mjs` reports the AppArmor label and cgroup it ran under, warns when it runs unconfined on a userns-restricted kernel, and removes a Chromium shared-memory file its own instance left in `/dev/shm` if no process uses it.** Every Lean check of an unconfined run would fail. One such file was left once by the snap's VS Code 1.145.2 at shutdown. *(snap)*
- **The demo driver has three modes: `--dry-run`, `--rehearse` and `--live`.**
  - `--dry-run` uses Test mode with an agent inside VS Code and a scripted Claude.
  - `--rehearse` uses Development mode and follows the exact live UI path up to the consent; the quota tripwire must then refuse the run.
  - `--live` needs `--live` and `TELELEAN_DEMO_LIVE=yes`, refuses under the tripwire, uses the real HOME with VS Code's own profile isolated, and cancels at the first usage-limit warning.

  Test mode is the only mode in which a backend other than the real Claude can be installed. It never shows the git or consent dialogs and has no folder picker, so the dry-run agent answers those in advance, and `--rehearse` covers that path without quota. *(demo driver)*
- **No fake backend in Development mode, not even behind an environment variable.** It would weaken the rule that only Test mode can get a backend other than the real Claude, and `--rehearse` already covers the live UI path up to the consent. *(demo driver, int)*
- **The driver's defaults keep a demo moving:** option 1 for each question, **Yes, I endorse it** for definitions, **I hold this** on a gap-closing suggestion, Accept. Every fresh model brings at least one `T.exists` question, so a driver that stopped at definitions would never finish. `--no-approve-definitions`, `--no-adopt`, `--answer` and `--end discard` change them. *(demo driver)*
- **The dry run's "Claude" computes its steps while they play, from the first message and the working copy's files.** So the user's own simple example runs end to end without a model: syllogisms and chains, with a genericity question whose answer changes the result, and anything else as whole-sentence propositions joined by a linking premise. Real Lean and the real gate judge it. *(demo driver)*
- **`docs/DEMO.md` says to open the demo in a new window (File → New Window), not to reload.** Developer: Reload Window would also restart the Claude Code session running in that window. *(int)*
- **`npm run demo` runs the demo driver.** *(int)*
- **The extension bundle was rebuilt after the fixes, and the bundle was checked for the new behaviour.** The user's VS Code loads telelean from `packages/extension`, so without the rebuild the demo would have run without the fixes. *(int)*
- **The live demo ran in the user's snap VS Code (`--vscode snap`), from the main session's shell.** That shell runs inside the snap VS Code and so carries the AppArmor label `bwrap` needs; a plain terminal would have been refused at the preflight. *(main)*

#!/bin/bash
# One Lake build at a time, no telelean refresh: does a source file saved while `lake build` compiles leave a module
# whose trace matches the sources on disk but whose .olean was compiled from the other version (Lake then trusts it)?
# Scratch only. Versions: A = mental_model; B = A + one marker theorem in Vocabulary.lean and Main.lean.
set -u
S=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad/turn9/closing-verify-2

W=$S/tmp-probes/poison; rm -rf $W; mkdir -p $W/A $W/B
cp -r $S/repo/mental_model $W/model; rm -rf $W/model/.lake $W/model/.git
V=Model/Spyro/Vocabulary.lean; M=Model/Spyro/Main.lean
mkdir -p $W/A/Model/Spyro $W/B/Model/Spyro
cp $W/model/$V $W/A/$V; cp $W/model/$M $W/A/$M
python3 - "$W" <<'PY'
import sys; w=sys.argv[1]
v=open(f'{w}/A/Model/Spyro/Vocabulary.lean').read().rstrip()
assert v.endswith('end Spyro')
open(f'{w}/B/Model/Spyro/Vocabulary.lean','w').write(v[:-len('end Spyro')]+'theorem probe_variant_b_vocab : True := trivial\n\nend Spyro\n')
open(f'{w}/B/Model/Spyro/Main.lean','w').write(open(f'{w}/A/Model/Spyro/Main.lean').read()+'\ntheorem probe_variant_b_main : True := trivial\n')
PY
put() { cp $W/$1/$V $W/model/$V; cp $W/$1/$M $W/model/$M; }
marks() { python3 -c "
import sys,re
for f in ['Vocabulary','Main']:
    try: o=open('$W/model/.lake/build/lib/lean/Model/Spyro/'+f+'.olean','rb').read()
    except FileNotFoundError: print(f+':none',end=' '); continue
    print(f+':'+('B' if re.search(rb'probe_variant_b_\w+',o) else 'A'),end=' ')
"; }
cd $W/model
put A; lake build > /dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "initial build failed"; exit 1; }
poison=0; n=0
for i in $(seq 1 ${1:-30}); do
  for pair in "A B" "B A"; do
    set -- $pair
    put $1; lake build > /dev/null 2>&1 & bp=$!
    sleep 0.$(( (RANDOM % 9) + 1 )); put $2; wait $bp; n=$((n+1))
    # Which version does Lake now consider up to date, and what do the .olean files hold?
    for v in A B; do
      put $v
      if lake build --no-build > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        m=$(marks)
        bad=0; [ "$v" = A ] && [[ "$m" == *":B"* ]] && bad=1; [ "$v" = B ] && [[ "$m" == *":A"* ]] && bad=1
        [ $bad = 1 ] && { poison=$((poison+1)); echo "build $n (sources $1 then $2 during the build): with sources $v Lake builds nothing (--no-build passes) but the .olean files hold: $m"; }
      fi
    done
  done
done
echo "single-build flips: $n builds, $poison poisoned states found (Lake up to date for one version while an .olean holds the other)"
EOF

issues.description:
Item 1 (seed wording) is still partly untrue. With telelean.run.reuseLeanBuild on, a run can start from a compiled module that does not match the file in its working copy, and Lake does not rebuild it.

The reworded texts promise otherwise:
- the setting description and the user guide: "Lake still rebuilds whatever in the copy does not match the run's files";
- seed.ts, plan 4.2 and decisions-log 31: "correctness rests on Lake's per-module check".
The only exception they name is two Lake builds writing the same module at once.

I found a more ordinary one, with a single build:
1. The user saves a file while a terminal `lake build` is compiling it.
2. The user undoes the save.
3. Lake recorded the first text as the input but compiled the second, so with the first text back Lake trusts the wrong compiled file.

After that:
- telelean's refresh reports ok with every module fresh and records the tree;
- a run with the setting on seeds it;
- the run's own Lean facts, which the gate's checks read, describe the other version of the file.

The default (off) is not affected: the run builds from scratch and its facts match its files.

The board's own facts come from the same .lake/build, so the board has the same exposure. That is an M1 matter, outside these items. Any other Lake build of the folder, telelean's own refresh included, is probably exposed the same way; I did not test it.

Already known; the fixer flagged it as an open issue. The ghost's Lean name the board shows before adoption can differ from the name adoption writes.

Two checks pick the name:
- runner ghostName, at propose time, only checks that <S>.<name> and its .holds are not declared;
- core adoptionPlan also rejects a name used as an identifier anywhere in the files, or declared at the top level, and then derives a different name.

The card chip and the propose_assumption tool result then name the first one. The adoption turn and the ghost's stored name are corrected afterwards.

## 3. The prototype gate, exactly

Closing round 1: sections 3.1 to 3.3 were checked line by line against the code (core `gate/g0.ts`, `gate/permitted.ts`, `gate/rules.ts`, `gate/decls.ts`, `gate/normalise.ts`; runner `gate/engine.ts`, `gate/findings.ts`) and describe what it does; the fixer-round notes they collected are folded into the rules.

The gate runs on the shadow after `finish`; `check_lean` and `freeze_statements` run subsets of the same rules (core `evaluateRules`, purposes `check`, `freeze`, `gate-proved`, `gate-other`). Inputs: the run base B (exactly the user's files at run start, the shadow's `base` commit, with B's Lean facts from the run's base check; for Accept's re-check after drift, the user's files at Accept, the `accept-base` commit, without facts: section 7.1), the adoption reference A (the shadow at its newest `adopt` commit, when a ghost was adopted: telelean's own ghost blocks and declarations are checked against it, never against B), the round start R (the shadow when the round began; B in round 1), the shadow now S (after normalisation, as committed: the gate judges one committed state) with the build mirror's fresh Lean facts of S, the round's freeze F, the selection Sel (target T, premises P, adopted ghosts), the finish status.

**Why these checks make "proved" mean "proved from exactly the selection"** (the Prototype profile's central claim): the target's statement and every selected statement are frozen before any proof exists (`proof-before-freeze`, which also catches a proof carried inside a definition, instance or structure, and the freeze); a formalised card's statement cannot be swapped (`markup`: no `lean:` line changed, no card re-bound); `existing-changed` keeps every declaration the user had, by text and, with B's facts, by meaning; G4 checks the target theorem against the freeze with the permitted set computed from the freeze; `footprint` holds for every declaration the run adds or changes, whatever its kind or type (a definition, instance or structure can carry a proof too) and whatever the finish status; no `example` (a proof without a name, which no rule could check) is ever left in the files; and what the proposal shows is always a judged state (gate-pass files, or a reverted, normalised and re-checked passing state).

**Order and short-circuits** (runner `engine.runCheck`, then `engine.gate`): G0 (text only, core `checkFileChanges`) → if any G0 finding, stop: Lean never elaborates text that fails G0 → sync the build mirror (a working copy that cannot be synced is an environment outcome, section 3.6) → G1: one Lean job, `semantic.refreshLeanFacts` on `build/`; a runLean `timeout`/`oom` is a `budget` finding and stops the check there, and `could-not-start`, `low-memory`, a cancellation or an unsupported project stop it as environment outcomes → core `evaluateRules` on S's project model with the fresh facts: G1's Lean-error findings, G3, G5 and the readiness and stage rules (failing closed, the engine adds a `build` finding for any Lean error the rules did not report) → in the gate, `finish(proved)` without a freeze always carries `not-frozen` → only when there is no finding at all, the status is `proved` and the round has a freeze: G4 (lake comparator).

Only paths that differ between B and S are judged; S here is every regular file in ws/ (`ShadowWorkspace.currentFiles`), so a stray `notes.md` Claude wrote is a `bad-path` finding (counted), not an environment failure. ## 4. The runner: flows

### 4.1 Preflight (WP3 `runPreflight`; before anything is created or sent)

In order, each refusal a plain sentence (`PreflightOutcome`): (1) busy: another non-terminal run of the root; (2) selection: T is a GOAL or DERIVATION card of the subject (an ASSUMPTION is something the user holds: "make it a Derivation first (D-11), then prove it"), every premise is a card of the subject, T ∉ P; (3) workspace: the ModelWorkspace implements the M2 members and the subject loads; (4) toolchain: `lean-toolchain` is `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0` (D-7) and the project has no Lake dependencies (as M1); (5) sandbox: `lean.checkSandboxSupport()`; (6) memory: MemAvailable ≥ the guard. Only when all six pass does `start` obtain the backend (the factory, first start only; it runs nothing but `claude --version`) and then declare the premises (`set-premises`, when non-empty and different from the declared ones); a refusal at any of these steps leaves the user's files, the runs dir and the processes exactly as they were. Right after the shadow is created, `engine.checkBase` builds the user's files as they are (one Lean job, not counted): Lean errors anywhere in them end the run as `failed` before any prompt (Claude may not change the user's files, so every attempt would fail on them), and the facts are kept as B's facts. The CLI's own checks follow at session start (guard self-test, `initialize` account = claude.ai subscription, `get_hooks_listing` shows the guard): all before the first prompt, so a refusal costs no quota.

### 4.2 The shadow (WP2; layout in `runner/src/shadow/types.ts`)

`<runsDir>/<rootKey>/<runId>/{ws, build, git, session, frozen/<n>, gate/<n>, scratch, run.json}`; `runsDir` = `<globalStorage>/runs` in the extension (03 section 8.4), a scratch dir in tests.
- **ws/** (Claude's cwd and the guard's root): the base texts from the TextSource view (`ModelWorkspace.readText`, open buffers first) of every model file and the project files. No `.lake`, `.telelean`, `.git`, `.gitignore`: the root holds no dot-entry, so the M0 guard allows Grep/Glob on it (m0-report lesson 4).
- **build/**: the Lean mirror (the model files + `.lake/`, the run's own Lean build). Closing round 1 (decisions-log section 30; `runner/src/shadow/seed.ts`): the mirror starts **without** the user's `.lake/build`, so the run's first Lean job (the base check) builds the model from scratch, about a second for Spyro. Lake may be writing the user's `.lake/build` while a run starts (the board's refresh after a save, an Undo or the start's own premises declaration; the Lean extension; a terminal), and fixer round 3's checks of the live tree could not rule out copying a build in progress: with an outside `lake build` running, 98 of 99 seeds the final verifier's probe used were partial or mixed snapshots (Lake's own hash check made every result correct anyway). Seeding is kept only behind the setting `telelean.run.reuseLeanBuild` (default off; `RunSettings.reuseLeanBuild`, passed as `CreateShadowOptions.copyBuild`), and then only from telelean's own last refresh output, untouched since: the model workspace's refresh calls `noteRefreshOutput` inside its own Lean job (`semantic.runExclusive`), which records the tree (every directory and regular file: device, inode, size, mtime, ctime) only after a refresh with status `ok` and every module fresh, and only when the tree is a complete build (each fresh module has its `.olean`, `.ilean` and `.trace`, no artifact newer than its trace, no Lake lock, no temporary file younger than 10 minutes); any other refresh forgets the record. `createRunShadow` then copies the tree inside `semantic.runExclusive` only when a listing taken now equals the record, re-checks every file after its copy and lists the tree again, which must still equal the record (any write, create, remove or rename changes a file's or its directory's ctime). Anything else seeds nothing (`ShadowWorkspace.buildSeed.skipped` says why; the RunManager logs it): never a refusal, never a gate finding, only a slower first build. A symlink or special file in `.lake/build` only means no seed (nothing of it is copied; it no longer refuses the shadow). Before every Lean job `syncMirror()` copies changed model files (content compare, mtimes of unchanged files kept, removed files deleted) and refuses symlinks, special files and dot-entries in ws/. Files in ws/ that are not model files (a stray `notes.md`) never reach build/; `currentFiles()` still returns them so G0 can report them (`bad-path`, counted). Lean runs there with M1's in-place refresh (`semantic.refreshLeanFacts({ root: build, … })`: sources read-only, `.lake` writable) and M0's `freezeChallenge`/`runComparator`; facts are root-relative, so their paths are ws/ paths. No sandbox or runLean change is needed.
- **git/**: `GIT_DIR` of the shadow's history (work tree ws/), isolated config; commits `base`, `freeze`, `adopt`, `normalise`, `gate-pass`, `revert`, `accept-base`, `rebase`, `checkpoint`.
- **session/**: the CLI's run dir (confinement files, MCP config with the bearer token, system prompt) and `transcript.jsonl` (every user turn verbatim, every event, tool call and result, state change, with timestamps: "exact texts saved", 03 section 14).
- **Pruning**: after a run ends, keep the newest 10 run dirs of the root (`telelean.run.keepRuns`), never deleting a non-terminal one.

/-- Write a trace file containing metadata on an artifact fetched from a cache. -/
@[inline] public def writeFetchTrace (path : FilePath) (inputHash : Hash) (outputs : Json) : IO Unit :=
  BuildMetadata.writeFile path (.ofFetch inputHash outputs)

/-- Write a trace file containing metadata about a build. -/
@[inline] public def writeBuildTrace
  [ToJson α] (path : FilePath) (depTrace : BuildTrace) (outputs : α) (log : Log)
: IO Unit := BuildMetadata.writeFile path (.ofBuild depTrace outputs log)

/-- Indicator of whether a build's output(s) are up-to-date. -/
public inductive OutputStatus
| /-- Needs rebuild -/ outOfDate
| /-- Up-to-date by modification time -/ mtimeUpToDate
| /-- Up-to-date by hash -/ hashUpToDate
deriving DecidableEq

/-- Constructs an `OutputStatus` from a hash check. -/
@[inline] public def OutputStatus.ofHashCheck (upToDate : Bool) : OutputStatus :=
  if upToDate then .hashUpToDate else .outOfDate

/-- Constructs an `OutputStatus` from a modification time check. -/
@[inline] public def OutputStatus.ofMTimeCheck (upToDate : Bool) : OutputStatus :=
  if upToDate then .mtimeUpToDate else .outOfDate

/-- Whether the build should be considered up-to-date for rebuilding. -/
@[inline] public def OutputStatus.isUpToDate (status : OutputStatus) : Bool :=
  status != .outOfDate

/-- Whether the build or rebuild should be considered up-to-date for caching. -/
@[inline] public def OutputStatus.isCacheable (status : OutputStatus) : Bool :=
  status != .mtimeUpToDate

@[specialize] def checkHashUpToDate'
  [CheckExists ι] [GetMTime ι]
  (info : ι) (depTrace : BuildTrace) (depHash : Option Hash)
  (oldTrace := depTrace.mtime)
: JobM OutputStatus := do
  if depTrace.hash == depHash then
    .ofHashCheck <$> checkExists info
  else if (← getIsOldMode) then
    .ofMTimeCheck <$> oldTrace.checkUpToDate info
  else
    return .outOfDate

/--
Checks if the `info` is up-to-date by comparing `depTrace` with `depHash`.
If old mode is enabled (e.g., `--old`), uses the `oldTrace` modification time
as the point of comparison instead.
-/
@[inline, deprecated "Deprecated without replacement." (since := "2025-03-04")]
public def checkHashUpToDate
  [CheckExists ι] [GetMTime ι]
  (info : ι) (depTrace : BuildTrace) (depHash : Option Hash)
  (oldTrace := depTrace.mtime)
: JobM Bool := (·.isUpToDate) <$> checkHashUpToDate' info depTrace depHash oldTrace

/--
**For internal use only.**
Checks whether `info` is up-to-date with the trace.
If so, replays the log of the trace if available.
-/
@[specialize] public def SavedTrace.replayIfUpToDate'
  [CheckExists ι] [GetMTime ι]
  (info : ι) (depTrace : BuildTrace) (savedTrace : SavedTrace)
  (oldTrace := depTrace.mtime)
: JobM OutputStatus := do
  if let .ok data := savedTrace then
    let status ← checkHashUpToDate' info depTrace data.depHash oldTrace
    if status.isUpToDate then
      updateAction .replay
      replay data.log
    return status
  else if (← getIsOldMode) then
    .ofMTimeCheck <$> oldTrace.checkUpToDate info
  else
    return .outOfDate
where replay log := log.replay -- specializes `replay` to `JobM`

/--
Checks whether `info` is up-to-date with the trace.
If so, replays the log of the trace if available.
-/
@[inline] public def SavedTrace.replayIfUpToDate
  [CheckExists ι] [GetMTime ι]
  (info : ι) (depTrace : BuildTrace) (savedTrace : SavedTrace)
  (oldTrace := depTrace.mtime)
: JobM Bool := (·.isUpToDate) <$> savedTrace.replayIfUpToDate' info depTrace oldTrace

/--
Returns `true` if the saved trace exists and its hash matches `inputHash`.

If up-to-date, replays the saved log from the trace and sets the current
build action to `replay`. Otherwise, if the log is empty and trace is synthetic,
or if the trace is not up-to-date, the build action will be set to `reuse`.
-/
public def SavedTrace.replayCachedIfUpToDate (inputHash : Hash) (self : SavedTrace) : JobM Bool := do
  if let .ok data := self then
    if data.depHash == inputHash then
      if data.synthetic && data.log.isEmpty then
        updateAction .reuse

#!/bin/bash
# claudewatch.sh <logfile> <stopfile>: every 0.2 s, records any NEW process named 'claude' (comm) or whose command line
# has a 'claude' program word, with exe and parent. Baseline processes (the user's own sessions) are ignored.
OUT=$1; STOP=$2
list() { { pgrep -x claude; pgrep -f '(^|/)claude( |$)'; } 2>/dev/null | sort -un; }
base=$(list | tr '\n' ' ')
echo "$(date +%T.%N) baseline: $base" >> $OUT
seen=" $base $$ "
while [ ! -f "$STOP" ]; do
  for p in $(list); do
    case "$seen" in *" $p "*) continue;; esac
    seen="$seen$p "
    pp=$(awk '{print $4}' /proc/$p/stat 2>/dev/null)
    echo "$(date +%T.%N) NEW pid=$p ppid=$pp exe=$(readlink /proc/$p/exe 2>/dev/null) cmd=$(tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$p/cmdline 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-200) parent=$(tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$pp/cmdline 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-200)" >> $OUT
  done
  sleep 0.2
done
echo "$(date +%T.%N) stopped" >> $OUT

- **A ghost check reuses the last clean check only when it was of exactly `ws/`'s files and the mirror still holds them; the engine's caches are bounded (32 models, 16 runs).** One engine serves many runs; the content comparison guards against the mirror changing under it. *(WP2)*

## 16. The prototype gate

- **telelean normalises before every check and after every revert: it writes the `lean:` pin, a derived id and the docstring = your sentence; Claude never edits blocks.** Deterministic D-8/D-9 handling, so the markup rule can demand byte-identical blocks and an accepted reverted state is pinned too. *(plan)*
- **Declarations that existed before the run must stay unchanged (text and docstring, and their elaborated meaning when the base check produced facts), except the target's `.holds`.** A cheap stand-in for formal immutability (H); it catches "existing vocabulary turned into a definition" (whose footprint looks clean), a rewritten gloss and an `open … in` that changes what unchanged text means. *(
- **The permitted signature is every non-Prop axiom of the project's modules.** Computable from Lean's facts; new ones must already pass the shape rule before the freeze. *(plan; narrowed in section 27)*
- **Lemmas Claude adds may not rest on unselected assumptions either, whatever the finish status; a "not proved" round may not leave a proof of the target in the files.** Otherwise an unchecked proof resting on a belief you did not select could reach your files through "Accept (not proved)". *(plan; extended to every declaration in section 28)*
- **A card formalised before the run keeps its Lean statement: `lean:` lines are only ever added (by normalisation), never changed; no formalised card is re-bound; no unselected card gets formalised.** Otherwise Claude could point the goal at a new, weaker statement and freeze that. *(plan)*
- **The token rules judge only the lines Claude added; a stray non-Lean file Claude writes is a "bad path" finding.** Your own `set_option … in` or `#eval` line must not fail every attempt; a stray file is Claude's mistake, not a machine problem. *(plan)*
- **The readiness rules (target and selected assumptions formalised, `.holds` present) apply to the freeze and to `finish(proved)`, not to a "not proved" finish.** An honest "could not formalise" should end cleanly instead of after three forced failures. *(plan)*

#!/bin/bash
# memwatch.sh <root-pid> <logfile>: samples MemAvailable every 2 s while root-pid lives; logs the minimum;
# if MemAvailable < 8000 MB, sends TERM to root-pid's own process tree only (my processes).
ROOT=$1; OUT=$2; MINAVAIL=999999
desc() { local p=$1; echo $p; for c in $(pgrep -P $p 2>/dev/null); do desc $c; done; }
while kill -0 $ROOT 2>/dev/null; do
  AV=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  [ $AV -lt $MINAVAIL ] && MINAVAIL=$AV
  if [ $AV -lt 8000 ]; then echo "$(date +%T) LOW MEMORY ${AV}MB: killing tree of $ROOT" >> $OUT; for p in $(desc $ROOT); do kill -TERM $p 2>/dev/null; done; fi

done

## 31. Closing fixes for M2, round 2 (docs, code comments and one new test)

- **The description of `telelean.run.reuseLeanBuild` no longer promises more than its record guarantees (section 30 corrected; nothing in telelean's behaviour changed).** The record is a listing of 
your `.lake/build` taken right after the board's refresh, so whatever another program (a terminal `lake build`, the Lean extension) finished writing while that refresh ran is part of it. The verifier 
of the first closing round wrote a second version of one module into `.lake/build` during 24 refreshes, the way Lake writes it (temporary name, then rename, its record last): every refresh was 
recorded, and 10 of the 14 copies runs then used held that module from the other version, 9 of them written during the refresh's check phase. The checks see which files exist and their times, not 
which version of your files a module was built from, so two complete versions look alike. Results stay right because Lake compares every module's record with the run's own files and rebuilds each 
module that does not match: the verifier built three such copies, Lake rebuilt the odd module, and every compiled file then equalled a clean build. The setting's description, the user guide, the plan 
(section 4.2) and the code comments now say what is true: a run copies what `.lake/build` held right after the board's last Lean check, untouched since, and Lake decides what it can reuse. One limit 
belongs to Lake itself: when a module's record matches, Lake does not re-read its compiled file, so two Lake builds writing the same module at the same moment (Lake 4.35 takes no lock) could leave a 
compiled file that Lake trusts wrongly, in your own `.lake/build` as in a copy of it; with the setting off (the default), nothing of your build enters a run. Kept as it is rather than adding a `lake 
build --no-build` check to every refresh, which would cost one more Lake process each time and still could not see that limit, or removing the setting. *(fix)*
- **The plan's section 3 now matches the gate's code in four more places (text only: the gate did not change, and it already failed in every one of these cases).** A stray file Claude writes at the 
root of its working copy (`notes.md`) or anywhere else outside the subject is "outside the subject" (`outside-subject`); only one inside the subject's folder is "bad path" (also corrected in section 
16 and in the plan's sections 0.1, 4.2 and 15.1). `lakefile.lean` is never scanned for forbidden tokens: as a project file it only gets `project-file`. The per-module `build` finding (a module that 
failed without a Lean message) appears only when the build reported no error message at all, and the engine's fail-closed `build` findings are added only when the rules reported none (a new core test 
pins the per-module rule). The ghost's Lean name is chosen twice: when Claude suggests the premise (Claude's own name if it is a plain identifier, not a keyword, neither it nor its `.holds` is 
declared in the subject and no earlier suggestion of the run has it, else one made from the sentence's first six words) and again at adoption, which also refuses a name used as an identifier anywhere

adoption names the result. *(fix)*

input.summary:
Fixed both open minor items. Only docs, code comments and one new test changed; telelean behaves exactly as before. Both items are fixed in /home/zhengyew/telelean.

Item 1 (seed claims overstated, setting telelean.run.reuseLeanBuild, which is off by default): I took the verifier's simplest option and reworded every claim. I did not add a `lake build --no-build` check and did not remove the setting. The text now says what the record actually holds: what .lake/build held right after the board's last successful refresh, untouched since. That includes anything another program (a terminal or the Lean extension) wrote while that refresh ran, and the checks cannot tell two complete versions apart. Correctness rests on Lake's per-module check, which compares each module's trace with the run's own sources and rebuilds any module that does not match. I also wrote down one limit that belongs to Lake itself, checked in the Lake 4.35 sources: Lake treats a module as up to date when its recorded input hash matches and its output files exist, without re-reading them, and Lake 4.35 has no build lock. So two Lake builds writing the same module at the same moment could leave outputs Lake wrongly trusts, in the user's own .lake/build as much as in a copy of it. With the setting off, nothing of the user's build enters a run. Places reworded: seed.ts (module comment and two doc comments), shadow/index.ts, shadow/types.ts (two places), run/types.ts, a run/manager.ts comment, a modelWorkspace.ts comment, the seed.test.ts header and describe title, plan sections 4.2 and 8.3, AT2.1, a new closing-r2 row in the contract log, decisions-log section 30 (corrected in place) plus a new section 31, user-guide (two places), and the setting's description in extension/package.json.

Item 2 (plan section 3 against the code):
(a) A stray `notes.md` at the root of ws/ or anywhere outside the subject is `outside-subject`; only one inside `<library>/<S>/` is `bad-path`. Fixed in 3.1 (sentence and table) and 4.2, and for consistency in plan 0.1 and 15.1, decisions-log section 16, and the core gate/index.ts doc comment.
(b) Every changed `.lean` file except `lakefile.lean` is scanned for tokens; `lakefile.lean` gets `project-file` only.
(c) The per-module `build` finding appears only when the build has no error message at all. I also made the fail-closed sentence exact (runner `buildErrorFindings` runs only when the rules reported no `build` finding), in the 3.3 row and the order paragraph.
(d) 3.8 now describes both naming steps. When Claude proposes, runner `ghostName` picks the name. At adoption, core `adoptionPlan` applies a stricter check: the name must be a valid identifier, not a keyword or command word, not used as an identifier anywhere in the files, and neither `<ns>.<name>`, its `.holds`, nor the bare name may be declared. Otherwise it uses `deriveId` with `-` and `.` turned into `_`, the `ghost_` prefix, and `_2`, `_3` suffixes.
A new core test pins (c). I checked (a) and (b) against core's built checkFileChanges.

I rebuilt and ran every suite twice. Pass 2 ran on the final, unchanged sources and is the one these results describe; every suite passed. No real Claude was started.

#!/bin/bash
# memwatch.sh <root-pid> <logfile>: samples MemAvailable every 2 s while root-pid lives; logs the minimum;
# if MemAvailable < 8000 MB, sends TERM to root-pid's own process tree only (my processes).
ROOT=$1; OUT=$2; MINAVAIL=999999
desc() { local p=$1; echo $p; for c in $(pgrep -P $p 2>/dev/null); do desc $c; done; }
while kill -0 $ROOT 2>/dev/null; do
  AV=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  [ $AV -lt $MINAVAIL ] && MINAVAIL=$AV
  echo "$(date +%T) avail=${AV}MB" >> $OUT
  if [ $AV -lt 8000 ]; then echo "$(date +%T) LOW MEMORY: killing tree of $ROOT" >> $OUT; for p in $(desc $ROOT); do kill -TERM $p 2>/dev/null; done; fi
  sleep 2
done
echo "DONE minAvail=${MINAVAIL}MB" >> $OUT

#!/bin/bash
# claudewatch.sh <logfile> <stopfile>: every 0.2 s, records any NEW process named 'claude' (comm) or whose command line
# has a 'claude' program word, with exe and parent. Baseline processes (the user's own sessions) are ignored.
OUT=$1; STOP=$2
list() { { pgrep -x claude; pgrep -f '(^|/)claude( |$)'; } 2>/dev/null | sort -un; }
base=$(list | tr '\n' ' ')
echo "$(date +%T.%N) baseline: $base" >> $OUT
seen=" $base $$ "
while [ ! -f "$STOP" ]; do
  for p in $(list); do
    case "$seen" in *" $p "*) continue;; esac
    seen="$seen$p "
    pp=$(awk '{print $4}' /proc/$p/stat 2>/dev/null)
    echo "$(date +%T.%N) NEW pid=$p ppid=$pp exe=$(readlink /proc/$p/exe 2>/dev/null) cmd=$(tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$p/cmdline 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-200) parent=$(tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$pp/cmdline 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-200)" >> $OUT
  done
  sleep 0.2
done
echo "$(date +%T.%N) stopped" >> $OUT

## 3. The prototype gate, exactly

Closing round 1: sections 3.1 to 3.3 were checked line by line against the code (core `gate/g0.ts`, `gate/permitted.ts`, `gate/rules.ts`, `gate/decls.ts`, `gate/normalise.ts`; runner `gate/engine.ts`, `gate/findings.ts`) and describe what it does; the fixer-round notes they collected are folded into the rules.

The gate runs on the shadow after `finish`; `check_lean` and `freeze_statements` run subsets of the same rules (core `evaluateRules`, purposes `check`, `freeze`, `gate-proved`, `gate-other`). Inputs: the run base B (exactly the user's files at run start, the shadow's `base` commit, with B's Lean facts from the run's base check; for Accept's re-check after drift, the user's files at Accept, the `accept-base` commit, without facts: section 7.1), the adoption reference A (the shadow at its newest `adopt` commit, when a ghost was adopted: telelean's own ghost blocks and declarations are checked against it, never against B), the round start R (the shadow when the round began; B in round 1), the shadow now S (after normalisation, as committed: the gate judges one committed state) with the build mirror's fresh Lean facts of S, the round's freeze F, the selection Sel (target T, premises P, adopted ghosts), the finish status.

**Why these checks make "proved" mean "proved from exactly the selection"** (the Prototype profile's central claim): the target's statement and every selected statement are frozen before any proof exists (`proof-before-freeze`, which also catches a proof carried inside a definition, instance or structure, and the freeze); a formalised card's statement cannot be swapped (`markup`: no `lean:` line changed, no card re-bound); `existing-changed` keeps every declaration the user had, by text and, with B's facts, by meaning; G4 checks the target theorem against the freeze with the permitted set computed from the freeze; `footprint` holds for every declaration the run adds or changes, whatever its kind or type (a definition, instance or structure can carry a proof too) and whatever the finish status; no `example` (a proof without a name, which no rule could check) is ever left in the files; and what the proposal shows is always a judged state (gate-pass files, or a reverted, normalised and re-checked passing state).

**Order and short-circuits** (runner `engine.runCheck`, then `engine.gate`): G0 (text only, core `checkFileChanges`) → if any G0 finding, stop: Lean never elaborates text that fails G0 → sync the build mirror (a working copy that cannot be synced is an environment outcome, section 3.6) → G1: one Lean job, `semantic.refreshLeanFacts` on `build/`; a runLean `timeout`/`oom` is a `budget` finding and stops the check there, and `could-not-start`, `low-memory`, a cancellation or an unsupported project stop it as environment outcomes → core `evaluateRules` on S's project model with the fresh facts: G1's Lean-error findings, G3, G5 and the readiness and stage rules (failing closed, the engine adds a `build` finding for any Lean error the rules did not report) → in the gate, `finish(proved)` without a freeze always carries `not-frozen` → only when there is no finding at all, the status is `proved` and the round has a freeze: G4 (lake comparator).

### 3.1 G0: token denylist and file rules (core `scanForbidden`, `checkFileChanges`)

Only paths that differ between B and S are judged; S here is every regular file in ws/ (`ShadowWorkspace.currentFiles`), so a stray `notes.md` Claude wrote is a `bad-path` finding (counted), not an environment failure. Each such path first gets the file rules below (at most one file-rule finding per path); then every added or changed `.lean` file, inside the subject or not, is scanned for forbidden tokens, and in it only Claude's lines: a forbidden token on a line whose exact text also occurs in B's version of the file is the user's own and is not reported (line-multiset comparison, `scanForbidden(file, text, ctx, baseText)`; extra copies of such a line are reported), so a user's `set_option … in` or `#eval` line never fails Claude's attempt just because Claude edited the same file. Tokens come from core's `lexLean` (comments, strings, docstrings and telelean blocks never count) and match by their text or their canonical name (`«sorry»` is `sorry`). A symlink, special file or dot-entry in ws/ never reaches G0: the shadow refuses it first (an environment outcome, section 3.6; Claude's confined tools cannot create one).

| Code | Forbidden (code tokens), or the file rule |
|---|---|
