The history snapshots stay in the git repository under `refs/telelean/` (no branch shows them); to remove them, run in the repository: `git for-each-ref --format='delete %(refname)' refs/telelean/ | git update-ref --stdin` (git frees the space at its next housekeeping).
129	
130	## 10. Proving with Claude: "These suffice" (M2)
131	
132	A run asks Claude to decide whether the target card follows from exactly the premises you selected. Claude works in a private copy of your model (never in your files): it formalises the cards that have no Lean yet, freezes the statements, proves, and says it is finished. telelean then checks the result itself, with Lean and fixed rules. You review a proposal on the board and decide: **Accept**, **Feedback** or **Discard**.
133	
134	### 10.1 What you need
135	
136	- **Claude Code**, logged in with your claude.ai subscription. telelean uses your own Claude Code (no API key): by default the binary of the VS Code Claude Code extension, else `claude` on the PATH, else `~/.local/bin/claude` (setting `telelean.claude.path` to choose one). Version 2.1.295 or newer.
137	- The model builds with toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0` and has no Lake dependencies; the Lean sandbox works (as for M1's checks); enough free memory (`telelean.memory.minAvailableGiB`).
138	- **Your files must build.** Right after the run starts telelean builds your files once; Lean errors anywhere end the run before Claude is contacted ("your files have Lean errors (…); fix or save them, then start again").
139	
140	### 10.2 Starting a run
141	
142	1. On the board, click the premises, then Ctrl/Cmd+click the target (a Goal or a Derivation; an Assumption is something you hold: make it a Derivation first). The tray shows "premises ⊢ target".
143	2. Press **These suffice ▶** (exactly these premises), **Add to its premises ▶** (the target's declared premises plus the selected ones) or, with only the target selected, **Self-evident?** (no premises at all).
144	3. The first time in a model folder, telelean asks for your consent (10.3).
145	4. telelean checks the start before anything is sent ("preflight"): no other run of this model folder is active; the selection is valid; toolchain, sandbox and memory are fine; Claude Code is found. Any refusal changes nothing. Only then does it declare the selected premises on the target (`premises:`, M1's undoable action; skipped when they are already declared, and never for Self-evident?), make the private copy, build your files once, and start Claude Code. Claude Code itself checks before the first prompt that you are logged in with a claude.ai subscription; a refusal there costs no quota.
146	
147	At most one run per model folder at a time. Closing the board does not stop a run: the header badge ("Claude: working on Spyro · 3/25 checks") shows it in any board of the folder.
148	
149	### 10.3 Consent and what leaves the machine
150	
151	Before the first run in a model folder telelean asks: *"Run Claude on this model? telelean sends this subject's cards (sentences, reasons, Lean statements), its vocabulary and your recorded answers, plus any model file Claude reads, to Anthropic through your Claude Code login (your claude.ai subscription; no API key)."* **Run with Claude** is remembered for that folder; **Cancel** starts nothing and is not remembered (you are asked again next time).
152	
153	What is sent, through your Claude Code login: a fixed system prompt (the same text every run), the first message (the target, the selected premises and the subject's other cards with their sentences, reasons and Lean; the vocabulary; your earlier answers that are in force; the run's budget), every model file Claude reads in its copy (all subjects of the project are in the copy, so imports work), and every tool result (Lean check results, your answers, the check verdicts). Your Feedback text and your answers go as messages. Nothing else from your machine is sent.
154	
155	What stays on your machine: each run's directory in VS Code's storage for telelean (`~/.config/Code/User/globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs/…`: Claude's working copy, its Lean build, its git history, `run.json` and `session/transcript.jsonl`, the exact text of every message and tool call). The newest `telelean.run.keepRuns` (10) finished runs per model folder are kept. Claude Code also keeps its own transcript of each session under `~/.claude/projects/` (that is how a session is resumed); telelean never reads it.
156	
157	### 10.4 The run panel
158	
159	The panel opens beside the board when a run starts (below the board on a narrow board); the header badge shows and hides it. Its status line: state and stage ("Working · formalising", "· proving", "Waiting for your answer", "Checking Claude's result", "Ready for review"), the round, Lean checks used (3/25), Claude's turns (12/80), Claude's working time (paused while a question waits for you), check attempts (1/3), tokens, the cost estimate and the usage-limit status. Below: **notices** (the check results, reverts, caps, machine problems), the **activity** feed (each check, freeze, suggestion; Claude's own words in italics with a "Claude" marker) and your answered questions. **Cancel** stops the run (10.11).
160	
161	Everything Claude wrote (its messages, questions, summaries, suggested premises, glosses of new vocabulary) is shown in italics with a marker, never in the style of your own words.
162	
163	### 10.5 Claude's questions
164	
165	When a sentence can be read in ways that change the result (modality, genericity, scope, word sense, …), Claude asks first: up to three questions at a time, each with a tag ("modality"), its options with their plain consequences, **In my own words**, **Leave it open** and **Decide for me**, and a scope for your answer: **this run** (default), **these cards** or **the whole subject**.

# Decisions log (M1 and M2)

Sections 1–13 are M1 ("the map without AI"); sections 14–26 are M2 (one-shot "These suffice" with Claude), further down.

Every smaller decision taken while planning, building and integrating M1, grouped by topic. One line each: **the decision**, then why. Sources: plan = `docs/m1-plan.md` section 13.1 (architect and review); WP1–WP6 = the builders; int = the integrator; fix = the fixers after the verification (section 10 lists the core and runner ones, section 11 the extension and webview ones, sections 12 and 13 the two closing rounds). None of these needed your approval to proceed, and all of them can be reversed. If you disagree with one, say which and it can be changed.

Contract changes (new exports, optional fields) are listed separately in `docs/m1-plan.md` section 14.

## 1. The model folder and its files

- **The opt-in marker is `.telelean/config.json` (it also names the Lake library), not `layout.json`.** Layout is per subject and optional; a dedicated file is a clearer marker. *(plan)*
- **Sidecars live per subject: `.telelean/subjects/<S>/layout.json` and `attic/`.** A subject's history snapshot and revert then cover exactly its own files. *(plan)*
- **`graph.json` sits at `.telelean/graph.json` and is gitignored.** It is rewritten after every refresh and every edit. *(plan)*
- **New subjects import Vocabulary ← Inbox ← Main (Main imports Inbox).** Cards you formalise by hand in Inbox can then be used from Main. *(plan)*
- **The exact scaffold texts are frozen in one function (`subjectScaffold`).** Initialize, New subject and the sample then write identical files. *(plan)*
- **`wording.jsonl` and `attempts.jsonl` are not written in M1.** Snapshots keep old wordings; attempts start with runs in M2. *(plan)*
- **`mental_model/` is not a git repository and has no `.lake/`.** It sits inside the git-free telelean folder; the board offers "Initialize git" when you want history there. *(plan)*
- **The scaffold `.gitignore` gains a fifth line, `/.telelean/*.tmp`, and every temp file of an atomic write goes into `.telelean/`.** A crash between write and rename then leaves nothing git would offer to commit (one kind of temp file used to sit inside the subject's snapshot scope). *(int)*
- **Initialize suggests the subject name from the folder name** (`mental_model` → `MentalModel`, `my-model 2` → `MyModel2`, fallback `Subject`). Plan 7.2's rule made concrete. *(WP4)*
- **A folder with both `lakefile.lean` and `lakefile.toml` is refused; a `lakefile.lean`-only folder gets the hint `lake translate-config toml`.** Lake prefers `lakefile.lean`, so reading the TOML could mislead. *(WP4)*
## 16. The prototype gate

- **telelean normalises before every check and after every revert: it writes the `lean:` pin, a derived id and the docstring = your sentence; Claude never edits blocks.** Deterministic D-8/D-9 handling, so the markup rule can demand byte-identical blocks and an accepted reverted state is pinned too. *(plan)*
- **Declarations that existed before the run must stay unchanged (text and docstring, and their elaborated meaning when the base check produced facts), except the target's `.holds`.** A cheap stand-in for formal immutability (H); it catches "existing vocabulary turned into a definition" (whose footprint looks clean), a rewritten gloss and an `open … in` that changes what unchanged text means. *(plan)*
- **The permitted signature is every non-Prop axiom of the project's modules.** Computable from Lean's facts; new ones must already pass the shape rule before the freeze. *(plan)*
- **Lemmas Claude adds may not rest on unselected assumptions either, whatever the finish status; a "not proved" round may not leave a proof of the target in the files.** Otherwise an unchecked proof resting on a belief you did not select could reach your files through "Accept (not proved)". *(plan)*
- **A card formalised before the run keeps its Lean statement: `lean:` lines are only ever added (by normalisation), never changed; no formalised card is re-bound; no unselected card gets formalised.** Otherwise Claude could point the goal at a new, weaker statement and freeze that. *(plan)*
- **The token rules judge only the lines Claude added; a stray non-Lean file Claude writes is a "bad path" finding.** Your own `set_option … in` or `#eval` line must not fail every attempt; a stray file is Claude's mistake, not a machine problem. *(plan)*
- **The readiness rules (target and selected assumptions formalised, `.holds` present) apply to the freeze and to `finish(proved)`, not to a "not proved" finish.** An honest "could not formalise" should end cleanly instead of after three forced failures. *(plan)*
- **The freeze copy drops the target's `.holds` and everything that uses it.** Needed after Feedback, on Accept's re-check, and for a pending-promotion target whose claimed `.holds` other proofs use. *(plan)*
- **Per-declaration budgets are Lean's default heartbeat limit (unchangeable, since `set_option` is forbidden), plus 120 s per Lean job and the memory cap.** 03's measured per-declaration budgets need the extractor; deferred to H. *(plan)*
- **The token denylist flags `native` anywhere (not only `+native`), adds `run_tac`, and matches `ofReduceBool`/`ofReduceNat`/`reduceBool`/`reduceNat` by their last name component.** A stricter list: `decide (config := {native := true})` and qualified names would slip through; a false positive only costs a retry. *(WP1)*
- **File rules give one finding per path, most specific first; a new `<library>/<S>.lean` and nested modules are accepted; positions follow Lean (1-based line, 0-based column) and name the enclosing declaration.** Clear single messages for Claude, matching the Lean messages it sees; the board can say "in cynder_not_good.holds". *(WP1)*

- **A derivation footprint widens the permitted set only for a proof you already had (same statement and proof text as at the run's start, or at Accept's re-check); a proof Claude writes for a selected premise is a lemma like any other.** Taking footprints from the current state let that proof be judged against a set containing its own axioms ("Gate passed" for a proof resting on an unselected assumption), and after Feedback the next freeze let the target rest on that assumption directly. *(fix)*
- **A declaration Claude adds that Lean reports nothing about (a `private` one: Lean's index skips private names) is a finding in every check, rather than silently skipped.** Fail closed: nothing about it could be checked, so a "not proved" round could carry a lemma resting on an unselected assumption into your files. *(fix)*

- **The usage-limit notice is worded like the status line, in local time ("Close to your plan's usage limit (five-hour window, 83% used); resets at 00:45.").** It used to print the CLI's raw status name and a UTC timestamp. *(fix)*
- **"Stop" on an interrupted run says "Run stopped", not "Proposal discarded"; closing the window also cancels the run's running Lean job.** There was no proposal; and a check or gate whose result is thrown away should not run on for up to two minutes when the extension host outlives the run manager. *(fix)*

I fixed all 13 issues in my paths: 2 blockers, 4 majors, 7 minors. Runner tests ran twice and core tests on the final code, all with real Lean where it applies; everything passes. I also rebuilt the repo.

Gate fixes (core):
- **P1/P6b, axiom below a selected premise card.** An axiom placed directly below the block of a selected Goal or Derivation card was taken as that card's statement and escaped every rule. Now, before the freeze, any new axiom is refused unless it is the `.holds` of a selected assumption or adopted ghost, or vocabulary not attached to any card. This holds whatever the axiom's type.
- **Permitted set.** The signature no longer admits an axiom attached to a card, or vocabulary of kind `other`.
- **Malformed statements.** In every check, a selected card of any type that Claude attached in this run to something other than a Prop statement is reported as `not-formalised`.
- **P2, circular permitted set.** `computePermittedAxioms` and `frozenSnapshot` take an optional B (the user's files at run start or at Accept). With B, a derivation's footprint counts only for a proof the user already had, unchanged. The engine's freeze and the not-proved check both pass B, so a proof Claude writes for a selected premise can no longer widen the set it is judged against, in that round or after Feedback.
- **P12, private declarations.** A declaration added in the run that Lean reports nothing about (e.g. `private`) is now a footprint finding instead of being skipped.

Literal walkthrough (TL107 after Accept): "I hold this" now also appends the adopted card to the target's `premises:` line, in the same change that writes the card. The markup rule accepts exactly that line as telelean wrote it. The change shows in the raw diff and Undo reverts it with the rest of the Accept.

Runner wording and lifecycle:
- An Accept that changes no file now says "Recorded: … (no file changed)." with no Undo hint.
- A run with no premises gets the label "Self-evident? → …".
- The usage-limit notice is worded like the status line, in local time (e.g. "Close to your plan's usage limit (five-hour window, 83% used); resets at 00:45.").
- Stop on an interrupted run says "Run stopped".
- Closing the window (`dispose()`) now cancels the run's running Lean jobs.

Safety:
- `scripts/smoke-claude.mjs` is dry by default. It goes live only with `--live` plus `TELELEAN_SMOKE_LIVE=yes`, decided before anything loads, and sets `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1` for itself otherwise. A new refusal test covers this.
- The quota tripwire is now armed by any value except empty, 0 or false.
- `createClaudeBackend` only skips the tripwire when a test gives both a scratch home and a scratch PATH.
- `startSession` only runs a .mjs/.js test double inside a `test/**/fixtures` folder.
- The test that ran your real Claude binary (`--version`) on every suite run now runs only with `TELELEAN_ALLOW_REAL_CLAUDE_VERSION=1`.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` is now passed through to runs.

Tests and docs: there are core regression tests for each case. Four new end-to-end cheat scripts with real Lean cover a selected Goal premise (freeze refused; a belief added after the freeze) and a selected Derivation premise. A fourth covers a private lemma. The literal end-to-end and m2flow tests now check there is no TL107 or mismatch after Accept. The user guide (sections 10.3, 10.6, 10.8–10.12), the plan (3.2, 3.3, 4.9, 10.3, 10.4, section 14) and the decisions log (new section 27) are updated.

I also re-ran the verifier's own probes (P1, P2, P6b, P11, P12) with real Lean: every cheat is now caught and none reaches your files.

===== WP5 summary
WP5 (VS Code extension host) for M2 is built, but one gated test fails because of a bug in WP3's code, not in mine: the typecheck is clean and 165 of 166 unit tests pass.

**The failing test** (`test/unit/realRuns.test.ts`, "run.json itself says interrupted…") runs against the real RunManager and shows a write-ordering bug in WP3's in-progress code. When the extension deactivates, WP3's `dispose()` writes the run as `interrupted` immediately, but earlier writes still queued behind it land afterwards. They leave run.json saying `working` (without `canResume`) and can recreate run folders that were just deleted. The user-visible effect after a reload is unchanged, because recovery turns `working` into `interrupted`, and the same file's other two tests pass. The fix belongs in WP3 (see open issues).

**What the extension does now (plan section 8):**
- **Runs per model folder.** Each model folder gets one RunManager, created with its workspace; `recover()` is called once, and the RunManager is disposed before the workspace. Run directories live under VS Code's global storage, in `runs/`. Closing the board does not stop a run.
- **Message routing.** The board session sends the 11 run messages to the RunManager and answers each with `actionResult`. Run messages are handled one at a time in arrival order, in a queue separate from board edits, so a slow start or Accept never blocks typing a card. Cancel skips the queue so it can stop a start that is still waiting for Lean. The run and proposal are posted to the board on attach, on `ready` and on every RunManager change, including a run of another subject.
- **Start a run.** If a run of the folder is already active, the start is refused (`conflict`) without asking anything. Otherwise the consent modal appears once per folder, with the plan's exact text and a "Run with Claude" button; a yes is remembered, a no starts nothing and asks again next time. Then `start({ subject, target, premises })` is called; the extension never declares premises itself.
- **Raw Lean diff.** `openProposalDiff` opens `vscode.changes` beside the board over a read-only `telelean-proposal:` document source, with the run's base on the left and the proposal on the right.
- **Settings.** `telelean.model`, `effort`, `claude.path` and the seven `run.*` settings are added with the plan's defaults and scopes; the run settings exactly equal the runner's defaults. The plan gave no limits, so I chose them.
- **Claude backend.** It is created only when the RunManager asks for it at a start, with the guard at `<extension>/dist/bin/telelean-path-guard.mjs`, the default hook runtime, `telelean/<version>`, `pdeathsig: true`, and the Claude Code extension's folder searched first.
- **Test mode.** The backend factory rejects with "real Claude is disabled in Test mode" and never calls `createClaudeBackend`; only `testing.useRunBackend` supplies a backend. `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1` is set in the vitest config, `.vscode-test.mjs` and `smoke.mjs`.
- **Bundling.** The bundle now includes the runner's llm, run, gate, shadow and proposal code plus the MCP SDK. `import.meta.url` is replaced with the bundle's own file URL, done a way that keeps strict mode. `build.mjs` copies the guard to `dist/bin` (checked byte-identical) and loads the bundle in a fresh Node process.
- **Carry-over 3.** `confirmedDependents` is passed into the change-kind action; a `needs-confirmation` answer still names the cards.
- **Deactivation.** `deactivate()` disposes every RunManager first and waits up to 4 s if `dispose()` returns a promise.

===== WP6 summary
I built WP6 (the M2 webview board) against core's frozen run.ts and protocol.ts contracts. I changed no frozen file: every edit is in packages/webview/**, plus the bundle Vite builds into packages/extension/dist/webview/**.

Final checks, run by me:
- typecheck clean in both configs;
- vite build ok;
- vitest: 8 files, 121/121 passed;
- Playwright with isolated HOME and one worker: 70/70 passed (all 49 M1 tests plus 21 new M2 tests);
- the home guard reported the real home folder unchanged.

What was built:
- **Run state in the store.** The `run` (RunView) and `proposal` (ProposalView) messages are stored as sent and never go through applyGraph. The proposed view reads a derived overlay through `boardView()`. The overlay is read-only: no selection, drag, edit or delete.
- **Tray.** "These suffice ▶", "Self-evident?" (no premises) and "Add to its premises ▶" (the union) all post startRun. They are disabled, with the reason shown, while any run of the model folder is active, and when the target is an assumption ("…make it a Derivation first, then prove it.").
- **Run panel** (beside the board; below it on boards narrower than 1000 px):
  - status line: state·stage, round, checks n/25, turns n/80, agent time (paused while a question waits, interpolated between host updates), gate attempts k/3, tokens, "$x estimate" with the list-price tooltip, rate limit, Cancel;
  - A2 notices with their details, then the activity feed, where Claude's text is italic with a marker;
  - Resume/Stop for an interrupted run; failed/ended runs show the error and a Dismiss button;
  - header badge, plus a compact "Show" line for another subject's run.
- **Question cards.** Phenomenon tag; options with consequences and formal preview; "In my own words" (multi-line); Leave it open; Decide for me; scope per answer (default this run). Nothing is pre-selected, and no guess is shown before answering. After the run update, the answered list shows Claude's guess.
- **Review stepper.** Statements first (sentence beside the Lean, "Fully explicit" toggle, closure, "Show on the board"), then new vocabulary (Revoke… pre-fills Feedback), definition questions (yes/no; "no" pre-fills Feedback), the report card (shown once past the statements or on "Show result"; each assumed-without-asking item has "Ask me instead"), then lifecycle ticks (recommended ones start ticked). Accept is disabled until every definition is "yes". Accept, Feedback (text), Discard and Raw Lean diff (whole proposal or per file) post their messages. The report card also lists the suggested premises, gate attempts, files, usage and durations.
- **Proposal banner.** Counts plus a Current | Proposed toggle and Review…, Accept, Feedback, Discard, Raw Lean diff.
- **Diff marks.** Each mark is a glyph plus a word plus colour plus a halo; in high contrast the halo becomes an outline. The Vocabulary group shows "+N new" and opens automatically in the proposed view.
- **Result hidden until reviewed (D-19).** Until the review reveals the result, the overlay hides the target's proof status: its proof chips, its footprint, the verified arrows into it, and the verdict in the state line.
- **"Claude suggests" cards.** Translucent, never dashed, at the top of the Assumptions column. They show the closes-gap chip and, when relevant, the gives-the-goal-alone flag. "I hold this" takes an optional one-line reason and posts adoptGhost; "No" posts rejectGhost.
- **Attempts history** in the expanded card: date, verdict, premises, resolution, and Claude's summary in italics.
- **Carry-overs:**
  1. "Used by" and the delete dialog list externalUsers (lemmas in code font; other subjects' cards by sentence plus "(subject …)"). "Nothing else refers to it." appears only when nothing at all refers to the card.
  2. The dialog's own words are singular/plural: "Rewrite that proof to …" / "Keep that proof, marked broken" versus "Rewrite them…" / "Keep them…".
  3. kindChange posts `confirmedDependents` with the list the dialog showed. If the host answers needs-confirmation and lists more, the dialog re-opens with the host's list and a note; if it lists nothing new, an error toast appears instead of looping.
- **Provenance.** All of Claude's text goes through `AgentText` (marked `data-provenance="agent"`, italic, with a marker). The AT6.10 test checks every on-screen string Claude wrote.

# telelean M1: user guide

M1 is "the map without AI": a board of your ASSUMPTION / DERIVATION / GOAL cards, read from and written to Lean files, checked by Lean, with undo and git history. Nothing in M1 calls Claude.

## 1. Start

1. **Load the new build.** You installed the extension in M0 with **Developer: Install Extension from Location…** (`/home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/extension`). That registration points at the folder, so the rebuilt `dist/` is used after **Developer: Reload Window**. Nothing to reinstall.
2. **Open a folder that holds a model**, for example `/home/zhengyew/telelean` (it contains the sample `mental_model/`) or `mental_model/` itself. telelean starts by itself only in windows that contain a model (a `.telelean/config.json`); its commands work in any window. Untrusted and virtual workspaces are not supported.
3. **Run `telelean: Open Board`** (Command Palette). With several models in the window it asks which one; with none it offers Initialize.

The sample `mental_model/` is your Spyro walkthrough as subject `Spyro`: three assumptions ("PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts" is comment-only with stance *rule*; "Cynder is a character who has a dark past" and "The new Spyro game is PG" are formalised) and one formalised, unproved goal ("Cynder would not be a good addition to the new Spyro game").

Opening the board builds the model with Lean in place: `mental_model/.lake/` and `.telelean/graph.json` appear (both gitignored).

## 2. Make a new model: `telelean: Initialize Model Here`

Run it from the Command Palette, or right-click a folder in the Explorer.

- **Empty folder:** it asks for the first subject's name (a Lean namespace such as `Spyro`; the default comes from the folder name) and writes the Lake project (`lakefile.toml` with `autoImplicit = false`, toolchain `v4.35.0`), `Model.lean`, `Model/<Subject>.lean`, `Model/<Subject>/{Vocabulary,Inbox,Main}.lean`, `.telelean/` and `.gitignore`.
- **Existing Lake project without dependencies:** it asks first, then only adds `.telelean/` and the missing `.gitignore` lines. Your Lean files are not changed.
- **Refused:** projects with Lake dependencies (Mathlib: M4), `lakefile.lean`-only projects (convert with `lake translate-config toml`), folders with other files but no lakefile.
- Then, if the folder is not inside a git repository, it offers `git init` for history (say no and history stays off; you can still accept later from the board).
- **A model folder that is already inside a git repository** (yours) gets history without being asked: opening its board writes "Initial state" snapshots there, as commits under private refs (`refs/telelean/…`; never a branch, never your staging area, never pushed). Section 9 says how to remove them.

## 3. The board

From top to bottom: the header (subject picker, History, Undo/Redo, Lean badge, Problems, legend), three columns (Assumptions, Derivations, Goals; each scrolls on its own), the selection tray, and the A|D|G box. The **Vocabulary group** is the first item of the Assumptions column, collapsed by default (click its heading to open it). **Problems** in the header lists the diagnostics of this subject. On a narrow board the columns keep a readable width and the board scrolls sideways.

**Keyboard.** Tab moves between cards and buttons; on a focused card, Enter expands it, Space adds it to the selection (or takes it out), F2 edits its sentence, Delete opens the delete dialog and **Alt+Up / Alt+Down** moves it up or down in its column. Opening a dropdown (subject picker, History, Problems, "uses:") moves the focus into it: Up/Down/Home/End move between its items, Escape or choosing an item gives the focus back to its button. Saving or cancelling an in-place edit gives the focus back to the card.

**Cards.** The face shows your sentence, "because: …" (your reason), the kind glyph **A**/**D**/**G**, status chips, and for formalised cards a "uses:" line. A glow (aura) means the card has a Lean statement. The chevron (or Enter on a focused card) expands it.

**Expanded card.** Lean code with **Copy** (puts exactly that code on the clipboard) and **Open in editor** (opens the file beside the board, never over it); problems; "Rests on" (the assumptions its proof uses) and "Presupposes" chips; "Depends on / Used by"; stance and source chips; **Make Assumption / Make Derivation / Make Goal**; **Edit**, **Add why / Edit why**, **Delete**.

**In the Lean code:** press and drag to select text (it never drags the card); hover an identifier for its gloss (or the card's sentence); click it to highlight the item in the Vocabulary group (or to reveal that card). Ctrl/Cmd+click is reserved for later.

**"uses:" line.** The vocabulary the card's statement uses, from Lean, two names inline ("HasDarkPast, cynder, …"); **▾ N** lists all of them with kinds and glosses, and picking one highlights it.

## 4. Every board action

## 9. Tests and tooling

- **The runner and the extension import core (and the runner) from source; the runner's build is a typecheck.** No build step or workspace links needed. *(plan)*
- **graph.json's JSON Schema is generated from a zod schema that stays out of the webview bundle; `zod` is declared in core and runner.** zod is installed; ajv is not a declared dependency and nothing may be added. *(plan, int)*
- **Core tests read fixture files with Vite `?raw` imports.** Core is typechecked without Node typings on purpose. *(plan)*
- **The VS Code smoke test always copies the real `mental_model/` (no stand-in), plus a separate pristine copy for the end-to-end suite outside the test window's folder.** A broken sample must fail the test; the other suites keep seeing exactly two model roots. *(int)*
- **The end-to-end suite drives the real board through the DevTools protocol of its own isolated test instance (a loopback port, playwright-core's `connectOverCDP`); the other suites run in a second instance without that port, as in a normal VS Code.** Only trusted input proves that a drag in the code selects text instead of moving the card; a negative control (guard off) fails as expected. *(int)*
- **Suites that open a board first close every editor and wait for the editor area to settle.** A board opened while "close all editors" was still running never loaded its webview (found when the old stub probes, which had added a delay, were removed). *(int)*
- **`TELELEAN_SMOKE_GREP` runs only matching smoke tests.** A development aid; `npm run test:smoke` still runs everything. *(int)*
- **The runner's `npm run typecheck` now covers its tests too (`tsconfig.test.json`).** Two type-only import mistakes were invisible before. *(int)*
- **The smoke script writes npm's debug logs into its own profile.** A builder's earlier setting made npm prune the real `~/.npm/_logs`. *(WP5)*
- **Vitest's results cache of the extension lives in `out/.vite`.** Test writes stay in build output. *(WP5)*

## 10. Fixes after the verification (core, runner, sample, docs)

- **A column-0 comment ends the declaration above it only when the next code after it starts a command (or there is none).** Lean treats comments as whitespace: a `--` or `/- -/` at column 0 inside a tactic proof or a multi-line statement, followed by more indented code, belongs to the declaration. The old rule cut such declarations in half, so D→A, A→G and delete broke files that compiled. *(fix)*
- **Two extra guards against cutting a declaration: `applyLeanOps` refuses when the line after a span is an indented continuation, and the planner refuses when Lean's own range of a freshly checked declaration ends after the span.** Defence in depth: a refusal ("edit it by hand") is always better than a half-removed proof. *(fix)*
- **Neighbouring declarations removed together are deleted in one piece.** One blank line stays where they were, not two. *(fix)*
- **Delete with its Lean asks first when other declarations would stop compiling, listing them (cards, then lemmas without a card and other subjects' proofs); the board resends with `confirmed: true`.** D-18 asks for a confirmation listing the dependents; the board alone sees only this subject's arrows. *(fix; the board's half, "Delete anyway", was added in the closing round, section 12)*
- **D→A / G→A on a proof that takes hypotheses asks first; "rewrite" drops the arguments (`(n.holds h)` becomes `n.holds`), "mark broken" leaves them.** The axiom states `n` directly; the drop zone used to promise the proofs "stay valid" while they broke. Only direct users change (their own types do not). *(fix)*
- **A→G / D→G "rewrite" of a proof that takes hypotheses replaces each whole application `(n.holds h …)` by the new hypothesis `h_n : n`.** The user then rests on `n` and keeps its other hypotheses; replacing only the name gave `(h_n h)`, which does not compile. *(fix)*
- **The mechanical rewrite only touches applications in parentheses with plain identifiers as arguments (`(n.holds h)`, `((n.holds a) b)`); anything else is refused with "choose mark broken".** Recognising every way to apply a function is not worth the risk; the refusal names the place. *(fix)*
- **Lean's double references (`@c` with and without the `@`, `(c)` with and without its parentheses) are merged to one span per identifier, and a leading `@` is accepted.** Found with real `.ilean` files; the rewrite refused these harmless forms before. *(fix)*
- **While files are not freshly checked, a use counts when its name resolves through the declaration's namespaces or any namespace `open`ed earlier in the file, or when it ends with two or more components of the target (`cynder_dark_past.holds`).** Generous on purpose: one question too many is harmless, one missed use removes a `.holds` others use. *(fix)*
- **"Self-evident" requires no card and no hidden axiom in the footprint.** A proof resting on an unmarked axiom (TL103/TL104) is not proved from nothing. *(fix)*
- **A plan never changes another card's binding: a comment-only card left directly above a declaration gets a blank line after it; any other change is refused.** Deleting the card below it used to make it silently bind to that declaration. *(fix)*
- **Editing a field that a block repeats (TL005) changes only the first line and keeps the others; removing such a field is refused.** The later lines are text you typed; deleting them silently, or promoting a hidden one, would surprise. *(fix)*
- **A board lists the vocabulary items of other subjects that its cards use, read-only, under their full names.** Hover glosses and click-to-highlight then work for explicit imports (D-10). *(fix)*
- **graph.json 1.1: `conditional_on` holds a conditional proof's hypotheses and `footprint` its real footprint.** Scripts could not see what a conditional result rests on; the change is additive except for that field's meaning on conditional nodes (no outside users yet). *(fix)*

cd /home/zhengyew/telelean; cat >> docs/user-guide.md <<'EOF'

## 10. Proving with Claude: "These suffice" (M2)

A run asks Claude to decide whether the target card follows from exactly the premises you selected. Claude works in a private copy of your model (never in your files): it formalises the cards that have no Lean yet, freezes the statements, proves, and says it is finished. telelean then checks the result itself, with Lean and fixed rules. You review a proposal on the board and decide: **Accept**, **Feedback** or **Discard**.

### 10.1 What you need

- **Claude Code**, logged in with your claude.ai subscription. telelean uses your own Claude Code (no API key): by default the binary of the VS Code Claude Code extension, else `claude` on the PATH, else `~/.local/bin/claude` (setting `telelean.claude.path` to choose one). Version 2.1.295 or newer.
- The model builds with toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0` and has no Lake dependencies; the Lean sandbox works (as for M1's checks); enough free memory (`telelean.memory.minAvailableGiB`).
- **Your files must build.** Right after the run starts telelean builds your files once; Lean errors anywhere end the run before Claude is contacted ("your files have Lean errors (…); fix or save them, then start again").

### 10.2 Starting a run

1. On the board, click the premises, then Ctrl/Cmd+click the target (a Goal or a Derivation; an Assumption is something you hold: make it a Derivation first). The tray shows "premises ⊢ target".
2. Press **These suffice ▶** (exactly these premises), **Add to its premises ▶** (the target's declared premises plus the selected ones) or, with only the target selected, **Self-evident?** (no premises at all).
3. The first time in a model folder, telelean asks for your consent (10.3).
4. telelean checks the start before anything is sent ("preflight"): no other run of this model folder is active; the selection is valid; toolchain, sandbox and memory are fine; Claude Code is found. Any refusal changes nothing. Only then does it declare the selected premises on the target (`premises:`, M1's undoable action; skipped when they are already declared, and never for Self-evident?), make the private copy, build your files once, and start Claude Code. Claude Code itself checks before the first prompt that you are logged in with a claude.ai subscription; a refusal there costs no quota.

At most one run per model folder at a time. Closing the board does not stop a run: the header badge ("Claude: working on Spyro · 3/25 checks") shows it in any board of the folder.

### 10.3 Consent and what leaves the machine

Before the first run in a model folder telelean asks: *"Run Claude on this model? telelean sends this subject's cards (sentences, reasons, Lean statements), its vocabulary and your recorded answers, plus any model file Claude reads, to Anthropic through your Claude Code login (your claude.ai subscription; no API key)."* **Run with Claude** is remembered for that folder; **Cancel** starts nothing and is not remembered (you are asked again next time).

What is sent, through your Claude Code login: a fixed system prompt (the same text every run), the first message (the target, the selected premises and the subject's other cards with their sentences, reasons and Lean; the vocabulary; your earlier answers that are in force; the run's budget), every model file Claude reads in its copy (all subjects of the project are in the copy, so imports work), and every tool result (Lean check results, your answers, the check verdicts). Your Feedback text and your answers go as messages. Nothing else from your machine is sent.

What stays on your machine: each run's directory in VS Code's storage for telelean (`~/.config/Code/User/globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs/…`: Claude's working copy, its Lean build, its git history, `run.json` and `session/transcript.jsonl`, the exact text of every message and tool call). The newest `telelean.run.keepRuns` (10) finished runs per model folder are kept. Claude Code also keeps its own transcript of each session under `~/.claude/projects/` (that is how a session is resumed); telelean never reads it.

### 10.4 The run panel

The panel opens beside the board when a run starts (below the board on a narrow board); the header badge shows and hides it. Its status line: state and stage ("Working · formalising", "· proving", "Waiting for your answer", "Checking Claude's result", "Ready for review"), the round, Lean checks used (3/25), Claude's turns (12/80), Claude's working time (paused while a question waits for you), check attempts (1/3), tokens, the cost estimate and the usage-limit status. Below: **notices** (the check results, reverts, caps, machine problems), the **activity** feed (each check, freeze, suggestion; Claude's own words in italics with a "Claude" marker) and your answered questions. **Cancel** stops the run (10.11).

Everything Claude wrote (its messages, questions, summaries, suggested premises, glosses of new vocabulary) is shown in italics with a marker, never in the style of your own words.

### 10.5 Claude's questions

When a sentence can be read in ways that change the result (modality, genericity, scope, word sense, …), Claude asks first: up to three questions at a time, each with a tag ("modality"), its options with their plain consequences, **In my own words**, **Leave it open** and **Decide for me**, and a scope for your answer: **this run** (default), **these cards** or **the whole subject**. Send it with **Send answers**. Claude's own guess is shown only after you answered (it never reaches the board before). Claude's clock is paused while it waits for you.

Every answer is recorded in `.telelean/subjects/<S>/decisions.json`. Answers with the scope "the whole subject" (and "these cards", when the run involves them) are sent to later runs as "earlier answers in force". (Revoking an answer comes in M3.)

### 10.6 The checks, the notices and the retry loop

Claude must first **freeze** the statements: the target's Lean statement and those of the selected premises. Proofs are refused before the freeze. When Claude says it is finished, telelean checks the result without Claude:

- only allowed Lean in what Claude wrote: no `sorry`, no `#eval` or other commands except `#check`/`#print`, no `set_option`, no metaprogramming, no imports from outside the project, no changes to the project files;
- the files build (each Lean job has a time and memory limit);
- the proof rests only on the selected premises, Lean's standard axioms, the vocabulary and the existence presuppositions of what the statements mention ("there is at least one character"): the **permitted set**, listed in the report; every lemma Claude adds is held to the same rule, also when it says "not proved";
- the frozen statements are unchanged (Lean's comparator), your words and blocks are unchanged, declarations that existed before the run are unchanged, and the only new beliefs are the `.holds` of selected assumptions Claude formalised;
- new vocabulary has the simple shape (sorts, predicates, constants, functions).

New **definitions** Claude introduces are never accepted silently: they become definition questions in the review. A premise Claude thinks is **missing** becomes a suggestion (10.9), never part of your files. Neither is a failure.

If the check fails, a notice says why, for example *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it added an axiom (`shortcut`), and only you can add beliefs. Asking Claude to retry."*, and Claude gets the exact failure and tries again. After the last allowed attempt (`telelean.run.maxGateAttempts`, 3 per round) telelean stops it and tells you, for example *"Claude's attempts didn't pass the checks 3 times: … telelean reverted its working copy to “Statements frozen (round 1)”."*: the proposal then shows the last state that passed (often the formalisation without a proof), which you can still accept, answer with Feedback, or discard.

More rules of the loop: edits Claude makes after its check passed are discarded (the proposal is always exactly the checked files); a turn that ends without finishing gets one reminder, then the round ends the same way as after the last attempt; reaching a cap (10.12) does too. Problems of the machine (the sandbox could not start, low memory) are not Claude's fault and are not counted: telelean tries the check once more after 30 seconds, and if it fails again the run ends as failed with the reason.

### 10.7 The proposal on the board

When a round ends, the banner reads "Claude's proposal: 1 new · 2 changed · +1 vocabulary" with **Current | Proposed**, **Review…**, **Accept**, **Feedback**, **Discard** and **Raw Lean diff…**. The board switches to **Proposed**: the subject as it would be after Accept, with diff marks on the cards ("+new", "~changed", "−removed": a glyph, a word, a colour and a halo; hover for what changed), and the vocabulary group opened with "+N new". The proposed view is read-only; **Current** shows your files as they are.

Until you have looked at the statements in the review, the target's result stays hidden ("result after the review"): meaning before proof status. **Show result** reveals it early. **Raw Lean diff…** opens the file changes beside the board (read-only; tab "Raw Lean diff: Spyro (round 1)"; per file from the report card).

### 10.8 The review

The review in the run panel goes step by step:

1. **Statements**: each new or changed statement, your sentence beside its Lean. **Fully explicit** shows every name in full and `Not (…)` instead of `¬`; the closure lists the names the statement uses, with glosses. **Show on the board** highlights the card.
2. **New vocabulary**: the sorts, predicates and constants Claude added. **Revoke…** prefills Feedback.
3. **Definitions**: each definition Claude introduced, with its code and the statements that rely on it. Each needs **Yes** before Accept is possible; **No** prefills Feedback.
4. **Result**: the report card: the verdict, the footprint (the cards and presuppositions the proof rests on, e.g. "assumes characters exist"), unused premises, "self-evident" when it needed no premise, **consistency unchecked** (checking that your assumptions do not contradict each other comes in M3), Claude's summary and the gap it reports, every choice Claude made without asking (each with **Ask me instead**, which prefills Feedback), the suggested premises, the check attempts, the changed files, usage and duration.
5. **Card changes**: for a proved Goal, "Make … a Derivation (Lean proved it from the selected premises; recommended)", ticked by default. Untick it to keep the card a Goal.

### 10.9 Suggested premises ("Claude suggests")

When the target does not follow, Claude may suggest a premise you might hold that closes the gap. It appears as a translucent **Claude suggests** card at the top of the Assumptions column (in the Proposed view, and in the report card): Claude's sentence in italics, its Lean statement, **closes the gap (checked)** (telelean checked in a scratch file that the suggestion, with your selected premises, proves the target) and, if so, **gives the goal on its own** (it may simply restate the goal).

**I hold this** (with an optional one-line reason) starts a new round: telelean writes the card into Claude's working copy as an Assumption right before the target (worded by Claude, with your reason), freezes the statements again with it selected, and Claude proves the target with it. The card reaches your files only if you then accept, and stays marked as Claude's wording (italics) until you edit its sentence. **No** declines it.

### 10.10 Accept, Feedback, Discard

- **Accept** applies exactly the checked files of the proposal (plus the ticked card changes) to your files, through M1's history: your hand edits are snapshotted first ("Manual edits"), then one history entry *"accept · These suffice → proved: …"* (with "(+ Make Derivation)" or "(+ 1 adopted assumption)" when they apply), and **one Undo step reverts the whole Accept** (History → Revert works too). Lean then checks your files and the board shows the real statuses (e.g. the target proved, in the Derivations column). A "not proved" round can be accepted too (its statements and vocabulary). If you changed model files while Claude worked, telelean puts Claude's changes on top of yours and checks the combination again (with your current files as the starting point) before applying it; an edit of yours within 3 lines of a change of Claude's counts as overlapping and Accept is refused (*"Your edits to Model/Spyro/Main.lean since the run started overlap Claude's; Discard, or Feedback to redo it on your current files."*). Accept never writes anything but the model's Lean files of the proposal and never applies part of a proposal.
- **Feedback** (a text field; Ctrl+Enter sends) starts a new round in the same Claude session with fresh caps: Claude may revise the statements and must freeze them again before it can claim "proved". The proposal is withdrawn until the round ends.
- **Discard** ends the run; nothing is written to your files.

Each round is recorded in `.telelean/subjects/<S>/attempts.jsonl` (verdict, premises, footprint, Claude's summary, usage), with what you did with it. Like `decisions.json` it is written directly, never undone and not part of history snapshots or reverts; commit it with your own commits if you want to keep it.

### 10.11 Cancel, reload, resume

- **Cancel** (run panel, while the run starts or Claude works) stops Claude and the run's Lean jobs at once; nothing is written. The working copy and transcript stay until old runs are pruned. **Dismiss** removes an ended run from the panel.
- **Window reload or restart:** a waiting question or a proposal comes back as it was; answering a restored question resumes the same Claude session. A run that was working comes back as **interrupted** with **Resume** (continues the same session) and **Stop** (= Discard). Nothing starts by itself after a reload.

### 10.12 Usage, quota and caps

The status line shows Claude's requests and tokens and Claude Code's own cost estimate ("$0.42 estimate": at API list prices; your subscription is not billed per token, but runs use your plan's usage). When Claude Code reports a usage-limit status other than "allowed", a notice says so. Caps bound one round (the first round, each Feedback, each adopted suggestion): 80 turns, 25 Lean checks, 20 minutes of Claude's working time (waiting for you does not count), 120 seconds per Lean job, 3 check attempts. Reaching the turn or time cap stops Claude; the round ends with the last state that passed.

### 10.13 Settings

All take effect after a window reload (Developer: Reload Window).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `telelean.model` | `claude-opus-5-5` | the Claude model of a run (Claude Code's `--model`; an alias such as `opus` works) |
| `telelean.effort` | `high` | low, medium, high, xhigh, max (Claude Code's `--effort`) |
| `telelean.claude.path` | empty (automatic) | the Claude Code executable; empty: the VS Code Claude Code extension's binary, then `claude` on the PATH, then `~/.local/bin/claude` |
| `telelean.run.maxTurns` | 80 | model responses per round (1–1000) |
| `telelean.run.maxChecks` | 25 | Lean checks per round (1–500; a check, a freeze and each suggested premise count one) |
| `telelean.run.maxAgentMinutes` | 20 | Claude's working minutes per round (1–240) |
| `telelean.run.leanJobSeconds` | 120 | time limit of each Lean job of a run (10–1800) |
| `telelean.run.maxGateAttempts` | 3 | check attempts per round before telelean stops Claude and reverts (1–10) |
| `telelean.run.keepRuns` | 10 | finished runs kept per model folder (1–100) |
| `telelean.run.contextScope` | `subject` | which other cards the first message lists: the whole subject, or `neighbourhood` (only cards the target's and premises' statements mention) |

The memory settings of section 8 (`telelean.memory.*`) apply to a run's Lean jobs too.

### 10.14 Limits of M2

- One run per model folder at a time; targets are Goals and Derivations of the board's subject.
- Accept takes the whole proposal (no partial Accept); a definition is endorsed only by its "Yes" before Accept.
- No consistency check of your assumptions yet ("consistency unchecked", M3); no countermodels; the review is minimal (no back-translation or alignment check).
- Recorded answers cannot be revoked yet (M3); "Decide for me" lets Claude choose and say so.
- Lean 4 core only (no Mathlib, M4). The checks are a prototype profile for your own use, not hardened against a determined adversary (later: H).
- A run needs Claude Code logged in with a claude.ai subscription; runs use your plan's usage.

### 10.15 Troubleshooting runs

- **"Not started: telelean sends nothing to Claude until you allow it"**: you pressed Cancel in the consent question; press These suffice again and choose **Run with Claude**.
- **"Claude could not be started: …"**: the message lists the places telelean looked for Claude Code, or says the version is too old or that Claude Code is not logged in with a claude.ai subscription. Install or update the Claude Code extension, or set `telelean.claude.path`, then reload.
- **"The run could not start: your files have Lean errors (…)"**: fix or save the files the message names (Problems on the board lists them), then start again.
- **"Claude is already working on …" / "…waiting for your review"**: one run per model folder; finish, cancel or discard the other one first (its badge is in the header).
- **"telelean could not run the checks (…); this is not Claude's fault"**: the sandbox or the memory guard stopped a Lean job twice; free memory or fix the sandbox, then start a new run.
- **Accept refused**: either your edits overlap Claude's (Discard, or Feedback to redo it on your current files) or Claude's changes no longer pass the checks on top of your current files (the message lists the findings).
- **To free disk space**: lower `telelean.run.keepRuns`, or delete old run folders under `~/.config/Code/User/globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs/` while no run is active.
EOF
