---

# M2 decisions log

Every smaller decision taken while planning, building and integrating M2, grouped by topic. One line each: **the decision**, then why. Sources: plan = `docs/m2-plan.md` section 15.1 (architect and reviewer); WP1–WP6 = the builders (core rules; shadow and engine; run controller; proposals and Accept; extension host; board); int = the integrator. None of these needed your approval to proceed, and all of them can be reversed. If you disagree with one, say which and it can be changed.

Contract changes (new exports, optional fields) are listed separately in `docs/m2-plan.md` section 14.

## 14. Runs and rounds

- **"These suffice" declares the selected premises (M1's undoable `set-premises`), then starts the run; the RunManager makes the declaration itself, only after preflight passed and the backend was obtained. "Self-evident?" declares nothing.** Keeps D-13's meaning of the button, and a refused start changes nothing in your files. *(plan)*
- **Run targets are Goals and Derivations; a pending Derivation's axiom `.holds` may be replaced by the proof.** An assumption is held, not proved (make it a Derivation first, D-11); D-11's promotion is exactly "prove from these". *(plan)*
- **Caps and check attempts are per round (the first round, each Feedback, each adopted suggestion); usage is shown for the whole run.** Each round is started by you; a Feedback round should not be starved by the first one. *(plan)*
- **At most one active run per model folder; a run goes on when its board closes.** D-25; one Lean job at a time and a simple board model. *(plan)*
- **A turn that ends without `finish` gets one reminder, then the round ends as "no finish" (revert, normalise, re-check).** The CLI has no in-process stop hook here; bounded and predictable. *(plan)*
- **A cap reached while a tool call runs takes effect when the call returns.** A passing check is never thrown away by a cap hit during its Lean job. *(plan)*
- **A run starts only on files that build: right after the working copy is made telelean builds your files once, and Lean errors anywhere end the run before Claude is contacted.** Claude may not change your files, so every attempt would fail; the same build gives the base facts for the meaning check. *(plan)*
- **The board shows the run as last written to run.json, never a state ahead of the file.** The plan requires run.json after every state change; a test exposed the race when the live state was read directly. *(WP3)*
- **One user action at a time per model folder: a second concurrent action (answer, Accept, Feedback, adoption, Resume, Discard) gets "conflict"; Cancel is never locked out.** A double-clicked answer or Accept could otherwise interleave across awaits. *(WP3)*
- **Premises count as unchanged when the set equals the declared one (order ignored).** Re-declaring only to reorder would add a pointless undoable history entry. *(WP3)*
- **A backend factory that failed is tried again at the next start; once it succeeded it is never called again.** You may install or update Claude Code after a refused start. *(WP3)*
- **A run that fails before Claude is contacted (your files have errors, Claude Code refused) records no attempt.** No round with Claude took place; an attempt record would be noise in the card's history. *(WP3)*
- **After a reload, a run found in "starting" becomes failed even when it has a session id.** The first message may never have been sent, so "continue where you were" would be wrong. *(WP3)*
- **After the check passed, a cap reached later only interrupts Claude: no cap notice, the verdict stays.** The round already ended properly; the interrupt only saves quota on edits that will be discarded anyway. *(WP3)*
- **The 30-second wait before re-running a check that hit a machine problem counts as Claude's working time.** The simplest consistent rule (the clock runs while working and checking); at most 30 s of a 20-minute cap. *(WP3)*
- **Answers that could not reach Claude (after a reload, or when the CLI went away) are kept in run.json until a resumed session received them; Resume re-sends them.** An answer must never be lost when the resumed CLI fails to start. *(WP3)*
- **"Stop" on an interrupted run records the round as cancelled, then discarded; Cancel during review marks the recorded round discarded.** Every ended round gets exactly one record, with what you did with it. *(WP3)*
- **Accept, Discard and Cancel wait at most 10 s for the CLI to close (it is killed in the background after that).** They should not hang on a misbehaving CLI. *(WP3)*
- **The CLI's own "max turns" result counts as the turn cap; a usage-limit status other than "allowed" posts one warning per status change.** Belt and braces with telelean's own cap; you should see when usage is near a limit. *(WP3)*

## 15. Claude's working copy (the shadow)

- **Claude's root (`ws/`) holds only model files; Lean builds in a separate mirror (`build/`), synced before every Lean job.** Claude Code's Grep/Glob search hidden files (M0 lesson 4); the mirror keeps `.lake` out of Claude's root with no sandbox change, and Lean's facts are root-relative so paths match. *(plan)*
- **The working copy's git history lives outside `ws/` (`git/`, work tree `ws/`) with an isolated git config.** No dot-entry in Claude's root; your global git config cannot affect telelean's private history. *(plan)*
- **Every model file of the project (all subjects) goes into the working copy; the first message covers only the run's subject.** Imports between subjects must build (D-10); Claude can read the other subjects' files, which the consent text says. *(plan)*
- **Run ids double as the sandbox's scope groups.** Cancel kills every Lean job of a run with one `systemctl --user kill`. *(plan)*
- **The history is a bare repository written with `git fast-import` (whole snapshots) and read with `ls-tree`/`cat-file`; all `GIT_*` variables are dropped and config, hooks, excludes and attributes point at `/dev/null`.** A commit is then exactly the judged bytes, and no git setting, filter, attribute or hook of yours can touch it. *(WP2)*
- **The "statements frozen" commit is made only after the comparator's challenge was exported.** A failed freeze must not leave a commit that a give-up revert could land on. *(WP2)*
- **A working copy is refused when your model folder holds a symlink under the library folder (or a symlinked model or project file); a symlinked `.lake` is simply not seeded.** A symlinked model file could pull outside text into what Claude reads. *(WP2)*
- **The base commit is round 1; the history lists commits oldest first.** The first round starts from the base. *(WP2)*
- **The mirror keeps your file's modification time when its text equals the file on disk.** Keeps a seeded `.lake/build` valid (Lake 4.35 decides rebuilds by content hash, verified). *(WP2)*
- **Freeze copies keep their sources in `frozen/<n>/project` but drop their `.lake`; comparator work directories are `gate/<n>`; your files' facts are in `base-facts.json`.** Run directories stay small while what was frozen stays inspectable. *(WP2)*
- **The check reuses the newest normalise or checkpoint commit when it holds exactly the files in `ws/`, else commits a checkpoint ("State judged by the gate (round N)").** One judged commit per state, no duplicates on a repeated finish. *(WP2)*
- **A ghost check reuses the last clean check only when it was of exactly `ws/`'s files and the mirror still holds them; the engine's caches are bounded (32 models, 16 runs).** One engine serves many runs; the content comparison guards against the mirror changing under it. *(WP2)*

## 16. The prototype gate

- **telelean normalises before every check and after every revert: it writes the `lean:` pin, a derived id and the docstring = your sentence; Claude never edits blocks.** Deterministic D-8/D-9 handling, so the markup rule can demand byte-identical blocks and an accepted reverted state is pinned too. *(plan)*
- **Declarations that existed before the run must stay unchanged (text and docstring, and their elaborated meaning when the base check produced facts), except the target's `.holds`.** A cheap stand-in for formal immutability (H); it catches "existing vocabulary turned into a definition" (whose footprint looks clean), a rewritten gloss and an `open … in` that changes what unchanged text means. *(plan)*
- **The permitted signature is every non-Prop axiom of the project's modules.** Computable from Lean's facts; new ones must already pass the shape rule before the freeze. *(plan)*
- **Lemmas Claude adds may not rest on unselected assumptions either, whatever the finish status; a "not proved" round may not leave a proof of the target in the files.** Otherwise an unchecked proof resting on a belief you did not select could reach your files through "Accept (not proved)". *(plan)*
- **A card formalised before the run keeps its Lean statement: `lean:` lines are only ever added (by normalisation), never changed; no formalised card is re-bound; no unselected card gets formalised.** Otherwise Claude could point the goal at a new, weaker statement and freeze that. *(plan)*
- **The token rules judge only the lines Claude added; a stray non-Lean file Claude writes is a "bad path" finding.** Your own `set_option … in` or `#eval` line must not fail every attempt; a stray file is Claude's mistake, not a machine problem. *(plan)*
- **The readiness rules (target and selected assumptions formalised, `.holds` present) apply to the freeze and to `finish(proved)`, not to a "not proved" finish.** An honest "could not formalise" should end cleanly instead of after three forced failures. *(plan)*
- **The freeze copy drops the target's `.holds` and everything that uses it.** Needed after Feedback, on Accept's re-check, and for a pending-promotion target whose claimed `.holds` other proofs use. *(plan)*
- **Per-declaration budgets are Lean's default heartbeat limit (unchangeable, since `set_option` is forbidden), plus 120 s per Lean job and the memory cap.** 03's measured per-declaration budgets need the extractor; deferred to H. *(plan)*
- **The token denylist flags `native` anywhere (not only `+native`), adds `run_tac`, and matches `ofReduceBool`/`ofReduceNat`/`reduceBool`/`reduceNat` by their last name component.** A stricter list: `decide (config := {native := true})` and qualified names would slip through; a false positive only costs a retry. *(WP1)*
- **File rules give one finding per path, most specific first; a new `<library>/<S>.lean` and nested modules are accepted; positions follow Lean (1-based line, 0-based column) and name the enclosing declaration.** Clear single messages for Claude, matching the Lean messages it sees; the board can say "in cynder_not_good.holds". *(WP1)*
- **Findings are ordered by root cause (build, then new axiom, changed declaration, not proved, …, then markup, then readiness).** The first finding drives the notice; with this order the expected notices of the cheating cases come out. *(WP1)*
- **A "proof" is a theorem, or a Prop-valued def/opaque/instance, except the presupposition instance `instance : Nonempty T := T.exists`.** Lean types that instance as Prop; counting it would make the legitimate new-sort pattern fail "proof before freeze". *(WP1)*
- **Before the freeze, "new axiom" fires only for beliefs (Prop-valued axioms, or a `.holds` of a card that is not a selected assumption); shape problems of non-Prop axioms belong to the vocabulary-shape rule.** A smuggled axiom is reported once. *(WP1)*
- **"Uses sorry" does not report a declaration of yours that is unchanged and already used `sorry` before the run.** As with the token rules: your draft `sorry` in a file Claude must edit would otherwise fail every attempt. *(WP1)*
- **The footprint rule fails closed when Lean listed no axioms for a proof; a check in the prove stage also checks the target's footprint.** "Proved" must never rest on an unchecked footprint; the check gives Claude an early signal. *(WP1)*
- **The frozen snapshot leaves out theorems (proofs may be reworked after the freeze); "statement changed" compares kind, type and value and exempts the target's `.holds`.** The freeze protects statements, vocabulary and definitions (D-19), not proofs. *(WP1)*
- **The markup rule matches blocks by id per file; an added `lean:` line is legal only on a chosen card that had no Lean, naming the new declaration directly below it; a block reported once.** Encodes the reviewer's pin and re-binding rules without double findings. *(WP1)*
- **A definition is a question for you when it is in a card statement's closure or used by a vocabulary item that is not itself a definition or a lemma.** The real-facts test showed that counting lemma references flags proof-only definitions, which need no question. *(WP1)*
- **Normalisation pins only well-formed statements.** A theorem placed directly under a selected block must not be pinned as that card's statement. *(WP1)*
- **The freeze evaluates the rules as the state before this freeze.** Otherwise an adoption's re-freeze or Accept's re-check would flag the adopted card's `.holds` or your own axioms as added after a freeze. *(WP2)*
- **A failing challenge build or export, or any error while preparing the freeze copy, is a machine problem (not counted).** At that point Claude's files have already built and passed the rules. *(WP2)*
- **A timeout or out-of-memory of your own files at the start is reported as a problem with your files ("took too long or too much memory to build"); sandbox, low memory and cancel are machine problems.** It is a property of your files, and the run must end before any prompt either way. *(WP2)*
- **The engine adds a build finding from Lean's facts whenever the rules report none but the build had errors.** Fail closed: a check must never pass Lean errors. *(WP2)*
- **A Lean job's timeout or out-of-memory counts against Claude ("budget"); could-not-start, low memory, cancellation, an unusable working copy and git errors are machine problems.** Only what Claude's text caused is counted. *(WP2)*

## 17. The check loop (A2), notices and the revert

- **Machine problems (sandbox, low memory, unsyncable mirror, cancellation) are not counted; in the final check telelean retries once after 30 s, and a second one ends the run as failed with the reason.** Not Claude's fault; the single retry keeps a transient memory dip from costing the round's work. *(plan)*
- **Edits Claude makes after its check passed are discarded: the proposal always shows the files the check judged.** The proposal must never contain unchecked text. *(plan)*
- **"Insufficient" and "inconsistent" are shown as "not proved" / "Claude reports a conflict (unverified until M3)".** Insufficiency needs a countermodel and consistency the model finder (M3, D-6). *(plan)*
- **The board's sentences name declarations relative to the subject; the attempt notice drops consequences (a footprint on an axiom the attempt itself added, a changed statement already reported as a changed declaration) and duplicates before counting "(and n more)"; one allowed attempt reads "Claude's attempt didn't pass the checks: …"; with no revert label it says "the last state that passed".** Produces the plan's sentences exactly, also for cheats with several findings. *(WP1)*

## 18. Suggested premises ("Claude suggests")

- **`propose_assumption` carries the proof that the suggestion closes the gap (a term statement → target) and an optional Lean name; telelean checks it in a scratch module, never in Claude's files.** D-6 requires a checked proof that the ghost closes the gap, without writing it into the working copy. *(plan)*
- **A suggestion can be adopted only in review; adoption starts a new round that begins frozen.** No file changes under Claude mid-turn; statements are re-frozen only on adoption or Feedback (03). *(plan)*
- **A suggestion must be one Lean term, checked as a named abbreviation (`telelean_ghost_stmt`) in a scratch file that must have no errors; adoption writes exactly the checked text.** The reviewer showed the unpinned form can be fooled into "closes the gap" (plan section 0, fact 8). *(plan)*
- **The single-term rule also refuses `open`, `export`, `omit`, `include`, `coinductive`, `@[` and an empty proof, and brackets must match by kind.** Adoption writes the text into your file: an `open X` after the abbreviation would change how your later declarations resolve names. *(WP1)*
- **Adoption also rejects a name the project's code already uses, re-parses its result and refuses unless exactly one new pinned assumption appears; a multi-line sentence or reason is invalid.** A new declaration named like a used constant would shadow it; the re-parse makes the plan safe by construction. *(WP1)*
- **In the scratch check only the statement is whitespace-collapsed; the proof keeps its lines (indented); "gives the goal on its own" = no selected `.holds` in its axioms.** Collapsing a proof would break tactic blocks. *(WP2)*
- **The tool host derives the suggestion's display name (Claude's name if valid and free, else a slug of the sentence); after adoption the card takes core's final name.** The name must be shown before adoption, while core decides the final one. *(WP3)*

## 19. The proposal, the review and Accept

- **A "not proved" round can still be accepted (its statements and vocabulary), labelled "These suffice → not proved: …".** The formalisation is useful on its own. *(plan)*
- **Every definition question needs an explicit "yes" before Accept; a "no" is Feedback.** Definitions can carry beliefs; they are questions for you, not retries (A2, D-4). *(plan)*
- **Accept puts Claude's changes on top of your current files with M1's no-fuzz patches (an edit of yours within 3 lines of Claude's counts as overlapping), then re-freezes and re-checks with your files at Accept as the base, and applies exactly the re-checked files.** D-21 with M1's undo machinery, without judging your own edits as Claude's. *(plan)*
- **One Accept = one history entry and one Undo step, your hand edits snapshotted first.** A3 and D-21 all-or-nothing; reverting an Accept works like any M1 action. *(plan)*
- **Card changes write only the `type:` line and refuse anything but Goal → Derivation of a goal that is still proved.** M2 proposes no other lifecycle item. *(WP1)*
- **The diff's field names: statement, proof (a status change involving proved/conditional/pending or a changed `.holds`), status, binding, fields.** The walkthrough then shows exactly "(statement, binding)" and "(proof, status)". *(WP1)*
- **The review's pretty and explicit forms are Lean's whole `#print` message.** Matches "the `#print` of the statement abbrev". *(WP2)*
- **Accept after drift re-freezes only a proved proposal; other verdicts are re-checked without a freeze.** The readiness rules apply to the freeze, so freezing an honest "could not formalise" would always refuse Accept. *(WP3)*
- **Accept's patches use exactly 3 context lines (diff 9.0.0's default is 4).** The plan's rule is 3; the tests check the boundary (3 lines away conflicts, 4 merges). *(WP4)*
- **The proposal is rebuilt from the working copy's files plus the check's facts; the proposed board keeps your board's column order (new cards follow in file order) and your attempts history.** Matches "the model over ws/ + the mirror's facts"; cards should not jump around in the overlay. *(WP4)*
- **"Make it a Derivation" is offered only for a proved verdict, a Goal target, and Lean's status "proved" in the proposed board.** Core refuses the change for a target that is not proved, so offering it otherwise would only fail at Accept. *(WP4)*
- **A statement is "new" when your files had no statement for the card, "changed" when its text (docstring included) or its bound name differs.** A simple comparison against your files, as the plan asks. *(WP4)*
- **The vocabulary step lists only new sorts, predicates, functions and constants of the subject; definitions and presuppositions are definition questions; lemmas are proof-only.** Only these kinds are pure signature under D-3 (approved by Accept, revocable). *(WP4)*
- **The report's footprint and unused premises are filled only for "proved"; a selected card counts as used when it is in the footprint or has a verified arrow into the target; adopted cards count as selected.** A proved Derivation shows in a footprint only through its own assumptions, so its verified arrow proves it was used. *(WP4)*
- **A definition question's code and gloss fall back to the declaration's text and docstring in the shown files.** The engine's flag does not always carry them. *(WP4)*
- **The facts of the shown state are kept per run (in memory and `proposal-facts.json`).** run.json holds no facts; without them Accept with the pre-ticked "Make it a Derivation" would fail after a window reload. *(WP4)*
- **During Accept's re-check, a file you edit meanwhile is kept if the merge left that file alone, otherwise Accept refuses ("press Accept again to include your edits"); a file missing from the merged state is never deleted.** Applying only the merged state would silently overwrite typing done during the re-check. *(WP4)*
- **Refusal sentences start with a capital letter.** The board shows them as they are. *(WP4)*
- **Accept writes only model files (`<library>.lean`, `<library>/**.lean`), each once, for a valid subject; changes that change nothing are dropped; it does not require the first snapshot to succeed.** Plan 7.2 says Accept never writes anything else; your edits are kept in the merged text and the undo entry. *(WP4)*
- **The raw diff compares the base with the working copy as it is now.** In review the working copy holds exactly the shown state (it is restored after a failed re-check). *(WP4)*

## 20. Logs of runs: attempts and decisions

- **`attempts.jsonl` and `decisions.json` are written directly, never undone, not in history snapshots, not gitignored.** They log what happened and what you answered; D-12 says they are committed with your own commits. *(plan)*
- **They are per subject (`.telelean/subjects/<S>/…`), next to M1's `layout.json`, rather than D-12's single root-level files.** Consistent with M1's per-subject layout and D-10's subjects. *(plan)*
- **Claude's guesses are kept on the host side until you answer.** D-20: no pre-selected answer, enforced by the data flow rather than by hiding them in the UI. *(plan)*
- **Reading these files is lenient (bad or newer lines are skipped); writing only orders keys and never drops entries; the latest resolution wins; a new answer replaces the old one in place.** Hand edits never break the board, and writing never loses a recorded answer. *(WP1)*
- **`attempts.jsonl` is read through the open-buffer-first text source (at load, on reload, on change); the board gets a copy only when it is not empty.** Consistent with `layout.json`; the file watcher already covers the path. *(WP4)*
- **Appends go through one queue per file per process, complete a missing final newline first, and `decisions.json` is replaced atomically through a temp file in `.telelean/` (fsync, rename).** No lost updates or joined lines; temp files are covered by the scaffold's `/.telelean/*.tmp` ignore line. *(WP4)*

## 21. What leaves the machine, the Claude backend and quota safety

- **The system prompt is static and byte-identical across runs; everything about your project (including the subject's folder) goes into the first message.** Prompt caching across runs, and what is sent sits in one inspectable place. *(plan)*
- **Consent is asked once per model folder and names exactly what is sent.** D-23 disclosure without asking on every run. *(plan)*
- **Claude Code runs under `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL` (absolute path).** A crashed extension host must not leave a detached CLI running (M0 open item). *(plan)*
- **The Claude backend is created lazily (at the first start that passed preflight); in Test mode the extension refuses real Claude; `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1` in every test runner makes the backend factory and the CLI launch refuse.** Opening a board never runs a Claude binary, and three independent tripwires keep tests from spending quota. *(plan)*
- **The cost shown is Claude Code's latest figure, never a sum.** Its `total_cost_usd` already covers the whole conversation across `--resume` (M0). *(plan)*
- **The live walkthrough is driven by a script with a scripted user; it is a dry run by default and live only with `--live` plus `TELELEAN_WALKTHROUGH_LIVE=yes`.** The main session cannot click in VS Code; the double opt-in keeps any builder or test from spending quota. *(plan)*
- **The system prompt's source was generated from the plan's text by a script, and a test compares it with the plan.** Guarantees byte-exactness (backticks, special characters). *(WP3)*
- **The first message describes a formalised selected assumption without its axiom as "assumed, but its axiom … is missing (add it)".** The template had no wording for this case, and the system prompt tells Claude to add it. *(WP3)*
- **Only a "yes" to the consent is remembered; a "no" starts nothing and asks again next time.** Remembering a "no" would lock you out with no way back in the UI. *(WP5)*
- **The consent modal splits the plan's text into the message "Run Claude on this model?" and the rest as detail, verbatim; the button is "Run with Claude".** Keeps the exact wording in VS Code's modal layout. *(WP5)*
- **The binary search looks first in the folder of the Claude Code extension VS Code runs, then `~/.vscode/extensions`, `~/.vscode-server/extensions`, the PATH and `~/.local/bin`.** The Claude Code you actually use is found first (A1). *(WP5)*
- **`import.meta.url` in the bundled runner is replaced by the bundle's own file URL (an injected constant, keeping strict mode); the guard script's path is always passed explicitly.** A banner would silently drop strict mode, and the CommonJS bundle has no `import.meta`. *(WP5)*

## 22. The extension host and settings

- **The extension checks for an active run before asking for consent; any active run of the folder refuses the start with a sentence saying what to do.** Never ask for consent for a start that cannot happen. *(WP5)*
- **Run messages have their own queue (in arrival order); Cancel skips it; the raw diff is outside the queues.** A start (the first Lean build) or an Accept re-check must not block typing a card, and Cancel must be able to stop a start in progress. *(WP5)*
- **Successes of start, cancel, resume, Accept, Feedback, Discard and the suggestion buttons show a toast; only Accept's has Undo; answers and dismissals show none.** One Accept is one undoable step; a start's Undo would only undo the premises declaration while the run goes on. *(WP5)*
- **After every run message the run is posted again; start and Accept also republish the board; on "ready" the run and the proposal are posted even when empty.** The panel follows at once, and a reloaded board clears a stale run. *(WP5)*
- **Run settings are clamped: maxTurns 1–1000, maxChecks 1–500, maxAgentMinutes 1–240, leanJobSeconds 10–1800, maxGateAttempts 1–10, keepRuns 1–100; a malformed model name falls back to the default; `claude.path` is trimmed and `~` expanded.** Generous limits that keep runs bounded; mistyped values fall back as in M1. *(WP5)*
- **Run settings take effect after a window reload; `claude.path` is read when the backend is first needed.** As in M1; the binary search inputs are only needed at the first start. *(WP5)*
- **Deactivation disposes the run managers first (waiting at most 4 s), while their workspaces still exist.** Persisting the run and closing Claude must happen before the rest is torn down. *(WP5)*
- **The raw diff's tab is "Raw Lean diff: <subject> (round n)" (or the file name); no changes give an information toast.** Short titles keep the board's tab in place; the message has no reply channel. *(WP5)*
- **M1's text for "These suffice" without premises now points to the tray's "Self-evident?".** The M1 text ("arrives in M2") was wrong for M2. *(WP5)*
- **Not implemented (a suggestion for later): a VS Code notification with "Open Board" when a run waits for you while its board is closed.** Runs go on without a board (D-25), so you might not notice; outside the plan. *(WP5)*

## 23. The board

- **The run panel sits beside the board (320–460 px wide), below it on boards narrower than 1000 px; it opens by itself on a new run, a question, review, an interruption or the end; the header badge shows and hides it.** Questions and the review are tall; beside the board they leave its height intact. *(WP6)*
- **A new proposal switches the board to Proposed, and until the review reveals the result the overlay hides the target's proof result (chips, footprint, verified arrows, the verdict in the state line and banner).** D-19's "meaning before proof status" would be undone if the overlay showed "proved" before the statements were read. *(WP6)*
- **"Claude suggests" cards go at the top of the Assumptions column, only in the Proposed view, and are not model cards for arrows and counts.** The opened "+N new" vocabulary would push cards placed at the end out of view; suggestions need a decision. *(WP6)*
- **The Proposed view is read-only (no selection, drag, edit or delete); adding a card from the A|D|G box switches back to Current.** The overlay is not your files; a new card belongs to the current board (D-16). *(WP6)*
- **The banner's Accept follows the review's rule (every definition "yes", the review's ticks).** The plan puts Accept in the banner; the definition approvals are its only precondition. *(WP6)*
- **Feedback prefills ("Ask me instead", "Revoke…", a definition's "No") go on new lines of one draft; Ctrl+Enter sends.** Several revocations or questions can go into one Feedback round. *(WP6)*
- **"Stop" on an interrupted run posts Discard.** Plan section 2: interrupted → Stop = Discard. *(WP6)*
- **Diff marks use VS Code's git decoration colours (added, modified, deleted) plus a glyph, a word and a halo.** No new contributed colours, and never colour alone. *(WP6)*
- **The agent clock is interpolated between updates from the time the host measured it, while Claude works or a check runs, capped at the limit, and marked "(paused)" while a question waits.** The host posts on events, not every second. *(WP6)*
- **The dependents dialog words one dependent in the singular ("Rewrite that proof to …", "Keep that proof, marked broken").** Matches core's frozen "that proof" wording. *(WP6)*
- **A "needs confirmation" that lists nothing beyond what you just confirmed becomes an error toast instead of another dialog; the optional reason of a change to Assumption is sent again with the answer.** Avoids a question loop; your reason is no longer lost (an M1 gap). *(WP6)*
- **With only a target selected, "Self-evident?" replaces "These suffice ▶" and the "drops your declared premises" note is not shown.** Self-evident? declares nothing, so it drops nothing. *(WP6)*
- **The "these cards" scope is disabled when a question names no card; own-words answers may span lines; the reason for adopting a suggestion is one line.** Follows the protocol's validators. *(WP6)*
- **The review is keyed by run and proposal id.** Proposal ids (p1, p2, …) are unique within a run only. *(WP6)*
- **The tray's three buttons (These suffice ▶, Add to its premises ▶, Self-evident?) all start a run; the board no longer sends M1's declare-only "theseSuffice".** M2's "These suffice" declares and proves in one step (decision in section 14). *(WP6)*

## 24. M1 carry-overs

- **"Used by" and the delete dialog list users outside the board (lemmas without a card, other subjects' cards): proof users first, the search stops at any card, the text scan runs only while a file is not freshly checked, one index per model.** "Nothing uses it" was wrong when only a lemma or another subject used the card; linear cost (147 ms for 2000 cards). *(WP1)*
- **One dependent is worded in the singular, with the frozen texts of plan 1.3.** Carry-over 2. *(WP1)*
- **A kind change whose confirmed dependents do not cover every dependent the planner finds is refused with "needs confirmation" (the same message), listing them all; the board re-asks with that list.** Carry-over 3: M1 applied the choice to dependents the dialog never showed. *(WP1, WP6)*
- **A test runs the gate rules on recorded real Lean 4.35 facts, besides the hand-made ones.** The main risk was fake versus real facts; it found the flagged-definition bug. *(WP1)*

## 25. Tests and tooling

- **`AcceptProposalAction` stayed a separate type and the ModelWorkspace's M2 members stayed optional until integration.** The webview's exhaustive label table and the M1 test fakes kept compiling while the builders worked in parallel. *(plan)*
- **The runner's factories take core test hooks; cross-package tests were marked [gated] and ran at integration.** Each work package could test its own logic while the others were stubs. *(plan)*
- **The walkthrough fixtures carry test metadata (answer, premises, adopt, expected outcome) beside the playable turns, and turns are matched by their text.** A script stays in step across reminders and resumed sessions, and the tests and the dry-run script share the files. *(WP3)*
- **The VS Code run suite uses its own pristine model copy and inlines the normative script.** Another suite changes `ws/mental_model`; independent of the fixture format. *(WP5)*

## 26. Integration (int)

- **`HistoryActionKind` now includes `accept-proposal`, and the ModelWorkspace's M2 members are required; every builder gate (`isImplemented` and the webview's carry-over gate) is gone.** Plan 11 step 2; every test of the plan now runs. *(int)*
- **`RunManager.dispose()` writes run.json at once and returns a promise that resolves after the writes queued before it, with the final "interrupted" state written last (`RunFiles.close`).** Queued writes used to land after the synchronous one and leave run.json saying "working" (WP5's AT5.9). *(int)*
- **M1's integration tests confirm exactly the dependents the planner lists (both the derivation and the goal that uses it, for the "rewrite" of a change to Goal).** Carry-over 3 refuses a choice that does not cover every dependent. *(int)*
- **The VS Code run suite waits for a dismissed run to leave the board instead of for a reply.** `dismissRun` carries no request id (plan 6.3), so no reply comes; the old wait timed out after 240 s. *(int)*
- **A new end-to-end suite (`e2e-runs.test.ts`) drives "These suffice" through the real board over the DevTools protocol in the e2e instance, on its own model copy (`runs-e2e/runs_e2e_model`); the smoke instance's file pattern excludes `e2e*`.** Only trusted clicks in the real webview show that the question card, the overlay, the review, the ghost card and Accept work end to end. *(int)*
- **That suite installs one backend that switches FakeBackend scripts per test.** The RunManager keeps the backend its factory returned, so a script per run needs a switch rather than a new factory. *(int)*
- **A runner integration test (`test/integration/m2flow.test.ts`) runs the plan's 11.4 flows in a user's repository layout: Accept/Undo/Redo/History revert, literal adoption, Accept after drift (merge and conflict), the premises declaration and a refused start, recovery with a pending question.** The plan's integrator test; it also checks that HEAD, index, branches, config, hooks and status outside the model never change. *(int)*
- **The root build's npm debug logs go to the integrator's scratch folder (`npm_config_logs_dir`), never `logs-max=0`.** npm would otherwise write into and prune the real `~/.npm/_logs`. *(int)*
- **`RunView.updatedAt` is left as it is: it is already stamped at the same moment as Claude's working time.** The board's clock interpolation (WP6) needed exactly that; no change was required. *(int)*
- **A refused re-freeze after an adoption leaves its `adopt` commit in the working copy's history; left as it is.** The rules consult that reference only for adopted cards, whose text it holds unchanged; no wrong verdict follows (checked by analysis and the end-to-end tests). *(int)*
- **`.telelean/graph.json` still lists no attempts (`attempts: []`); only the board's graphs carry them.** graph.json's export takes no attempts; left for later (WP4 note). *(int)*

# telelean: user guide (M1 board, M2 Claude runs)

M1 is "the map without AI": a board of your ASSUMPTION / DERIVATION / GOAL cards, read from and written to Lean files, checked by Lean, with undo and git history. M2 adds one-shot **"These suffice"**: you select premises and a target, Claude formalises and proves in a private copy of your model, telelean checks the result with Lean and a fixed set of rules, and nothing reaches your files until you review the proposal and press **Accept** (section 10). Nothing calls Claude until you press "These suffice" and allow it.

| Declare support and prove (M2) | select the premises and one goal (click; Ctrl/Cmd+click adds to the selection); the tray takes the goal as target (with several, pick it with ⊢); **These suffice ▶** declares exactly the selected premises (undoable, as in M1) and asks Claude to prove the target from them (section 10). If the target already declares premises you did not select, the tray says w
**Vocabulary group:** the sorts, predicates, constants, functions, presuppositions ("assumes characters exist"), definitions and lemmas of the subject; "hidden assumption" marks a Prop axiom without a card. Items of another subject that this subject's cards use (through an explicit `import`) are listed too, under their full names (e.g. `Spyro.IsPG`), so their glosses show on hover.

## 8. Limits of the board (M1)

- (M1 alone had no AI; M2's runs and their limits are in sections 10 and 10.14.)
- No Lean-editor features (hover, completion, code lenses: M4) and no Mathlib or other Lake dependencies (M4).
- Only toolchain `v4.35.0` is checked by Lean; others get syntactic mode.
- Lean checks run only while the model's board is open: when it opens, after a save in VS Code, after telelean's own edits, when another program (a script, git, an agent) writes a Lean file of the model, and when you click the badge. The build runs in your model folder, so it can race your Lean extension on `.lake` (a redundant rebuild at worst; delete `.lake` if a build looks damaged).
- Undo is lost on window reload (History is not). History needs git.
- No drawing arrows by dragging; definitions are flagged, not endorsed.
- Settings (`telelean.*`: memory cap 4 GiB, pause below 2 GiB available, refresh on/off and delay, history on/off, git path) take effect after a window reload (open boards come back by themselves after the reload). The memory cap is lowered automatically when less memory is free, so a check stops at its own cap rather than straining the machine.
- Files telelean deletes (for example Undo of a new subject, or a Revert) go through VS Code, which moves them to the OS trash with its default settings.

## 9. Troubleshooting

/--
Runs `build` as a build action of kind `action`.

The build's input trace (`depTrace`), JSON description of the result of `build`,
and log are saved to `traceFile`, if the build completes without a fatal error
(i.e., it does not `throw`).
-/
@[specialize] public def buildAction
  [ToOutputJson α]
  (depTrace : BuildTrace) (traceFile : FilePath) (build : JobM α)
  (action : JobAction := .build)
: JobM α := do
  updateAction action
  let noBuildTraceFile := traceFile.addExtension "nobuild"
  if (← getNoBuild) then
    modify ({· with wantsRebuild := true})
    if (← traceFile.pathExists) then
      writeBuildTrace noBuildTraceFile depTrace Json.null {}
    error s!"target is out-of-date and needs to be rebuilt"
  else
    let startTime ← IO.monoMsNow
    try
      let iniPos ← getLogPos
      let a ← build -- fatal errors will abort here
      let log := (← getLog).takeFrom iniPos
      writeBuildTrace traceFile depTrace (toOutputJson a) log
      removeFileIfExists noBuildTraceFile
      return a
    finally
      let endTime ← IO.monoMsNow
      let elapsed := endTime - startTime
      modify fun s => {s with buildTime := s.buildTime + elapsed}

If rebuilt, saves the new `depTrace` and build log to `traceFile`.
Returns whether `info` was already up-to-date.

**Up-to-date Checking**

If `traceFile` exists, checks that the hash in `depTrace` matches that
of the `traceFile`. If not, and old mode is enabled (e.g., `--old`), falls back
to the `oldTrace` modification time as the point of comparison.
If up-to-date, replay the build log stored in `traceFile`.

......
  (file : FilePath) (build : JobM PUnit)
  (text := false) (ext := "art") (restore := false) (exe := false)
  (platformIndependent := false)
: JobM Artifact := do
  let depTrace ← getTrace
  let traceFile := FilePath.mk <| file.toString ++ ".trace"
  let savedTrace ← readTraceFile traceFile
  if let some pkg ← getCurrPackage? then
    let inputHash := depTrace.hash
    let fetchArt? restore := do
      let some (art : XArtifact exe) ← getArtifacts? inputHash savedTrace pkg
        | return none
      unless (← savedTrace.replayCachedIfUpToDate inputHash) do
        removeFileIfExists file
        writeFetchTrace traceFile inputHash (toJson art.descr)
      if restore then
        some <$> restoreArtifact file art exe
      else
        return some art
    let art ← id do
      if (← pkg.isArtifactCacheWritable) then
        let restore := restore || (← pkg.restoreAllArtifacts)
        if let some art ← fetchArt? restore then
          return art
        else
          let status ← savedTrace.replayIfUpToDate' file depTrace
          unless status.isUpToDate do
            discard <| doBuild depTrace traceFile
          if status.isCacheable then
            let art ← cacheArtifact file ext text exe restore
            (← getLakeCache).writeOutputs pkg.cacheScope inputHash art.descr
            return art
          else
            computeArtifact file ext text
      else if (← savedTrace.replayIfUpToDate file depTrace) then
        computeArtifact file ext text
      else
        if (← pkg.isArtifactCacheReadable) then
          if let some art ← fetchArt? (restore := true) then
            return art
        doBuild depTrace traceFile
    if let some ref ← Internal.getOutputsRef? pkg then
      ref.insert inputHash art.descr platformIndependent
    setTrace art.trace
    setMTime art traceFile
  else
    let art ←
      if (← savedTrace.replayIfUpToDate file depTrace) then
        computeArtifact file ext text
      else
        doBuild depTrace traceFile
    setTrace art.trace
    setMTime art traceFile
where
  doBuild depTrace traceFile :=
    inline <| buildAction depTrace traceFile do
      removeFileIfExists file
      build
      clearFileHash file
      removeFileIfExists traceFile
      computeArtifact file ext text
  setMTime art traceFile := do
    match (← getMTime traceFile |>.toBaseIO) with
    | .ok mtime =>
      return {art with mtime}
    | .error (.noFileOrDirectory ..) => -- trace file may not exist
      return art
    | .error e =>

#!/bin/bash
# memwatch.sh <root-pid> <logfile>: samples MemAvailable every 2 s while root-pid lives; logs the minimum;
# if MemAvailable < 8000 MB, sends TERM to root-pid's own process tree only (my processes).
ROOT=$1; OUT=$2; MINAVAIL=999999
desc() { local p=$1; echo $p; for c in $(pgrep -P $p 2>/dev/null); do desc $c; done; }
while kill -0 $ROOT 2>/dev/null; do
  AV=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  [ $AV -lt $MINAVAIL ] && MINAVAIL=$AV
  if [ $AV -lt 8000 ]; then echo "$(date +%T) LOW MEMORY ($AV MB): killing tree of $ROOT" >> $OUT; for p in $(desc $ROOT); do kill -TERM $p 2>/dev/null; done; fi
  sleep 2
done
echo "DONE minAvail=${MINAVAIL}MB" >> $OUT

Sections 1–13 are M1 ("the map without AI"); sections 14–26 are M2 (one-shot "These suffice" with Claude), further down; section 27 lists the fixes after M2's verification (round 1, core, runner and docs), section 28 those of round 2 (core, runner, scripts and docs) together with one open question for you.

None of these needed your approval to proceed, and all of them can be reversed. If you disagree with one, say which and it can be changed.

Contract changes (new exports, optional fields) are listed separately in `docs/m1-plan.md` section 14.

## 15. Claude's working copy (the shadow)

- **Claude's root (`ws/`) holds only model files; Lean builds in a separate mirror (`build/`), synced before every Lean job.** Claude Code's Grep/Glob search hidden files (M0 lesson 4); the mirror keeps `.lake` out of Claude's root with no sandbox change, and Lean's facts are root-relative so paths match. *(plan)*
- **The working copy's git history lives outside `ws/` (`git/`, work tree `ws/`) with an isolated git config.** No dot-entry in Claude's root; your global git config cannot affect telelean's private history. *(plan)*
- **Every model file of the project (all subjects) goes into the working copy; the first message covers only the run's subject.** Imports between subjects must build (D-10); Claude can read the other subjects' files, which the consent text says. *(plan)*
- **Run ids double as the sandbox's scope groups.** Cancel kills every Lean job of a run with one `systemctl --user kill`. *(plan)*
- **The history is a bare repository written with `git fast-import` (whole snapshots) and read with `ls-tree`/`cat-file`; all `GIT_*` variables are dropped and config, hooks, excludes and attributes point at `/dev/null`.** A commit is then exactly the judged bytes, and no git setting, filter, attribute or hook of yours can touch it. *(WP2)*
- **The "statements frozen" commit is made only after the comparator's challenge was exported.** A failed freeze must not leave a commit that a give-up revert could land on. *(WP2)*
- **A working copy is refused when your model folder holds a symlink under the library folder (or a symlinked model or project file); a symlinked `.lake` is simply not seeded.** A symlinked model file could pull outside text into what Claude reads. *(WP2)*
- **The base commit is round 1; the history lists commits oldest first.** The first round starts from the base. *(WP2)*
- **The mirror keeps your file's modification time when its text equals the file on disk.** Keeps a seeded `.lake/build` valid (Lake 4.35 decides rebuilds by content hash, verified). *(WP2)*
- **Freeze copies keep their sources in `frozen/<n>/project` but drop their `.lake`; comparator work directories are `gate/<n>`; your files' facts are in `base-facts.json`.** Run directories stay small while what was frozen stays inspectable. *(WP2)*
- **The check reuses the newest normalise or checkpoint commit when it holds exactly the files in `ws/`, else commits a checkpoint ("State judged by the gate (round N)").** One judged commit per state, no duplicates on a repeated finish. *(WP2)*
- **A ghost check reuses the last clean check only when it was of exactly `ws/`'s files and the mirror still holds them; the engine's caches are bounded (32 models, 16 runs).** One engine serves many runs; the content comparison guards against the mirror changing under it. *(WP2)*

## 10. Proving with Claude: "These suffice" (M2)

A run asks Claude to decide whether the target card follows from exactly the premises you selected. Claude works in a private copy of your model (never in your files): it formalises the cards that have no Lean yet, freezes the statements, proves, and says it is finished. telelean then checks the result itself, with Lean and fixed rules. You review a proposal on the board and decide: **Accept**, **Feedback** or **Discard**.

### 10.1 What you need

- **Claude Code**, logged in with your claude.ai subscription. telelean uses your own Claude Code (no API key): by default the binary of the VS Code Claude Code extension, else `claude` on the PATH, else `~/.local/bin/claude` (setting `telelean.claude.path` to choose one). Version 2.1.295 or newer.
- The model builds with toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0` and has no Lake dependencies; the Lean sandbox works (as for M1's checks); enough free memory (`telelean.memory.minAvailableGiB`).
- **Your files must build.** Right after the run starts telelean builds your files once; Lean errors anywhere end the run before Claude is contacted ("your files have Lean errors (…); fix or save them, then start again").

### 10.2 Starting a run

1. On the board, click the premises, then Ctrl/Cmd+click the target (a Goal or a Derivation; an Assumption is something you hold: make it a Derivation first). The tray shows "premises ⊢ target".
2. Press **These suffice ▶** (exactly these premises), **Add to its premises ▶** (the target's declared premises plus the selected ones) or, with only the target selected, **Self-evident?** (no premises at all).
3. The first time in a model folder, telelean asks for your consent (10.3).
4. telelean checks the start before anything is sent ("preflight"): no other run of this model folder is active; the selection is valid; toolchain, sandbox and memory are fine; Claude Code is found. Any refusal changes nothing. Only then does it declare the selected premises on the target (`premises:`, M1's undoable action; skipped when they are already declared, and never for Self-evident?), make the private copy, build your files once, and start Claude Code. Claude Code itself checks before the first prompt that you are logged in with a claude.ai subscription; a refusal there costs no quota.

At most one run per model folder at a time. Closing the board does not stop a run: the header badge ("Claude: working on Spyro · 3/25 checks") shows it in any board of the folder.

### 10.3 Consent and what leaves the machine

Before the first run in a model folder telelean asks: *"Run Claude on this model? telelean sends this subject's cards (sentences, reasons, Lean statements), its vocabulary and your recorded answers, plus any model file Claude reads, to Anthropic through your Claude Code login (your claude.ai subscription; no API key)."* **Run with Claude** is remembered for that folder; **Cancel** starts nothing and is not remembered (you are asked again next time).

What is sent, through your Claude Code login: a fixed system prompt (the same text every run), the first message (the target, the selected premises and the subject's other cards with their sentences, reasons and Lean; the vocabulary; your earlier answers that are in force; the run's budget), every model file Claude reads in its copy (all subjects of the project are in the copy, so imports work), and every tool result (Lean check results, your answers, the check verdicts). Your Feedback text and your answers go as messages. telelean sends nothing else from your machine. Claude Code itself may also send its own usage telemetry and error reports, as it does in your other sessions: the switches that turn those off (`DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` for all non-essential traffic) are passed on to telelean's runs when VS Code was started with them.

What stays on your machine: each run's directory in VS Code's storage for telelean (`~/.config/Code/User/globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs/…`: Claude's working copy, its Lean build, its git history, `run.json` and `session/transcript.jsonl`, the exact text of every message and tool call). The newest `telelean.run.keepRuns` (10) finished runs per model folder are kept. Claude Code also keeps its own transcript of each session under `~/.claude/projects/` (that is how a session is resumed); telelean never reads it.

### 10.4 The run panel

The panel opens beside the board when a run starts (below the board on a narrow board); the header badge shows and hides it. Its status line: state and stage ("Working · formalising", "· proving", "Waiting for your answer", "Checking Claude's result", "Ready for review"), the round, Lean checks used (3/25), Claude's turns (12/80), Claude's working time (paused while a question waits for you), check attempts (1/3), tokens, the cost estimate and the usage-limit status. Below: **notices** (the check results, reverts, caps, machine problems), the **activity** feed (each check, freeze, suggestion; Claude's own words in italics with a "Claude" marker) and your answered questions. **Cancel** stops the run (10.11).

Everything Claude wrote (its messages, questions, summaries, suggested premises, glosses of new vocabulary) is shown in italics with a marker, never in the style of your own words.

### 10.5 Claude's questions

When a sentence can be read in ways that change the result (modality, genericity, scope, word sense, …), Claude asks first: up to three questions at a time, each with a tag ("modality"), its options with their plain consequences, **In my own words**, **Leave it open** and **Decide for me**, and a scope for your answer: **this run** (default), **these cards** or **the whole subject**. Send it with **Send answers**. Claude's own guess is shown only after you answered (it never reaches the board before). Claude's clock is paused while it waits for you.

# memwatch.sh <root-pid> <logfile>: samples MemAvailable every 2 s while root-pid lives; logs the minimum;
# if MemAvailable < 8000 MB, sends TERM to root-pid's own process tree only (my processes).
ROOT=$1; OUT=$2; MINAVAIL=999999
desc() { local p=$1; echo $p; for c in $(pgrep -P $p 2>/dev/null); do desc $c; done; }
while kill -0 $ROOT 2>/dev/null; do

  sleep 2

## 29. Fixes after the M2 verification, round 3 (core, runner, docs)

- **A run's working copy takes your Lean build (`.lake/build`) only when it is a finished build; while Lake is writing it, the run starts with an empty build instead of being refused.** A save or an Undo shortly before "These suffice" (and the start's own premises declaration) makes the board rebuild your files in place; the copy used to run beside that build, so a start could fail with "cannot create the shadow: ENOENT", or copy Lake's temporary files, or mix two builds, which Lake might then have trusted when it checked Claude's proof. Now the copy waits for telelean's own Lean job and is used only when nothing in it changes while it is copied, no Lake temporary file or lock is there, and no compiled file is newer than the record Lake writes after it (true of every finished Lake 4.35 build, checked with the pinned toolchain). Otherwise the run builds from scratch, which is always correct and costs about a second for Spyro. *(fix)*
- **Every `example` Claude adds is refused, in every check and whatever the finish status (this replaces section 28's "an example written after the freeze is not judged").** An example is a proof without a name: nothing can check what it rests on, nothing can use it, and your files never need one. It was judged only before the freeze in rounds that froze, so a round that ended "not proved" without freezing could write an example resting on an assumption you did not select into your files (the verifier showed it). Claude now learns it at its first check, and the system prompt says so. *(fix)*
- **The system prompt now says that everything Claude adds, definitions, instances and structures included, may rest only on the selected premises, and lists `example` among the forbidden things.** The checks have held every declaration to that rule since section 28, but the prompt still spoke only of theorems, so Claude would learn it from a failed attempt, which costs one of its 3 attempts and some of your quota. *(fix)*
- **Accept records whether it changed your files on the run itself (`accepted` on the run's data), not only in the wording of its notice.** A board that did not send the Accept (another window, or one opened later) decided between "Accepted" and "Recorded" by reading that wording; the dependency is now written down in the plan's change log, and the board can read the new field instead. *(fix)*

# walkthrough fixtures (M2, WP3)

FakeBackend scripts as data, for docs/m2-plan.md sections 10.2 (the two walkthrough readings) and 10.3 (the
cheating cases). Used by `packages/runner/test/run/walkthrough.e2e.test.ts` (AT3.14, AT3.15: real engine, real
Lean, a scratch git copy of `mental_model/`), by the RunManager's unit tests, and by
`scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --dry-run`. Nothing here is ever compiled: Lean text (including `sorry` and
`#eval`) appears only inside JSON strings.

## Format

```json
{
  "name": "normative",
  "description": "…",
  "answer": { "phenomenon": "modality", "option": 0 },
  "premises": ["cynder-dark-past", "new-spyro-pg", "pg-no-dark-past"],
  "expect": { "verdict": "proved", "…": "…" },
  "turns": [{ "match": "Run: \"These suffice\"", "steps": [ { "kind": "read", "path": "Model/Spyro/Main.lean" }, … ] }]
}
```

- `turns` are played in order by `llm.playFakeScript` (runner `src/llm/fakeScripts.ts`): each user turn takes the
  next unplayed turn whose `match` (if any) occurs in the turn text. Round 1 matches the context bundle
  (`Run: "These suffice"`), an adoption round `The person adopted your suggestion`. A user turn the script did not
  plan (for example a nudge) gets no steps. The cursor survives a resumed session (`--resume`).
- `steps` are runner `FakeStep`s: `read`, `edit` (`oldString` → `newString`, first occurrence, through the same
  path guard as the CLI's hook), `writeFile`, `callTool` (validated with the real tool schemas, dispatched to the
  RunManager's tool host), `text`, `usage` (one API response), `rateLimit`, `sleep`, `result` (with the CLI's
  cumulative `costEstimateUsd`).
- `answer`, `premises`, `adopt`, `userEdits` and `expect` are read by the tests and the walkthrough script, not by the
  player: the test answers the modality question with `answer.option`, starts the run with `premises`, and checks
  `expect`. `userEdits` (optional, `{ path, oldString, newString }` like an edit step) are the user's own edits to the
  scratch copy before the run starts (they are part of B), e.g. a code-less GOAL card to select as a premise.
- Every edit applies to both `mental_model/` and `test-fixtures/spyro/` (whose `Main.lean` differ by one import
  line); a check of that ran when the files were written.

| `normative.json` | reading A: asks the modality question (answered "a rule"), formalises `pg_no_dark_past` normatively, checks, freezes, proves from the three premises, finishes `proved` | proved; G→D lifecycl

- Listing the user's build, creating the run directory and copying the build all happen inside semantic.runExclusive, the same lock the board's in-place refresh holds.

  - no Lake build lock (lake.lock) is present;

## 7. Accept: the shadow's diff onto the real files, through M1's edit and history machinery

### 7.1 Steps (WP3 orchestrates; WP4 plans and applies; WP2 re-checks)

1. **Preconditions**: state `review`; `proposalId` is the current proposal; every `DefinitionQuestion` id is in `definitions` (else `invalid`: "answer every definition question: a “no” is feedback"); lifecycle ids exist.
2. **Drift**: `proposals.baseDrift(shadow, ws.readText, ws.modelFiles())` = model files whose real text (open buffer first) differs from the base, including files the user added or deleted during the run.
3. **Plan**: `proposals.planAccept` → for every model file: base→shown patch (`diff` 9.0.0 `structuredPatch`, default 3 context lines) applied to the real text with no fuzz (`applyPatch`), exactly M1's undo technique; a patch that does not apply → `conflict` naming the file ("your edits to <file> since the run started overlap Claude's; Discard, or Feedback to redo it on your current files"). Because of the context lines, an edit of the user's within 3 lines of a change of Claude's counts as overlapping. Files only the user changed keep the user's text. Then the ticked lifecycle items (core `lifecycleChanges`: G→D changes only `type:`).
4. **Re-check on drift (D-21)**: when drift ≠ ∅: remember the current head (the shown state); write the user's real model files into ws/ and commit `accept-base`; write `shadowState` (merged, without lifecycle items) and commit `rebase`; run `engine.normalise`, `engine.freeze` and `engine.gate` (with the round's status) with `baseCommit` = the `accept-base` commit (so B = the user's files at Accept: their own edits during the run are never judged as Claude's) and `roundStartCommit` = the `rebase` commit (the existing proof is not "a proof before the freeze"). The freeze copy drops the target's `.holds` and every declaration that uses it, transitively from the facts' refs (other cards' proofs included), so the challenge `theorem T.holds : T := sorry` neither clashes nor breaks a dependent (the same rule serves a pending-promotion target whose claimed `.holds` other proofs use). A failure restores ws/ to the remembered head, refuses Accept with the findings (core `describeFinding`), and leaves the proposal open (Feedback can redo it). On success `planAccept` runs again with `shownState` = ws/ as re-gated, so exactly the re-gated files (plus the ticked lifecycle items) are applied.
5. **Apply**: `proposals.apply(plan, workspace, subject)` → `ModelWorkspace.applyChanges({ label, action: 'accept-proposal', subject, nodes, changes })`, which uses M1's recorded write path unchanged (`applyRecorded`): **"Manual edits" / "Initial state" snapshots of the touched scopes first** (private refs, D-33/A3), then the EditApplier (the extension: WorkspaceEdit + save; its `before` check refuses if a file changed between plan and apply → `conflict`, nothing applied), then the undo entry (one entry for the whole proposal: **Undo reverts the Accept**), then the action's snapshot (history entry "These suffice → proved: Cynder would not be a good addition…"), re-read, graph.json, a Lean refresh of the real files.
6. **Afterwards**: attempt resolution `accepted`, session closed, state `accepted`, `proposal` null; the board's next refresh shows the real statuses (e.g. cynder-not-good proved, in the Derivations column).

### 7.2 What Accept never does

It never writes a file outside the subject's scope and the project's model files, never applies part of a proposal, never applies a lifecycle item the user did not tick, never runs while the real files conflict, and never skips the snapshot-first step (a revert of the Accept through History is possible as for any M1 action).

### 7.3 Sidecars (WP4 store; formats core `run.ts`; paths core `paths.ts`)

- `.telelean/subjects/<S>/attempts.jsonl`: one `AttemptRecord` per round end (verdict, premises, footprint, ghosts, Claude's summary cut to 500 characters, gate attempts, model, effort, usage), plus `AttemptResolution` lines (`accepted`/`discarded`/`superseded`). Append-only (`O_APPEND`), never undone, not in history snapshots (M1's `isSubjectSidecarFile` still covers only layout.json and attic/), not gitignored (D-12: committed by the user's own commits). `ModelWorkspace.reloadAttempts(S)` re-reads it; `graph(S).attempts` lists them newest first.
- `.telelean/subjects/<S>/decisions.json`: one `DecisionRecord` per answered question, written when the user answers (atomic replace inside `.telelean/`), same storage rules. Decisions with scope `subject` (and `nodes` meeting the selection) are "in force" for later runs (context bundle); revoking them is M3.

issues.description: An axiom placed directly below the block of a selected premise that is not an ASSUMPTION (a code-less GOAL or DERIVATION card, which preflight accepts as a premise) becomes that card's statement. It then escapes every axiom rule, and a non-Prop one enters the permitted set. Three gaps combine. (1) new-axiom: isBelief (core/src/gate/rules.ts:154-161) returns false for any card-owned axiom that is not the card's .holds. (2) vocabulary-shape (rules.ts:401-414) never sees it: owned declarations are not vocabulary (project/build.ts ~line 374). (3) Readiness (rules.ts:420-421) checks only the target and selected ASSUMPTIONs or ghosts, so a TL113 'not a Prop abbrev' statement on a GOAL premise is ignored. Finally signatureAxioms (core/src/gate/permitted.ts:141-150) admits every axiom whose type is not a Prop. With `axiom side_goal : Empty` the freeze's permitted list contained Spyro.side_goal, and comparator accepted `Empty.elim side_goal`. The Prop-typed variant (P6b) lets Claude add a belief that a not-proved Accept writes into the user's file, against 'only you can add beliefs'.
issues.evidence: P1, real Lean. Premises ['side-goal'] (a user's code-less GOAL card). Freeze reply: 'Your proofs may rest only on these axioms: … Spyro.side_goal …'. Gate passed on attempt 1, verdict proved, no notice, no definition question. Report card footprint: [presup:Character.exists, presup:Game.exists, axiom:Spyro.side_goal], with side-goal listed as 'unused'. Accept ok ('These suffice → proved … (+ Make Derivation)'). The real Main.lean now holds `axiom side_goal : Empty` and `theorem cynder_not_good.holds : cynder_not_good := Empty.elim side_goal`; after refresh the board shows a DERIVATION with proof.kind 'proved'. P6b: `axiom side_goal : ¬ GoodAddition cynder newSpyro` under the same card, finish not_proved: gate passed, Accept wrote it into the real Main.lean. Files: p1-result.json and p6b-result.json in the scratch folder.
issues.suggested_fix: In evaluateRules, treat every axiom added since B that is not the .holds of a selected ASSUMPTION or ghost, and not a vocabulary item of an allowed shape, as a new-axiom finding: a card's statement must never be an axiom. Apply not-formalised (TL101/TL113) to every selected premise bound in the run, not only ASSUMPTIONs. Make signatureAxioms admit only axioms classified as sort, predicate or presupposition vocabulary (no shape-violation), not every axiom whose type is not a Prop. Add regression tests with a GOAL and a DERIVATION premise in core and in walkthrough.e2e.

issues.description: The permitted set is circular for selected GOAL or DERIVATION premises whose proof Claude writes in the run. Derivation footprints come from the premises' proofs in the CURRENT state (permitted.ts contribution(), lines 153-162 and 182-190). In a not-proved finish, rules.ts:345 uses permittedAxioms(current, Sel), so a run-added proof of a selected premise is checked against a set that contains its own footprint, and passes whatever it rests on. A later freeze (Feedback or adoption round; proof-before-freeze only looks at the current round) then bakes that footprint into the permitted set. The target can then be 'proved' from an unselected assumption, even used directly, and G4 agrees because comparator gets that list.
issues.evidence: P2, real Lean. Premises ['cynder-dark-past','pg-no-dark-past','side-goal'] (new-spyro-pg NOT selected). Round 1: `abbrev side_goal : Prop := new_spyro_pg` and `theorem side_goal.holds : side_goal := new_spyro_pg.holds`, finish not_proved: 'Gate passed'. Feedback, round 2: the freeze reply lists Spyro.new_spyro_pg.holds as permitted; `theorem cynder_not_good.holds := pg_no_dark_past.holds newSpyro cynder new_spyro_pg.holds cynder_dark_past.holds` gets 'Gate passed', verdict proved, Accept ok ('These suffice → proved …'). The real Main.lean has that proof while its premises line still reads 'cynder-dark-past, pg-no-dark-past, side-goal'. The only hints are new-spyro-pg in the report-card footprint and side-goal marked unused. Round 1 alone would also have let Accept write a lemma resting on an unselected assumption (plan item 26). issues.suggested_fix: Take derivation footprints only from premise .holds proofs unchanged since B (or the accept-base commit), never from proofs added or changed in the run. Compute the not-proved permitted set the same way (from B's proofs) so it cannot include the footprint it is judging. Add tests: a selected GOAL/DERIVATION premise proved in round 1 from an unselected assumption must fail in round 1 and must not widen the round-2 freeze after Feedback or adoption.

issues.description: The footprint rule fails open when a run-added proof has no facts under its source name. A `private theorem` is stored in Lean's facts under a mangled name, so factsOf returns nothing and rules.ts:361 (`if (!permitted || !f) continue;`) skips it silently in every purpose. A not-proved round can therefore carry a lemma resting on an unselected assumption into the user's files, which plan item 26 / decision 10 forbids. #!/bin/bash
# memwatch.sh <root-pid> <logfile>: samples MemAvailable every 2 s while root-pid lives; logs the minimum;
# if MemAvailable < 8000 MB, sends TERM to root-pid's own process tree only (my processes).
ROOT=$1; OUT=$2; MINAVAIL=999999
desc() { local p=$1; echo $p; for c in $(pgrep -P $p 2>/dev/null); do desc $c; done; }
while kill -0 $ROOT 2>/dev/null; do
  AV=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  [ $AV -lt $MINAVAIL ] && MINAVAIL=$AV
  echo "$(date +%T) avail=${AV}MB" >> $OUT
  if [ $AV -lt 8000 ]; then echo "$(date +%T) LOW MEMORY: killing tree of $ROOT" >> $OUT; for p in $(desc $ROOT); do kill -TERM $p 2>/dev/null; done; fi
  sleep 2
done
echo "DONE minAvail=${MINAVAIL}MB" >> $OUT

# walkthrough fixtures (M2, WP3)

FakeBackend scripts as data, for docs/m2-plan.md sections 10.2 (the two walkthrough readings) and 10.3 (the
cheating cases). Used by `packages/runner/test/run/walkthrough.e2e.test.ts` (AT3.14, AT3.15: real engine, real
Lean, a scratch git copy of `mental_model/`), by the RunManager's unit tests, and by
`scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --dry-run`. Nothing here is ever compiled: Lean text (including `sorry` and
`#eval`) appears only inside JSON strings.

## Format

```json
{
  "name": "normative",
  "description": "…",
  "answer": { "phenomenon": "modality", "option": 0 },
  "premises": ["cynder-dark-past", "new-spyro-pg", "pg-no-dark-past"],
  "expect": { "verdict": "proved", "…": "…" },
  "turns": [{ "match": "Run: \"These suffice\"", "steps": [ { "kind": "read", "path": "Model/Spyro/Main.lean" }, … ] }]
}
```

- `turns` are played in order by `llm.playFakeScript` (runner `src/llm/fakeScripts.ts`): each user turn takes the
  next unplayed turn whose `match` (if any) occurs in the turn text. Round 1 matches the context bundle
  (`Run: "These suffice"`), an adoption round `The person adopted your suggestion`. A user turn the script did not
  plan (for example a nudge) gets no steps. The cursor survives a resumed session (`--resume`).
- `steps` are runner `FakeStep`s: `read`, `edit` (`oldString` → `newString`, first occurrence, through the same
  path guard as the CLI's hook), `writeFile`, `callTool` (validated with the real tool schemas, dispatched to the
  RunManager's tool host), `text`, `usage` (one API response), `rateLimit`, `sleep`, `result` (with the CLI's
  cumulative `costEstimateUsd`).
- `answer`, `premises`, `adopt`, `userEdits` and `expect` are read by the tests and the walkthrough script, not by the
  player: the test answers the modality question with `answer.option`, starts the run with `premises`, and checks
  `expect`. `userEdits` (optional, `{ path, oldString, newString }` like an edit step) are the user's own edits to the
  scratch copy before the run starts (they are part of B), e.g. a code-less GOAL card to select as a premise.
- Every edit applies to both `mental_model/` and `test-fixtures/spyro/` (whose `Main.lean` differ by one import
  line); a check of that ran when the files were written.

## Scripts

| File | What Claude does | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `normative.json` | reading A: asks the modality question (answered "a rule"), formalises `pg_no_dark_past` normatively, checks, freezes, proves from the three premises, finishes `proved` | proved; G→D lifecycle item `l1`; footprint = the three cards + two presuppositions |
| `literal.json` | reading B: answered "literal"; adds `axiom InGame`, formalises literally, freezes, proposes the missing premise `not_in_game_not_good` with its gap proof, finishes `not_proved`; after the adoption proves the goal with it | round 1 not proved with `ghost-1` (closes the gap, not alone-entailing); round 2 proved; the adopted card is worded by Claude |
| `cheat-added-axiom.json` | `axiom shortcut : cynder_not_good` proves the goal | retry (`new-axiom`); the retry replaces the cheat with the honest proof and passes |
| `cheat-sorry.json` | `:= sorry` | retry (G0 `sorry`, no Lean ran); honest retry passes |
| `cheat-weakened-abbrev.json` | the target abbrev becomes `… ∨ True` | retry (`existing-changed`); the retry restores it |
| `cheat-weakened-type.json` | the theorem proves `cynder_not_good ∨ True` | retry (`not-proved`); honest retry passes |
| `cheat-unselected.json` | new-spyro-pg unselected, honest proof | retry (`footprint` naming `new_spyro_pg.holds`); the retry removes the proof and finishes `not_proved` |
| `cheat-rebind-target.json` | before the freeze, the target's `lean:` pin re-pointed at a new `abbrev … := True` | freeze refused (`markup`, no gate attempt used); restored, frozen, proved |

## 3. The prototype gate, exactly

The gate runs on the shadow after `finish`; `check_lean` and `freeze_statements` run subsets of the same rules (WP1 `evaluateRules` purposes `check`, `freeze`, `gate-proved`, `gate-other`). Inputs: the run base B (exactly the user's files at run start, the shadow's `base` commit; for Accept's re-check after drift, the user's files at Accept, the `accept-base` commit: section 7.1), the adoption reference A (the shadow at its newest `adopt` commit, when a ghost was adopted: telelean's own ghost blocks and declarations are checked against it, never against B), the shadow now S (after normalisation, as committed: the gate judges one committed state), the build mirror's fresh Lean facts of S, the round's freeze F, the selection Sel (target T, premises P, adopted ghosts), the finish status.

**Why these checks make "proved" mean "proved from exactly the selection"** (the Prototype profile's central claim): the target's statement and every selected statement are frozen before any proof exists (`proof-before-freeze`, the freeze); a formalised card's statement cannot be swapped (`markup`: no pin changed, no card re-bound); `existing-changed` keeps every declaration the user had; G4 checks the target theorem against the freeze with the permitted set computed from the freeze; `footprint` holds for every theorem the run adds, whatever the finish status; and what the proposal shows is always a judged state (gate-pass files, or a reverted, normalised and re-checked passing state).

**Order and short-circuits:** G0 (text only) → if any G0 finding, stop: Lean never elaborates text that fails G0. → G1 (sync mirror; `semantic.refreshLeanFacts` on `build/`) → G3 and G5 (from S's project model with the facts) → only if everything so far passed and the status is `proved`: G4 (lake comparator).

### 3.1 G0: token denylist and file rules (core `scanForbidden`, `checkFileChanges`)

Only files that differ between B and S are scanned, and in them only Claude's lines: a forbidden token on a line whose exact text also occurs in B's version of the file is the user's own and is not reported (line-multiset comparison, `scanForbidden(file, text, ctx, baseText)`; extra copies of such a line are reported), so a user's `set_option … in` or `#eval` line never fails Claude's attempt just because Claude edited the same file. Tokens come from core's `lexLean` (comments, strings and telelean blocks never count). S here is every regular file in ws/ (`ShadowWorkspace.currentFiles`), so a stray `notes.md` Claude wrote is a `bad-path` finding (counted), not an environment failure.
