### 10.6 The checks, the notices and the retry loop

Claude must first **freeze** the statements: the target's Lean statement and those of the selected premises. Proofs are refused before the freeze. When Claude says it is finished, telelean checks the result without Claude:

- only allowed Lean in what Claude wrote: no `sorry`, no `#eval` or other commands except `#check`/`#print`, no `set_option`, no metaprogramming, no imports from outside the project, no changes to the project files;
- the files build (each Lean job has a time and memory limit);
- the proof rests only on the selected premises, Lean's standard axioms, the vocabulary and the existence presuppositions of what the statements mention ("there is at least one character"): the **permitted set**, listed in the report; every lemma Claude adds is held to the same rule, also when it says "not proved";
- the frozen statements are unchanged (Lean's comparator), your words and blocks are unchanged, declarations that existed before the run are unchanged, and the only new axioms are the `.holds` of selected assumptions Claude formalised and vocabulary of its own (an axiom written directly below a card's block would be that card's statement: it is refused, whatever its type);
- a card Claude formalises gets a real statement (`abbrev … : Prop := …`), whatever its kind; a selected Goal or Derivation that Claude proves in the run is a lemma like any other: its proof must rest on the selected premises too, and it never widens the permitted set (only proofs you already had count as yours);
- Lean must report on every declaration Claude adds: one it cannot see (a `private` declaration) is refused, since nothing could be checked about it;
- new vocabulary has the simple shape (sorts, predicates, constants, functions).

New **definitions** Claude introduces are never accepted silently: they become definition questions in the review. A premise Claude thinks is **missing** becomes a suggestion (10.9), never part of your files. Neither is a failure.

If the check fails, a notice says why, for example *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it added an axiom (`shortcut`), and only you can add beliefs. Asking Claude to retry."*, and Claude gets the exact failure and tries again. After the last allowed attempt (`telelean.run.maxGateAttempts`, 3 per round) telelean stops it and tells you, for example *"Claude's attempts didn't pass the checks 3 times: … telelean reverted its working copy to “Statements frozen (round 1)”."*: the proposal then shows the last state that passed (often the formalisation without a proof), which you can still accept, answer with Feedback, or discard.

More rules of the loop: edits Claude makes after its check passed are discarded (the proposal is always exactly the checked files); a turn that ends without finishing gets one reminder, then the round ends the same way as after the last attempt; reaching a cap (10.12) does too. Problems of the machine (the sandbox could not start, low memory) are not Claude's fault and are not counted: telelean tries the check once more after 30 seconds, and if it fails again the run ends as failed with the reason.

### 10.7 The proposal on the board

When a round ends, the banner reads "Claude's proposal: 1 new · 2 changed · +1 vocabulary" with **Current | Proposed**, **Review…**, **Accept**, **Feedback**, **Discard** and **Raw Lean diff…**. The board switches to **Proposed**: the subject as it would be after Accept, with diff marks on the cards ("+new", "~changed", "−removed": a glyph, a word, a colour and a halo; hover for what changed), and the vocabulary group opened with "+N new". The proposed view is read-only; **Current** shows your files as they are.

### 10.14 Limits of M2

- One run per model folder at a time; targets are Goals and Derivations of the board's subject.
- Accept takes the whole proposal (no partial Accept); a definition is endorsed only by its "Yes" before Accept.
- No consistency check of your assumptions yet ("consistency unchecked", M3); no countermodels; the review is minimal (no back-translation or alignment check).
- Recorded answers cannot be revoked yet (M3); "Decide for me" lets Claude choose and say so.
- Lean 4 core only (no Mathlib, M4). The checks are a prototype profile for your own use, not hardened against a determined adversary (later: H).
- A run needs Claude Code logged in with a claude.ai subscription; runs use your plan's usage.

### 10.15 Troubleshooting runs

- **"Not started: telelean sends nothing to Claude until you allow it"**: you pressed Cancel in the consent question; press These suffice again and choose **Run with Claude**.
- **"Claude could not be started: …"**: the message lists the places telelean looked for Claude Code, or says the version is too old or that Claude Code is not logged in with a claude.ai subscription. Install or update the Claude Code extension, or set `telelean.claude.path`, then reload.
- **"The run could not start: your files have Lean errors (…)"**: fix or save the files the message names (Problems on the board lists them), then start again.
- **"Claude is already working on …" / "…waiting for your review"**: one run per model folder; finish, cancel or discard the other one first (its badge is in the header).
- **"telelean could not run the checks (…); this is not Claude's fault"**: the sandbox or the memory guard stopped a Lean job twice; free memory or fix the sandbox, then start a new run.
- **Accept refused**: either your edits overlap Claude's (Discard, or Feedback to redo it on your current files) or Claude's changes no longer pass the checks on top of your current files (the message lists the findings).
- **To free disk space**: lower `telelean.run.keepRuns`, or delete old run folders under `~/.config/Code/User/globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs/` while no run is active.

  sleep 2
done
echo "DONE minAvail=${MINAVAIL}MB" >> $OUT
EOF

input.summary:
I fixed all three issues. Every check I ran passed.

**Major: proofs carried by declarations that are not theorems.** The rules are in `/home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/core/src/gate/rules.ts`.

**Footprint.** The `footprint` rule now judges every declaration added or changed in the run, of any kind or type: def, abbrev, instance, opaque, structure, class and inductive. Axioms stay with `new-axiom`.
- Names that only Lean reports are judged too, such as a `where` declaration or a structure's field. They count as new when the declaration containing them is added or changed. When the reference has no Lean facts (a round start or Accept's base), the name counts as new only if its source text is new.
- A structure or class also answers for what the constants written in its source rest on. Checked on the pinned Lean 4.35: a field's default value lives in a hidden `S.f._default` definition. Neither `#print axioms S` nor the `.ilean` index lists it, but the index does record that the structure mentions `.holds`.
- A proof is held to the permitted set. Any other declaration is held to the permitted set plus the existence presuppositions. Without that, every new constant `noncomputable opaque c : T` would fail, since it rests on `T.exists` by design.
- The "Lean reported nothing about it" refusal now covers every kind of declaration, a `private structure` included.
- Claude gets a dedicated message for a non-theorem ("… is not a theorem but carries a proof resting on …").

**Before the freeze.** A declaration that is not a proof but rests on more than Lean's standard axioms, the vocabulary and the presuppositions now counts as a proof written before the freeze (finding token `carrier`, with its own board sentence). This also applies when it rests on a selected premise, since D-19 forbids every proof before the freeze. The presupposition-instance pattern can no longer hide such a proof either.

**Tests.**
- New core test `/home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/core/test/gate/carriers.test.ts` (9 tests). It covers the PLift def, the Inhabited instance, a structure default and a `where` declaration, in not-proved and proved rounds, plus controls that must pass.
- Two new end-to-end cheat scripts, `cheat-carrier-not-proved` and `cheat-carrier-proved`, run with real Lean. In both, the first finish fails with `footprint` for each of the three carriers and the retry passes. In the not-proved one, `check_lean` and the freeze also refuse the carriers first. After Accept, the user's file contains none of them.
- Run against the old rules, 6 of the 8 core tests in the file at that time and both end-to-end cheat tests fail. Against the new rules they pass.

**Minor: walkthrough script tripwire.** `/home/zhengyew/telelean/scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs` now refuses `--live` at once for any value that arms the quota tripwire (`true` too), not only `1`. It uses the runner's own rule, kept in a new import-free helper `/home/zhengyew/telelean/scripts/quota-tripwire.mjs` so the script can decide before it bundles anything. A new runner test (`quotaTripwire.test.ts`) checks the helper against `realClaudeDisabled()` for 16 spellings without running the script. I also added the suggested `true` case to `walkthroughScript.test.ts`, but did not run it (see test runs).

**Minor: docs.**
- `docs/m2-plan.md`:
  - section 14 now logs the webview fixer's two conventions (the `Not started:` prefix shown as an info toast, and the persisted `runSplit` key) and my round-2 changes;

minor_decisions.decision: Anything that is not a proof may also rest on the vocabulary's existence presuppositions (`T.exists`); proofs stay held to the permitted set exactly.
minor_decisions.rationale: A constant `noncomputable opaque c : T` and a presupposition instance rest on `T.exists` by design (D-3). Judging them strictly would fail every new constant of a sort the selected statements do not mention. A presupposition only says a sort is non-empty, and any proof using such a constant is still judged strictly.

minor_decisions.decision: The source-references extension (also judging what the constants a declaration mentions rest on) applies to structures and classes only.
minor_decisions.rationale: Checked with the pinned Lean 4.35. Structure and class field defaults live in `S.f._default`, which neither `#print axioms S` nor `.ilean` lists, while `.ilean` attributes the usage to S. An inductive's constructor defaults are `optParam`s that `#print axioms` already follows. Using references for theorems would flag lemmas a proof mentions but never uses (e.g. in `simp [x]`).

minor_decisions.decision: Names only Lean reports count as added when their containing declaration (found by range) is added or changed. Without one, the name must be new to the reference; if the reference has no facts (round start, Accept base), its source text must also be new.
minor_decisions.rationale: The engine builds the round-start model from text only, so `known` lacks such names. Without the text check, the user's own declarations could be flagged as carriers in a Feedback round.

minor_decisions.rationale: D-19 forbids every proof before the freeze. This criterion leaves vocabulary, definitions, presupposition instances and Lean's generated structure-field projections (theorems over vocabulary only) alone.

#!/bin/bash
# RAM watchdog (turn 2). Warn < 12 GB available, critical < 4 GB.
# On critical, kills ONLY processes started for this work: telelean-* systemd scopes,
# VS Code *test* instances (.vscode-test), and anything whose cwd is in my scratchpad.
SCR=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad
state=ok
while true; do
  avail=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  if [ "$avail" -lt 4096 ]; then
    if [ "$state" != crit ]; then
      echo "CRITICAL: MemAvailable ${avail} MB — killing my own test/build processes"
      systemctl --user kill 'telelean-*' 2>/dev/null
      pkill -f '\.vscode-test/' 2>/dev/null
      for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do c=$(readlink "$p/cwd" 2>/dev/null); case "$c" in "$SCR"*) kill "${p#/proc/}" 2>/dev/null;; esac; done
      state=crit
    fi
  elif [ "$avail" -lt 12288 ]; then
    [ "$state" = ok ] && echo "WARN: MemAvailable ${avail} MB"
    state=warn
  else
    [ "$state" != ok ] && echo "RECOVERED: MemAvailable ${avail} MB"
    state=ok
  fi
  sleep 5
done

setsid sh -c 'ulimit -c 0; exec node scripts/smoke.mjs' > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
echo "smoke pid/pgid $PID" >> "$LOG.watch"
while kill -0 $PID 2>/dev/null; do
  avail=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)

  if [ "$avail" -lt 4096 ]; then
    echo "CRITICAL ${avail} MB: killing this smoke run's process group" >> "$LOG.watch"
    kill -TERM -$PID 2>/dev/null; sleep 5; kill -KILL -$PID 2>/dev/null
  fi
  sleep 10
done
wait $PID
echo "EXIT $?" >> "$LOG.watch"
EOF

input.summary:
I fixed all six UX issues (one major, five minor) in packages/webview, with small changes in packages/extension. All affected suites pass on the final build: webview 127/127 unit and 78/78 browser tests, extension 166/166 unit tests, and the full VS Code smoke (36 + 20 passing, 0 isolation failures).

Major issue, narrow board during a run:
- While a run is active, the selection tray folds to one line: the selection summed up ("3 premises ⊢ “…”"), Clear, the disabled button and the reason. A chevron unfolds it for that run.
- While the run panel is shown, the A|D|G box hides its optional second row until it has the focus or some content. The box still works.
- Below the board, the panel now sizes to its content up to 60% (was 48%).
- The panel's edge towards the board is a resize handle. It works by dragging, by arrow keys or Home/End, and double-click or Enter restores the default. The size is kept per layout in the webview state.
- A new question set or review, and every review step change, now scrolls into view inside the panel only.
- Tested at 790×795 (the first question's options are all visible, the board is over 250 px high) and at 545 px wide (the raw-diff-beside case: the statement and its Lean are visible).
- I did not change where the raw diff opens. It still follows the M1 rule in groups.ts: use an existing other editor group, and split only when the board's group is the only one. The half-width board is now usable. Whether to change that rule is listed in open issues.

Minor issues:
- **Diff mark:** the "~changed" / "+new" badge now sits on its own line above the sentence, so the sentence keeps the card's width.
- **Statement step:** the Lean shows only the proposition. A new helper drops Lean's `#print` header and leaves any other text as it is. The sentence now sits above the Lean, and the Lean name in the heading is no longer upper-cased.
- **Gave-up rounds:** this applies to rounds that gave up, hit a limit, or ended without finishing. The header badge says "Claude: gave up · Spyro" and the state line "Ready for review · Claude gave up". The proposal banner adds a line saying what happened and that the proposal holds only the last passing state, and Accept is no longer the primary button. The gave-up and revert notices now come before the review. Notices from earlier attempts are folded below it under "Earlier notices (n)". While Claude is still working, every notice shows as before. Proof results are still hidden until the statements are reviewed.
- **Wording:**
  - "check attempts" replaces "gate attempts" everywhere.
  - Each failed check shows a plain-words label ("what it rests on"), with "Check G3: …" in the tooltip.
  - With a Derivation selected, the tray now says "Choose the target (a Goal or a Derivation) with ⊢."
  - Declining consent shows an info toast, cleared by the next start.
  - A small extra fix: the other-subject run line no longer lower-cases "Claude".

I updated one VS Code test in the extension: the cheating test now unfolds "Earlier notices" before it checks the failed-attempt notice.

minor_decisions.decision: Rebuilt only the webview (vite, into packages/extension/dist/webview) and the extension (esbuild), not root `npm run build`.
minor_decisions.rationale: Root build also runs tsc for core and runner, which writes their dist folders outside my assigned paths. The extension bundle and tests read core and runner sources directly through tsconfig paths, so the two builds I ran are all the extension needs.

minor_decisions.decision: The tray folds and the A|D|G box hides its optional row in the wide layout too, not only below 1000 px.
minor_decisions.rationale: The run buttons are disabled during any run, so the folded tray loses nothing. The same behaviour in both layouts is easier to predict, and vertical room matters in both. The chevron and the focus bring the full forms back.

minor_decisions.decision: Default panel height below the board: sized to its content, at most 60%. Once the user drags, an explicit share is kept with px limits.
minor_decisions.rationale: A fixed split wastes room when the panel has little to show, such as while starting or working. 60% leaves the board over 250 px on the reported 790x795 board. The handle lets the user change the balance.

minor_decisions.decision: The split is stored as a fraction of the workspace per layout in the webview state (runSplit) and applied through the CSSOM (a custom property), with the same px limits repeated in CSS.
minor_decisions.rationale: Fractions follow window resizes. The CSP forbids style attributes but allows CSSOM. Keeping the limits in CSS too keeps a stored value sensible after a resize.

minor_decisions.decision: Which notices go before the review: only the latest gave-up/cap and revert notices for an outcome verdict. Everything else folds below the review once a round has ended. While working, all notices show first as before.
minor_decisions.rationale: Notices carry no round number, so showing all warning-level notices first would put a round-1 give-up above a later round-2 proof. The latest outcome notices are what explain the current proposal.

minor_decisions.decision: Declined consent is recognised by the 'Not started:' prefix of the host's text, pinned by an extension unit test, instead of changing the outcome shape.
minor_decisions.rationale: The code 'not-yet' also covers real preflight failures. Changing the actionResult to ok:true would break existing extension tests and the API callers. Both sides of the convention are in my packages.

minor_decisions.decision: The failed check's step is shown as a plain-words chip with the step name in the tooltip, rather than dropping it.
minor_decisions.rationale: Plain words help scanning ('build' versus 'what it rests on') without jargon. The tooltip keeps the precise step name for the curious.

minor_decisions.decision: From the middle of the task on, I ran node_modules/.bin binaries directly and set npm_config_logs_dir to my scratch dir for the VS Code smoke runs.
minor_decisions.rationale: npm and npx write and prune debug logs in ~/.npm/_logs by default. I noticed this partway through and stopped adding logs there.

effects_outside_repo: ~/.npm/_logs: my npm and npx calls between about 23:24 and 23:44 (+08:00) each wrote one debug log there (npm's default; about 11 files, roughly 1 KB each, containing command lines and paths, no secrets): npm run typecheck/build, npx vitest, npx playwright, the extension typecheck/vitest/build, and 'npm config get' twice. npm keeps only 10 logs, so these runs also deleted older log files there, which may have belonged to other sessions. Logs dated after 23:44 come from other processes; my later commands used node_modules/.bin directly or npm_config_logs_dir in my scratch dir. I did not set npm_config_logs_max.

The leftover /tmp/playwright-artifacts-O6yYln dated 15:19 is not mine.

1	# telelean: user guide (M1 board, M2 Claude runs)
2	
3	M1 is "the map without AI": a board of your ASSUMPTION / DERIVATION / GOAL cards, read from and written to Lean files, checked by Lean, with undo and git history. M2 adds one-shot **"These suffice"**: you select premises and a target, Claude formalises and proves in a private copy of your model, telelean checks the result with Lean and a fixed set of rules, and nothing reaches your files until you review the proposal and press **Accept** (section 10). Nothing calls Claude until you press "These suffice" and allow it.
4	
5	## 1. Start
6	
7	1. **Load the new build.** You installed the extension in M0 with **Developer: Install Extension from Location…** (`/home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/extension`). That registration points at the folder, so the rebuilt `dist/` is used after **Developer: Reload Window**. Nothing to reinstall.
8	2. **Open a folder that holds a model**, for example `/home/zhengyew/telelean` (it contains the sample `mental_model/`) or `mental_model/` itself. telelean starts by itself only in windows that contain a model (a `.telelean/config.json`); its commands work in any window. Untrusted and virtual workspaces are not supported.
9	3. **Run `telelean: Open Board`** (Command Palette). With several models in the window it asks which one; with none it offers Initialize.
10	
11	The sample `mental_model/` is your Spyro walkthrough as subject `Spyro`: three assumptions ("PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts" is comment-only with stance *rule*; "Cynder is a character who has a dark past" and "The new Spyro game is PG" are formalised) and one formalised, unproved goal ("Cynder would not be a good addition to the new Spyro game").
12	
13	Opening the board builds the model with Lean in place: `mental_model/.lake/` and `.telelean/graph.json` appear (both gitignored).
14	
15	## 2. Make a new model: `telelean: Initialize Model Here`
16	
17	Run it from the Command Palette, or right-click a folder in the Explorer.
18	
19	- **Empty folder:** it asks for the first subject's name (a Lean namespace such as `Spyro`; the default comes from the folder name) and writes the Lake project (`lakefile.toml` with `autoImplicit = false`, toolchain `v4.35.0`), `Model.lean`, `Model/<Subject>.lean`, `Model/<Subject>/{Vocabulary,Inbox,Main}.lean`, `.telelean/` and `.gitignore`.
20	- **Existing Lake project without dependencies:** it asks first, then only adds `.telelean/` and the missing `.gitignore` lines. Your Lean files are not changed.
21	- **Refused:** projects with Lake dependencies (Mathlib: M4), `lakefile.lean`-only projects (convert with `lake translate-config toml`), folders with other files but no lakefile.
22	- Then, if the folder is not inside a git repository, it offers `git init` for history (say no and history stays off; you can still accept later from the board).

26	
27	From top to bottom: the header (subject picker, History, Undo/Redo, Lean badge, Problems, legend), three columns (Assumptions, Derivations, Goals; each scrolls on its own), the selection tray, and the A|D|G box. The **Vocabulary group** is the first item of the Assumptions column, collapsed by default (click its heading to open it). **Problems** in the header lists the diagnostics of this subject. Saving or cancelling an in-place edit gives the focus back to the card.

The user's files change only on Accept. Files were byte-identical before Accept in every run, and also after cancel, Discard, give-up, Stop, reload/resume, declined consent, a failed start and a refused Accept. Each Accept is one history entry ("accept · These suffice → proved: … (+ Make Derivation)" / "(+ 1 adopted assumption)") and Undo restores it byte-exactly; after a merged Accept, Undo returns to the user's own edit.

Consent works as documented. The real modal (Development mode) shows exactly the guide's text; Cancel is not remembered and a yes is. The quota tripwire also holds outside Test mode: "Claude could not be started: real Claude is disabled here (TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1): no Claude binary was looked up or run."

Questions follow D-20. Phenomenon tags, options with consequences, own words, Leave it open, Decide for me, and scope radios ("these cards" disabled when a question names no card) are all there. Send stays disabled until every question has an answer. The give-up and revert notices and the report's "reverted to Statements frozen (round 1)" are shown. Feedback, by button or Ctrl+Enter, continues the same session in round 2 with a fresh freeze.

#!/bin/bash
# memwatch.sh <root-pid> <logfile>: samples MemAvailable every 2 s while root-pid lives; logs the minimum;
# if MemAvailable < 8000 MB, sends TERM to root-pid's own process tree only (my processes).
ROOT=$1; OUT=$2; MINAVAIL=999999
desc() { local p=$1; echo $p; for c in $(pgrep -P $p 2>/dev/null); do desc $c; done; }
while kill -0 $ROOT 2>/dev/null; do
  AV=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  [ $AV -lt $MINAVAIL ] && MINAVAIL=$AV
  echo "$(date +%T) avail=${AV}MB" >> $OUT
  if [ $AV -lt 8000 ]; then echo "$(date +%T) LOW MEMORY: killing tree of $ROOT" >> $OUT; for p in $(desc $ROOT); do kill -TERM $p 2>/dev/null; done; fi
  sleep 2
done
echo "DONE minAvail=${MINAVAIL}MB" >> $OUT

#!/bin/bash
# claudewatch.sh <logfile> <stopfile>: every 0.1 s, records any NEW process running the real Claude Code binary
# (path under ~/.vscode/extensions/.../native-binary/claude or a 'claude' on the real PATH), with its parent chain.
OUT=$1; STOP=$2
base=$(pgrep -f '/home/zhengyew/.vscode/extensions/[^ ]*native-binary/claude' | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
echo "$(date +%T.%N) baseline: $base" >> $OUT
seen=" $base "
while [ ! -f "$STOP" ]; do
  for p in $(pgrep -f '/home/zhengyew/.vscode/extensions/[^ ]*native-binary/claude'); do
    case "$seen" in *" $p "*) continue;; esac
    seen="$seen$p "
    pp=$(awk '{print $4}' /proc/$p/stat 2>/dev/null)
    echo "$(date +%T.%N) NEW pid=$p ppid=$pp cmd=$(tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$p/cmdline 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-200) parent=$(tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$pp/cmdline 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-200)" >> $OUT
  done
  sleep 0.1
done
echo "$(date +%T.%N) stopped" >> $OUT

## 3. The prototype gate, exactly

The gate runs on the shadow after `finish`; `check_lean` and `freeze_statements` run subsets of the same rules (WP1 `evaluateRules` purposes `check`, `freeze`, `gate-proved`, `gate-other`). Inputs: the run base B (exactly the user's files at run start, the shadow's `base` commit; for Accept's re-check after drift, the user's files at Accept, the `accept-base` commit: section 7.1), the adoption reference A (the shadow at its newest `adopt` commit, when a ghost was adopted: telelean's own ghost blocks and declarations are checked against it, never against B), the shadow now S (after normalisation, as committed: the gate judges one committed state), the build mirror's fresh Lean facts of S, the round's freeze F, the selection Sel (target T, premises P, adopted ghosts), the finish status.

**Why these checks make "proved" mean "proved from exactly the selection"** (the Prototype profile's central claim): the target's statement and every selected statement are frozen before any proof exists (`proof-before-freeze`, the freeze); a formalised card's statement cannot be swapped (`markup`: no pin changed, no card re-bound); `existing-changed` keeps every declaration the user had; G4 checks the target theorem against the freeze with the permitted set computed from the freeze; `footprint` holds for every theorem the run adds (fixer round 2: for every declaration it adds, whatever its kind or type, since a definition, instance or structure can carry a proof too), whatever the finish status; and what the proposal shows is always a judged state (gate-pass files, or a reverted, normalised and re-checked passing state).

**Order and short-circuits:** G0 (text only) → if any G0 finding, stop: Lean never elaborates text that fails G0. → G1 (sync mirror; `semantic.refreshLeanFacts` on `build/`) → G3 and G5 (from S's project model with the facts) → only if everything so far passed and the status is `proved`: G4 (lake comparator).

### 3.1 G0: token denylist and file rules (core `scanForbidden`, `checkFileChanges`)

Only files that differ between B and S are scanned, and in them only Claude's lines: a forbidden token on a line whose exact text also occurs in B's version of the file is the user's own and is not reported (line-multiset comparison, `scanForbidden(file, text, ctx, baseText)`; extra copies of such a line are reported), so a user's `set_option … in` or `#eval` line never fails Claude's attempt just because Claude edited the same file. Tokens come from core's `lexLean` (comments, strings and telelean blocks never count). S here is every regular file in ws/ (`ShadowWorkspace.currentFiles`), so a stray `notes.md` Claude wrote is a `bad-path` finding (counted), not an environment failure.

| Code | Forbidden (code tokens) |
|---|---|
| `hash-command` | `#` immediately followed by an identifier other than `check` and `print` (`#eval`, `#exit`, `#reduce`, `#synth`, …) |
| `metaprogramming` | `initialize`, `builtin_initialize`, `run_cmd`, `run_elab`, `run_meta`, `macro`, `macro_rules`, `syntax`, `notation`, `infix`, `infixl`, `infixr`, `prefix`, `postfix`, `elab`, `elab_rules`, `declare_syntax_cat`, `declare_simp_like_tactic` |
| `native-code` | `native_decide`, `bv_decide`, `implemented_by`, `extern`, `csimp`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`, `reduceBool`, `reduceNat`; `native` preceded by `+` (`decide +native`) |
| `unsafe` | `unsafe`, `partial` |
| `set-option` | `set_option` (every option: limits such as `maxHeartbeats`, `maxRecDepth`, `synthInstance.*`, `debug.*`, `autoImplicit`, …) |
| `sorry` | `sorry`, `admit` |
| `import` | an `import` whose module is not in `G0Context.projectModules` (the library's modules in S) |
| `project-file` | `lakefile.toml`, `lakefile.lean`, `lean-toolchain` or `lake-manifest.json` differs from B |
| `outside-subject` | a changed, added or deleted file outside `<library>/<S>/**` and `<library>/<S>.lean` |
| `deleted-file` | a model file of B missing from S |
| `bad-path` | an added path that is not `<library>/<S>/<Module>.lean` with valid module components; anything that is not a regular file (the shadow refuses it first) |

### 3.2 The permitted set (core `computePermittedAxioms`, from the frozen model)

Computed at every freeze from the project model of S **as frozen** (its facts), passed to comparator as `permitted_axioms`, shown to the agent in the freeze reply and on the report card:

```
permitted(F) = STD                       = { propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound }
             ∪ signature                 = { a | a is an axiom of the project's modules, facts.typeSort(a) ≠ "Prop",
                                                 a is vocabulary of kind sort/predicate/function/constant (never a declaration
                                                 bound to a card, never vocabulary of kind `other`) }
                                           (sorts `axiom T : Type`, predicates `… → Prop`, function and constant axioms)
             ∪ selected                  = { n.holds | n ∈ P ∪ ghosts, n.holds is an axiom }
             ∪ presuppositions           = { p ∈ lean.presupposes(x) | x ∈ {T} ∪ P ∪ ghosts }   (D-3b; via #print axioms of the statements)
             ∪ derivation footprints     = ⋃ { axioms(d.holds) \ {sorryAx} | d ∈ P, d.holds is a theorem, d proved (not conditional), T.holds ∉ axioms(d.holds),
                                                 d.holds is the user's own: the same statement and source text in B }
unusable     = { p ∈ P | p has no .holds (code-less, an unproved goal or derivation), a conditional one, one resting on T's own claimed .holds (circular),
                         or one proved only in this run }
```

Spyro, normative reading, all three selected: `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, and `Spyro.` + `Character`, `Game`, `HasDarkPast`, `IsPG`, `GoodAddition`, `cynder_dark_past.holds`, `new_spyro_pg.holds`, `pg_no_dark_past.holds`, `Character.exists`, `Game.exists`: 13 names, exactly t

454:## 28. Fixes after the M2 verification, round 2 (core, runner, scripts, docs)
455-
456-- **Every declaration Claude adds is held to the permitted set, whatever its kind or type, not only theorems; so is every name Lean reports inside one (a `where` declaration, a structure's field).** A definition, instance or structure can carry a proof without being a theorem (`def h : PLift p := ⟨p.holds⟩`, an `Inhabited (PLift p)` instance, a field whose default value is `p.holds`); such a declaration resting on an assumption you did not select passed every check and Accept wrote it into your files, after a "not proved" round and a "proved" one alike (the verifier showed it with real
457-- **A declaration that is not a proof may also rest on the vocabulary's existence presuppositions (`T.exists`), even when no selected statement mentions T; a proof may not.** A named constant (`noncomputable opaque c : T`) rests on `T.exists` by design (D-3), so without this every new constant or presupposition instance of a sort the selected statements do not mention would fail; a presupposition says only that a sort is not empty, and any proof that uses such a constant is still judged strictly. *(fix)*
458-- **A structure or class also answers for what the constants written in it rest on.** Lean keeps a field's default value in a hidden helper (`S.f._default`) that neither `#print axioms S` nor Lean's index lists, while the index does record that the structure mentions the assumption: checked on Lean 4.35 with the pinned toolchain. *(fix)*
459-- **Before the freeze, a declaration that is not a proof but rests on more than the vocabulary layer (Lean's standard axioms, the signature, the presuppositions) counts as a proof written before the freeze, also when it rests on a selected premise.** D-19 forbids every proof before the freeze, and a proof inside a definition is one; Claude learns it at its first check instead of at the end of the round. *(fix)*
460-- **The "Lean reported nothing about it" refusal covers declarations of every kind (a `private structure` too), not only theorems, definitions, instances and opaques.** Fail closed, as in section 27: a private structure with a proof in a default value was the same hole by yet another route. *(fix)*
461-- **Not changed: an `example` written after the freeze is not judged, and a field default written as a tactic (`h : p := by exact p.holds`) is not a proof.** An example has no name and nothing can use it; a tactic default is only text that runs when a structure value is built, so the proof that builds one shows the assumption in its own footprint. *(fix)*
462-- **`scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs` refuses `--live` at once under every value that arms the quota tripwire (`true` too), with the runner's own rule, shared in `scripts/quota-tripwire.mjs`.** It refused only for exactly `1`; with `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=true` a live walkthrough got past the early refusal and was stopped only later by the backend (safe, but not the "refuses at once" of plan 12.2). *(fix)*
463-- **Open question for you: where should "Raw Lean diff…" open?** Now it opens in an editor group beside the board, and when the board is the only group VS Code splits the window, so the board shrinks to half its width (the webview fixer made the half-width board usable; the final verifier's narrow-window screenshot confirms it). The alternative is to open the diff as a tab in the board's own group, over the board, so the board keeps its full width but is hidden until you switch back. Say which you prefer; the current behaviour stays until then. *(fix, for you to decide)*

## 12. The real-Claude walkthrough (main session only, after integration)

### 12.1 The script (built by WP3)

`node scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs [--dry-run] [--live] [--reading normative|literal|both] [--model claude-opus-5-5] [--effort high] [--work-dir DIR] [--max-turns 80] [--max-checks 25] [--max-agent-minutes 20] [--binary PATH] [--approve-definitions]`. It bundles the runner into the work dir, copies `mental_model/` to `<work>/model-<reading>/`, initialises git there (isolated config), runs one Lean refresh, and drives the RunManager like a user: answers a question whose phenomenon is `modality` or whose text mentions "cannot" with free text (normative: "I mean it as a rule: PG games should not include characters with dark pasts. I do not mean it is impossible for a PG game to contain one.";

### 12.2 Procedure

1. Preconditions: integration done, all suites green, `--dry-run` passes for both readings, `free -m` shows ≥ 12 GB available, no other heavy process running, and `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE` not set in the shell that runs the live command (with it set the live run refuses at once: safe, but it would look like a failure).
2. `node scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --dry-run --binary-check` → note the binary (expected: the VS Code Claude extension's `resources/native-binary/claude`, version ≥ 2.1.295, e.g. 2.1.314) and confirm the argv has no `--bare` and the environment strips `CLAUDE*`/`ANTHROPIC_*`.
3. Tell the user before spending quota: two live runs on the default model, roughly the numbers in 12.3.
4. Normative: `TELELEAN_WALKTHROUGH_LIVE=yes node scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --live --reading normative --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --work-dir <scratch>/m2-walkthrough`. Pass: subscription auth verified before the first prompt; Claude asks about the modality (or formalises the normative reading directly and lists it under assumed_without_asking); freeze; gate passes with verdict proved (gate attempts ≤ 3); lifecycle G→D offered and applied; after Accept the copy's refresh shows `cynder-not-good` proved, DERIVATION, footprint = the three premises + two presuppositions.
5. Literal: the same with `--reading literal`. Pass: round 1 verdict not-proved with at least one ghost that closes the gap; after adoption round 2 is proved; the adopted card carries `worded_by: agent`; the copy refreshes to proved.
6. If a reading fails: record everything, do not loop; at most one retry per reading, and only after reading the transcript (a different but faithful formalisation is acceptable; a cheat that the gate caught is a pass of the gate, not of the walkthrough).
7. Record, per reading: `summary.json` (verdict per round, gate attempts with failures, notices, questions asked and the answers given, ghosts, flagged definitions, the final diff of the copy, final statuses), `transcript.jsonl`, usage (requests, input / output / cache-read / cache-write tokens, the CLI's cost estimate, rate-limit events), durations (wall, agent-active), CLI and model versions, the guard log (denials, if any). Save them into the prompt log's bundle as the walkthrough report. Also report the effects outside the scratch dir: the CLI itself stores each session's transcript under `~/.claude/projects/<its encoding of the shadow's ws/ path>/<session id>.jsonl` (that is how `--resu
8. Optional, with the user: the same flow in VS Code (Extension Development Host on a copy of `mental_model/`), pressing These suffice on the board.

### 12.3 Expected cost (an estimate, not a measurement)

Per reading, about 10–20 model requests (normative) and 20–35 over two rounds (literal); each request carries the cached system prompt, tool schemas and conversation (~10–30k input tokens, mostly cache reads), so both readings together ≈ 0.5–1.5 M cache-read tokens, 50–150 k cache-write tokens, a few thousand uncached input tokens, and 20–60 k output tokens at effort high. Wall time ≈ 5–15 minutes per reading. The CLI reports its own cost estimate at API list prices (M0's smoke test: 8 Haiku requests ≈ $0.003); a subscription is not billed per token, but this is ordinary quota use, so the main session announces it first and stops at any rate-limit warning.

issues.description: Open issue from the extension fixer, not fixed. A run's working copy is seeded from the user's live .lake/build with no coordination with the workspace's own Lean refresh. createRunShadow first lists .lake/build (collectBuildSeed). Afterwards it runs lstat and copyFile on each file, with no lock and no re-check. The workspace's refreshLeanFacts runs `lake build` in place under the semantic runExclusive lock, and seeding does not take that lock. If Lake rewrites the build in between, the start is refused with ENOENT; this happens after a save or Undo shortly before 'These suffice', and RunManager.start's own set-premises write also schedules a refresh. When the start is not refused, the build mirror can hold a snapshot of a build in progress: Lake's temporary files instead of the artifacts, and possibly artifacts from two builds. Lake may then trust that snapshot when it checks the run. This is a proof-integrity risk for the review verdict. The board's own refresh after Accept would still show the truth. The VS Code e2e test was changed to wait for idle Lean before each start, so no test exercises this race any more.

Code: packages/runner/src/shadow/index.ts:93-115 (listing), 148, 172-179 (lstat and copyFile; any error refuses the start); packages/runner/src/run/manager.ts:864 (set-premises write) and 880 (createShadow right after it); packages/runner/src/semantic/index.ts:46 (runExclusive, used only by refreshes); packages/extension/test/suite/e2e-runs.test.ts:173-176 (the test now waits for idle Lean).
issues.suggested_fix: Seed only from a quiescent build: run collectBuildSeed and the copy inside semantic.runExclusive, or behind a ModelWorkspace pause/whenIdle hook. input.summary:
I fixed the one minor issue in my paths. smoke.mjs's leftover-unit check (6c) can now tell when an empty telelean-* scope belongs to the current run, and it stops it. The runner change that would stop such scopes from being left in the first place is outside my paths, so it is in open_issues.

What changed: a new helper module, packages/extension/scripts/smoke-units.mjs, finds this run's extension host pids and Claude run ids. It reads them from the test instance's own logs in its isolated user-data/logs (the "Extension host with pid N" lines and the "runId" entries) and from the run folders under globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs. It then matches runLean's unit names against them: telelean-tlws<pid>_<w>_<k>-<n>.scope (refreshes), telelean-p<pid>-<n>.scope (runLean's default run id) and telelean-<runId>-<n>.scope (Claude runs). Check 6c in smoke.mjs now treats a unit as this run's if a process in it points into the run's profile (as before) or if its name matches. Any unit of this run is stopped, plus reset-failed. If it still has processes, the check fails (as before). If it is empty, the script waits up to 2 s for systemd to end it, then stops it and prints a new non-failing WARN line, which is also saved in smoke-summary.json. Units that belong to other processes are only noted.

The issue's guess about the cause is wrong. The scope was not left by the extension host exiting mid-refresh. The user journal shows telelean-tlws1979697_2_1-23.scope "Started" at 02:50:30.013. That is 4 ms after runs.test.ts closed the runs_model board at 02:50:30.009, which disposed that workspace and cancelled refresh 1. The host kept running until 02:50:45.5. There was never a "Consumed CPU" line for the scope, and it only stopped at 02:53:25 when the verifier stopped it by hand.

The actual cause is in runLean. On a cancel, its terminate() SIGKILLs systemd-run while systemd-run is still waiting for its scope to be created. systemd 255 then puts the dying, not-yet-reaped process into the new cgroup. The kernel silently skips a process that is exiting, so the cgroup is never populated and systemd never gets the "empty" event. The scope then stays active/running with 0 tasks. runLean's close handler only runs `systemctl kill` on it, which cannot end an empty scope.

I reproduced this with a probe in my scratch folder. When systemd-run was killed 9 to 19 ms after starting, with the caller busy for 100 ms, 32 of 45 scopes were left active, with 0 tasks and 'populated 0'. `systemctl --user kill` left 11 of 11 such scopes active. `systemctl --user stop` removed them all.

I also tested the fix end to end. I made a real stuck scope named after the first smoke instance's host pid (telelean-tlws1996279_99_1-991.scope) and ran the full smoke. Both instances passed. smoke.mjs matched the scope to host 1996279, stopped it and printed one WARN line. Nothing was left behind afterwards. I did not touch any code that goes into the extension bundle, so I did not rebuild, and the dist/ hashes are unchanged.

open_issues: Runner (outside my paths: packages/runner/src/lean/runLean.ts and lean/systemd.ts), for the core-runner fixer. This is the real cause of the leftover scopes, and it is not the extension host exiting. runLean's terminate() calls child.kill('SIGKILL') (line 403). When a cancel or abort arrives while systemd-run is still waiting for its scope job, systemd 255 puts the dying, unreaped process into the new cgroup, and the kernel skips it without an error. The scope then becomes active/running with a cgroup that never had a process, and no 'empty' event ever comes. The close handler's fallback after its 2 s settle loop (line 483-485) is `systemctl kill`, which cannot end an empty scope. Suggested fix: add a stopUnit helper (`systemctl --user stop <unit>.scope`) and call it, followed by reset-failed, when the scope is still active or deactivating after the settle loop. Alternatively, always stop the unit after a cancel or timeout. An extra option: in terminate(), wait for the 'child-pid' status record before killing, so systemd-run is never killed while the scope is being created. Evidence: the journal for telelean-tlws1979697_2_1-23.scope (Started 02:50:30.013, 4 ms after the runs_model board closed and its workspace was disposed at 02:50:30.009; Stopped 02:53:25, by the verifier); the probe /tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad/turn9/fix3-extension-webview/probe-race.mjs (32 of 45 stuck; kill does not clear them, stop does).

The extension has no runner API it could call for this, so I made no change on the extension side.

1	# Design amendments (turn 2, 2026-11-01)
2	
3	These amend `verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_1/user_requested_documents/02_design_decisions.md` and `03_architecture.md`, and take precedence where they conflict. The ★ recommendations were approved with the notes below.
4	
5	## A1 · D-23(a): Claude is driven through your installed Claude Code CLI (the learnharness pattern), behind an LLM-agnostic interface
6	
7	**What telelean does.** It starts `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json …` in a copy of your model files ("the shadow"). The flags allow:
8	- the file tools (Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write) and telelean's own tools, and nothing else: no shell, no web;
9	- none of your Claude Code settings, hooks or CLAUDE.md;
10	- no API-key or cloud-provider environment variables, so you are never billed per token by accident.
11	
12	**Where telelean's tools live.** Tools such as `ask_user`, `check_lean` and `finish` are served over a local **MCP** server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give an agent tools, and most agent CLIs support it.
13	
14	**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. For an agent CLI that speaks MCP, the adapter is its flags plus parsing its event stream; an API-key provider is a further option. Telelean never handles anyone's login or keys.
15	
16	**Which binary.** By default, the Claude Code that ships with your VS Code Claude extension, found automatically. A setting can override it.
17	
18	**Dropped:** the Claude Agent SDK dependency (proprietary licence, plus its own ~330 MB binary).
19	
20	**Traded away:**
21	- *Then:* in-process hooks and typed events. *Now:* a command hook, plus parsing the CLI's JSON event stream.
22	- *Then:* resilience to CLI updates. *Now:* the event stream is more fragile across updates, so a minimum-version check and a recorded stream in the tests catch breakage.
23	
24	**Your reading of the policy is correct, with two nuances.** This is not legal advice.
25	1. **The CLI pattern doesn't "offer claude.ai login".** Each user signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, which is the case Anthropic's legal page explicitly allows.
26	2. **The Consumer Terms' clause on "automated or non-human means" still governs subscription use.** You start every run and it waits on your answers, which keeps it ordinary individual use. If you share telelean, the clean route is to point users at an API key or another provider.
27	
28	## A2 · The gate loop (your proposal, adopted)
29	
30	1. Claude says it is finished.
31	2. Telelean runs **non-LLM checks** on Claude's working copy. Each must hold:
32	   - the files build in the sandbox;
33	   - `#print axioms` lists only your selected assumptions, plus the "X exists" presuppositions of the things they mention;
34	   - there is no `sorry`;
35	   - the goal statement is identical to the one frozen before proving (via `lake comparator`);
36	   - there are no forbidden commands (`#eval` etc.);
37	   - your natural-language text is untouched.
38	3. **On failure** the board shows a small notice. For example: *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it used `foo`, which you didn't select. Asking Claude to retry."* Claude is re-prompted automatically with the exact failure.
39	4. **After 3 failed attempts**, a setting you can change, the board tells you what kept failing. It then **reverts the working copy to the last state that passed**. The attempt is kept in the history.
40	
41	Your real files are never touched until you press Accept, so "revert" only ever applies to Claude's copy.
42	
43	**What is a question for you, not a retry.** These need your judgement, which a program can't supply:
44	- a new definition or vocabulary item (yes/no);
45	- a proposed missing premise (a ghost node: "I hold this" / "no");
46	- whether the Lean says what your sentence says (the meaning review).
47	
48	**The honest limit.** The checks guarantee that the goal follows from the selected assumptions *as formalised*. Whether the formalisation matches your meaning is what the review step (and M3's faithfulness tools) is for.
49

24	| The sandbox blocks your home folder and the network | Inert probes: writing to the real `$HOME` fails; listing `$HOME` shows an empty tmpfs; DNS, TCP, D-Bus and abstract sockets are all blocked |
25	| The memory cap works | 600 MB allocated under a 256 MB cap is reported as `oom` (cgroup `oom_kill=1` and systemd `Result=oom-kill` agree) |
26	| Nothing survives a timeout, cancel or crash | The whole scope is killed in each case, including when the host process dies |
27	| `#print axioms` footprints are exact | `cynder_not_good.holds` has exactly the 11 expected axioms |
28	| `lake comparator` runs under the sandbox | Honest proof: accepted. Rejected: weakened goal (both ways), unselected assumption, smuggled axiom, `sorry`, retyped assumption, missing proof, vocabulary turned into a definition. A sandbox start-up failure is reported as "could not start", never as "rejected" |
29	| No side effects | `~/.elan/known-projects` stays at 36 lines; no units or processes are left over |

32	
33	**Offline (93 tests):**
34	- argv assembly;
35	- environment sanitising: every `CLAUDE*`/`ANTHROPIC_*` variable is stripped, because a Claude-enabled VS Code exports parent-session variables;
36	- parsing of the JSON event stream;
37	- the loopback MCP tool server (bearer token; Host/Origin checks);
38	- the path guard;
39	- the fake backend.

42	- **8 requests;** about 36k cache-read, 9k cache-write and 14 uncached input tokens, and 1.1k output tokens. The CLI's cost estimate is **$0.003**.
43	- **(a) Login and long waits: pass.** The subscription (Claude Ultra, first-party, no API key) was verified *before* any prompt was sent. The shell tool was absent and telelean's tools loaded. A question blocked for **75 s** and the answer still reached Claude.
44	- **(b) File confinement: pass.**
45	  - Allowed: reading the model file.
46	  - Denied: `/etc/hostname`, a decoy file outside the copy, and whole-folder Grep/Glob, which would have searched hidden files.
47	  - No hidden or outside content leaked.
48	- **(c) Reload: pass.** The CLI was killed mid-question, then `--resume` continued the same session and finished.
49	
50	## Spike 3: the board in a real VS Code webview
51	
52	The board has:
53	- three independently scrolling columns, with each card's sentence first, a kind glyph, a blue aura when formalised, and a chevron that expands to the Lean code;
54	- SVG arrows: dashed for declared, solid for verified. They follow scrolling and resizing, and become a stub plus an "n linked" badge when one end is scrolled away;
55	- drag to another column, which requests a kind change;
56	- click and Ctrl/Cmd-click selection, with a tray holding a target slot and a **These suffice** button;
57	- the A|D|G box.
58	
59	Colours come only from VS Code theme variables, and the Content Security Policy is strict and nonce-based. In the real VS Code 1.140 test instance the webview loads with **0 CSP violations** and reports "4 cards, 3 arrows" for Spyro and "75 cards, 34 arrows (31 stubs)" for the large test graph.

61	## Design changes learned in M0 (to fold into M1/M2)
62	
63	1. **Sandbox:**
64	   - Add a small *keeper* process with `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL`. Without it a crashed host leaves the sandbox running; this was tested as a negative control.
65	   - Set `OOMPolicy=stop` and run `reset-failed` afterwards.
66	   - "Could not start" is decided by bwrap's `exit-code` record, not by `child-pid`.
67	   - PATH must put the toolchain's `bin/` first, never elan's proxies.
68	2. **Comparator messages.** A weakened goal abbrev is reported as "definition mismatch" against the abbrev's own name. The user- and LLM-facing message should say "a definition the frozen statement depends on changed".
69	3. **Claude CLI:**
70	   - Telelean's MCP tools need `alwaysLoad` and `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`, otherwise they hide behind a ToolSearch tool that isn't allowed.
71	   - Long questions need a per-server MCP timeout.
72	   - The account check uses the CLI's `initialize` reply before any prompt, so a refusal costs nothing.
73	   - In `-p` mode the CLI silently ignores an invalid settings file. Telelean therefore asks the running CLI for its hook list and refuses to start without the guard. The minimum CLI version is 2.1.295.
74	   - `--max-turns` counts per user turn, so telelean enforces its own run cap.
75	   - Haiku 5.5 can't switch thinking off in CLI 2.1.314; low effort keeps output short.

## 10. Proving with Claude: "These suffice" (M2)

A run asks Claude to decide whether the target card follows from exactly the premises you selected. Claude works in a private copy of your model (never in your files): it formalises the cards that have no Lean yet, freezes the statements, proves, and says it is finished. telelean then checks the result itself, with Lean and fixed rules. You review a proposal on the board and decide: **Accept**, **Feedback** or **Discard**.

### 10.1 What you need

- **Claude Code**, logged in with your claude.ai subscription. telelean uses your own Claude Code (no API key): by default the binary of the VS Code Claude Code extension, else `claude` on the PATH, else `~/.local/bin/claude` (setting `telelean.claude.path` to choose one). Version 2.1.295 or newer.
- The model builds with toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0` and has no Lake dependencies; the Lean sandbox works (as for M1's checks); enough free memory (`telelean.memory.minAvailableGiB`).
- **Your files must build.** Right after the run starts telelean builds your files once; Lean errors anywhere end the run before Claude is contacted ("your files have Lean errors (…); fix or save them, then start again").

### 10.2 Starting a run

1. On the board, click the premises, then Ctrl/Cmd+click the target (a Goal or a Derivation; an Assumption is something you hold: make it a Derivation first). The tray shows "premises ⊢ target".
2. Press **These suffice ▶** (exactly these premises), **Add to its premises ▶** (the target's declared premises plus the selected ones) or, with only the target selected, **Self-evident?** (no premises at all).
3. The first time in a model folder, telelean asks for your consent (10.3).
4. telelean checks the start before anything is sent ("preflight"): no other run of this model folder is active; the selection is valid; toolchain, sandbox and memory are fine; Claude Code is found. Any refusal changes nothing. Only then does it declare the selected premises on the target (`premises:`, M1's undoable action; skipped when they are already declared, and never for Self-evident?), make the private copy, build your files once, and start Claude Code. Claude Code itself checks before the first prompt that you are logged in with a claude.ai subscription; a refusal there costs no quota.

At most one run per model folder at a time. Closing the board does not stop a run: the header badge ("Claude: working on Spyro · 3/25 checks") shows it in any board of the folder.

### 10.3 Consent and what leaves the machine

Before the first run in a model folder telelean asks: *"Run Claude on this model? telelean sends this subject's cards (sentences, reasons, Lean statements), its vocabulary and your recorded answers, plus any model file Claude reads, to Anthropic through your Claude Code login (your claude.ai subscription; no API key)."* **Run with Claude** is remembered for that folder; **Cancel** starts nothing and is not remembered (you are asked again next time).

What is sent, through your Claude Code login: a fixed system prompt (the same text every run), the first message (the target, the selected premises and the subject's other cards with their sentences, reasons and Lean; the vocabulary; your earlier answers that are in force; the run's budget), every model file Claude reads in its copy (all subjects of the project are in the copy, so imports work), and every tool result (Lean check results, your answers, the check verdicts). Your Feedback text and your answers go as messages. Nothing else from your machine is sent.

What stays on your machine: each run's directory in VS Code's storage for telelean (`~/.config/Code/User/globalStorage/telelean.telelean/runs/…`: Claude's working copy, its Lean build, its git history, `run.json` and `session/transcript.jsonl`, the exact text of every message and tool call). The newest `telelean.run.keepRuns` (10) finished runs per model folder are kept. Claude Code also keeps its own transcript of each session under `~/.claude/projects/` (that is how a session is resumed); telelean never reads it.

#!/bin/bash
# memwatch.sh <root-pid> <logfile>: samples MemAvailable and the summed RSS of root-pid's process tree (plus
# processes in telelean-* systemd scopes) every second until root-pid exits; kills root-pid's tree if
# MemAvailable drops below 8 GB (the machine crashed from RAM exhaustion before).
ROOT=$1; OUT=$2; PEAK=0; PEAKAVAIL=999999; MINAVAIL=999999
desc() { local p=$1; echo $p; for c in $(pgrep -P $p 2>/dev/null); do desc $c; done; }
while kill -0 $ROOT 2>/dev/null; do
  AV=$(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)
  PIDS=$(desc $ROOT | sort -u)
  # Lean jobs run in transient systemd scopes; their processes may not be descendants.
  for u in $(systemctl --user list-units --plain --no-legend --no-pager 'telelean-*' 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'); do
    cg=$(systemctl --user show "$u" -p ControlGroup --value 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$cg" ] && [ -f "/sys/fs/cgroup$cg/cgroup.procs" ] && PIDS="$PIDS $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup$cg/cgroup.procs)"
  done
  RSS=0; for p in $(echo $PIDS | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -u); do r=$(awk '/VmRSS/ {print $2}' /proc/$p/status 2>/dev/null); RSS=$((RSS + ${r:-0})); done
  RSS=$((RSS/1024))
  [ $RSS -gt $PEAK ] && PEAK=$RSS
  [ $AV -lt $MINAVAIL ] && MINAVAIL=$AV
  echo "$(date +%T) avail=${AV}MB treeRSS=${RSS}MB nproc=$(echo $PIDS | wc -w)" >> $OUT
  if [ $AV -lt 8000 ]; then echo "$(date +%T) LOW MEMORY: killing tree of $ROOT" >> $OUT; for p in $(desc $ROOT); do kill -TERM $p 2>/dev/null; done; fi
  sleep 1
done
echo "DONE peakTreeRSS=${PEAK}MB minAvail=${MINAVAIL}MB" >> $OUT
EOF

issues.description: The quota-tripwire exemptions are broader than their purpose (defence in depth only; no current test exploits them, which I checked by grep, the tripwire runs and the layer-1-off runs). (a) ClaudeCliBackend.startSession lets ANY binary start when the launcher is process.execPath. A JavaScript Claude Code CLI (npm-installed cli.js) given as the binary would start a real session under node. (b) createClaudeBackend skips the tripwire whenever settings.resolve is defined, even `{}` or `{ runVersion }`; it then scans the real ~/.vscode/extensions, PATH and ~/.local/bin, and with `{}` runs their --version. startSession is still blocked by the setpriv launcher. issues.description: RunManager.dispose() (window closing or deactivation) closes the Claude session and persists 'interrupted', but never cancels the run's Lean jobs. When the extension host exits, the runLean keeper (pdeathsig) takes the scope down. But if the host survives deactivation (extension disabled or updated, or testing.disposeWorkspace), a running check or gate job keeps going for up to leanJobMs (120 s, under the 4 GiB cap), and its result is thrown away.
issues.evidence: /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/runner/src/run/manager.ts:1776-1804: dispose() stops the clock, calls run.files.close(...), `void session?.close({ force: true })`, and has no cancelLean or lean.cancelRun call (cancel() at :1384 has one). In my probe, dispose() during check_lean's Lean job left `telelean-<runId>-10.scope` running right after dispose. It disappeared within 5 s only because the Spyro job finished. run.json said interrupted, canResume true.
issues.suggested_fix: In dispose(), for an active run, fire and forget `(services.cancelLean ?? lean.cancelRun)(run.runId).catch(() => undefined)`, as cancel() does.

## 8. The LLM harness

### 8.1 The slot (S9)
```ts
interface LlmBackend { id: 'claude-agent-sdk' | 'claude-cli' | 'fake' | 'anthropic-api';
  caps: { builtinFileTools: boolean; subscriptionAuth: boolean; resume: boolean };
  startSession(cfg: SessionConfig): Promise<LlmSession>; }
interface LlmSession { send(turn: string): AsyncIterable<LlmEvent>; interrupt(): Promise<void>; close(): Promise<void>; }
interface AgentToolHost {                 // one implementation, used by every backend AND the fake
  check_lean(a): Promise<CheckResult>; ask_user(a): Promise<Answers>; propose_assumption(a): Promise<Adoption>;
  finish(a): Promise<GateVerdict>; }
```
- **FakeBackend** replays scripts of `{writeFile | edit | callTool}` steps *against the shadow*. The walkthrough test therefore exercises the real tools, gate and proposal logic.
- **Recorded stream.** One real SDK stream, recorded during M0/M2, is replayed in unit tests to catch SDK drift.
- **Later:** an API-key backend, needed before any sharing (D-23).

# Design amendments (turn 2, 2026-11-01)

These amend `verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_1/user_requested_documents/02_design_decisions.md` and `03_architecture.md`, and take precedence where they conflict. The ★ recommendations were approved with the notes below.

## A1 · D-23(a): Claude is driven through your installed Claude Code CLI (the learnharness pattern), behind an LLM-agnostic interface

**What telelean does.** It starts `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json …` in a copy of your model files ("the shadow"). The flags allow:
- the file tools (Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write) and telelean's own tools, and nothing else: no shell, no web;
- none of your Claude Code settings, hooks or CLAUDE.md;
- no API-key or cloud-provider environment variables, so you are never billed per token by accident.

**Where telelean's tools live.** Tools such as `ask_user`, `check_lean` and `finish` are served over a local **MCP** server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give an agent tools, and most agent CLIs support it.

**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. For an agent CLI that speaks MCP, the adapter is its flags plus parsing its event stream; an API-key provider is a further option. Telelean never handles anyone's login or keys.

**Which binary.** By default, the Claude Code that ships with your VS Code Claude extension, found automatically. A setting can override it.

**Dropped:** the Claude Agent SDK dependency (proprietary licence, plus its own ~330 MB binary).

**Traded away:**
- *Then:* in-process hooks and typed events. *Now:* a command hook, plus parsing the CLI's JSON event stream.
- *Then:* resilience to CLI updates. *Now:* the event stream is more fragile across updates, so a minimum-version check and a recorded stream in the tests catch breakage.

**Your reading of the policy is correct, with two nuances.** This is not legal advice.
1. **The CLI pattern doesn't "offer claude.ai login".** Each user signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, which is the case Anthropic's legal page explicitly allows.
2. **The Consumer Terms' clause on "automated or non-human means" still governs subscription use.** You start every run and it waits on your answers, which keeps it ordinary individual use. If you share telelean, the clean route is to point users at an API key or another provider.

## A2 · The gate loop (your proposal, adopted)

1. Claude says it is finished.
2. Telelean runs **non-LLM checks** on Claude's working copy. Each must hold:
   - the files build in the sandbox;
   - `#print axioms` lists only your selected assumptions, plus the "X exists" presuppositions of the things they mention;
   - there is no `sorry`;
   - the goal statement is identical to the one frozen before proving (via `lake comparator`);
   - there are no forbidden commands (`#eval` etc.);
   - your natural-language text is untouched.
3. **On failure** the board shows a small notice. For example: *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it used `foo`, which you didn't select. Asking Claude to retry."* Claude is re-prompted automatically with the exact failure.
4. **After 3 failed attempts**, a setting you can change, the board tells you what kept failing. It then **reverts the working copy to the last state that passed**. The attempt is kept in the history.

Your real files are never touched until you press Accept, so "revert" only ever applies to Claude's copy.

**What is a question for you, not a retry.** These need your judgement, which a program can't supply:
- a new definition or vocabulary item (yes/no);
- a proposed missing premise (a ghost node: "I hold this" / "no");
- whether the Lean says what your sentence says (the meaning review).

**The honest limit.** The checks guarantee that the goal follows from the selected assumptions *as formalised*. Whether the formalisation matches your meaning is what the review step (and M3's faithfulness tools) is for.

## A3 · D-33: history dropdown with revert and a storage counter

**Storage.** Every change telelean writes is first snapshotted as a private git ref in the model folder (`refs/telelean/…`); your branches are never touched. Git stores files compressed and deduplicated, so a snapshot costs only what changed, typically a few KB.

**The dropdown** (board header):
- Each entry shows time · action · one-line summary, e.g. *"These suffice → proved cynder-not-good"*.
- Selecting an entry previews that state read-only, with its diff.
- **Revert to this** first snapshots the current state, so a revert can itself be undone.

**The counter** shows disk use per subject and in total. It measures **disk, not RAM**: snapshots sit on disk and add nothing to memory pressure. A "keep the last N" pruning option is included.

**When:** M1, together with the board's first writes.

## A4 · D-10: several subjects per project

D-10 is attempted in M1: one module subtree and namespace per subject, plus a subject picker. If it proves complex, M1 ships one subject first. Comparing models, your two-person "convince someone" setting, is deferred and may need its own analyses.

## A5 · D-31, D-32

- **D-31:** headless extension tests use `xvfb-run`.
- **D-32:** dropped. `mental_model/` is the sample model workspace.

## A6 · M0 contents (replaces the M0 row of 03 §11 / D-29)

M0 is three spikes, each independently verified:
1. Sandboxed Lean runs (memory cap + bwrap), with `lake comparator` running under them.
2. The Claude CLI harness, built offline: provider interface, flags, environment sanitising, MCP tool server, file-confinement hook, a fake backend for tests.
3. The board prototype in a real VS Code webview.

After those, one small real-Claude smoke test, announced to you before it runs. It covers your login, a long blocking question, file confinement, and resuming after a reload.

**Recommendation.**

  1. Sort axioms are 0-ary `axiom T : Type` only: no `Sort u`, no universe parameters, and no `axiom T : Prop` used as a sort.

### D-18 ★ Node lifecycle (IC-10; your cynder.lean revisions)
**Recommendation.**
- **Delete.** Removes the block, and optionally the declaration, after a confirmation that lists the affected dependents.
- **Suspend.** Excludes an assumption for *what-if* exploration without deleting it.
- **Refine / supersede**, your "h1 is actually … superseding h1":
  - The "Refine…" action, which you can also type as `h1 is actually …` into "Ask Claude…", starts a run scoped to that node.
  - **By default the vocabulary stays unchanged.** The refined fact becomes an ASSUMPTION (`abbrev cynder_past : Prop := cynder.past = "dark"` + `axiom cynder_past.holds : cynder_past`) and **inherits h1's rationale**.
  - h1 is re-derived through a **bridge** (`∀ c, c.past = "dark" → HasDarkPast c`). The bridge is a new belief, so Claude proposes it as a ghost for you to adopt.
  - h1 then stays on the board, collapsed under its refinement ("h1 ⇐ refined by …"), and dependents compile unchanged. The new block carries `supersedes: h1`.
  - The alternative is to redefine the vocabulary (e.g. `HasDarkPast c := c.past = "dark"`). That needs your endorsement, and it changes the meaning of every node whose statement closure mentions it. All of those nodes are listed in the review as "meaning changed by refinement", and the gate's immutability check is authorised for exactly that set. This pattern is re-verified in M3.
- **Merge.** Re-points premises, layout and decisions.
- **Attempts history.** Every "These suffice" press is kept with its verdict.
- **Anti-goals (M3).** A statement that "should NOT follow"; if it becomes provable, telelean reports over-generation, as in your smoking.lean §6.

A re-freeze happens only when you adopt a ghost or send feedback.

**The end review shows meaning before proof status.** For each new or changed statement:

- **Scope.** You choose it per answer: this run, these nodes, or the whole subject.
- **Unasked choices.** Every interpretive choice Claude made *without* asking is listed under "Assumed without asking", with "Ask me instead". It is not common ground until you acknowledge it.
- **(a) Storage.** `.telelean/decisions.json`, recording who decided and who worded it. Decisions show as ⚑ chips on affected cards and in a drawer. Revoking one marks the affected formalisations stale. The alternative is DECISION markup blocks inside your Lean files.
- **Budget.** At most 3 questions per batch by default, adjustable.

**Walkthrough.** The first question is the modality of "PG games *cannot have* …" (literal vs normative; doc 01 §3).

### D-21 Accepting, feedback and hand edits (S3, S16, S33, S42)
**Default.**
- A proved GOAL→DERIVATION is proposed in the diff, never made silently.
- Accept is all-or-nothing (node-level partial accept comes later). Feedback continues the same Claude session.
- **Hand edits are authoritative.** Editing a statement or sentence yourself marks its sign-off stale and drops it from any frozen set, with a "Re-sign" action. Lean you write counts as signed off by you.
- If files changed during a run, telelean 3-way merges, re-runs the gate, and only then applies.

### D-22 Where the board lives (IC-17)
**Default.** An editor-area tab that restores after a reload.

# semantic fixtures

Used by `packages/runner/test/semantic/` (WP3, the M1 semantic layer: `lake build` + `.ilean` + check file →
`LeanFacts`). Base project: `../spyro`. Plain, trusted Lean files: no `#eval`, no `.telelean/config.json`.
Tests always copy `../spyro` to a scratch directory (`$TELELEAN_TEST_TMP`) and apply an overlay there; nothing is
ever built here.

## `overlays/<name>/`

Files copied over a scratch copy of `../spyro` (complete replacements of the files they contain).

| Overlay | What it is | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `build-error` | the `proved` stage of `../runner-lean`, but the goal's proof uses the wrong assumption: a type error with a multi-line message | AT3.2: `Model.Spyro.Main` failed, the root `Model` dependency-failed, Vocabulary fresh |
| `extras` | the `proved` stage plus: a conditional theorem `d1.holds (h : cynder_not_good) : d1`; a two-hypothesis conditional `d3.holds` whose `#check` output wraps; a derivation used by a proof (`d0.holds`, `g2.holds : g2 := d0.holds.2`); a proof through an untracked lemma (`g3.holds := helper_lemma`); a sorry theorem `withSorry`; a hidden assumption `axiom hidden : ∀ c : Character, HasDarkPast c`; `axiom c2 : Character`, `axiom P0 : Prop`, `axiom f : Character → Game`; a def used by a statement abbrev (`darkAndPG`, `uses_def`); a structure with a documented field (`Rec.past`); a data instance (`instInhabitedRec`); a private theorem (skipped); and `Model/Spyro/Orphan.lean`, imported by nothing (`not-built`) | AT3.3 |
| `nonbmp-error` | `../spyro` plus a line with a non-BMP character (`𝔸`, two UTF-16 units) before an unknown identifier | AT3.9: Lean says column 30 (code points), the facts say character 31 (UTF-16) |
| `toolchain` | `lean-toolchain` = `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0` | AT3.6: `unsupported-toolchain`, nothing spawned |
| `manifest-package` | a `lake-manifest.json` listing one package (`mathlib`; the file is only read, nothing is fetched) | AT3.11: `unsupported-project` |

The "missing manifest" case of AT3.11 has no overlay: the test deletes `lake-manifest.json` from its scratch copy.

-- Extras for the semantic-layer tests (see test-fixtures/semantic/README.md). Plain declarations, no #eval.

/-- Cynder would not be a good addition, or something false -/
abbrev d1 : Prop := ¬ GoodAddition cynder newSpyro ∨ False
/-- d1 holds if the goal does: a conditional proof -/
theorem d1.holds (h : cynder_not_good) : d1 := Or.inl h

abbrev a_statement_with_a_rather_long_name_so_that_types_wrap : Prop := HasDarkPast cynder
abbrev another_statement_with_a_long_name_so_types_wrap_too : Prop := IsPG newSpyro
/-- Both long-named statements -/
abbrev d3 : Prop := HasDarkPast cynder ∧ IsPG newSpyro
theorem d3.holds (h1 : a_statement_with_a_rather_long_name_so_that_types_wrap)
    (h2 : another_statement_with_a_long_name_so_types_wrap_too) : d3 :=
  ⟨h1, h2⟩

/-- Cynder has a dark past and the new Spyro game is PG -/
abbrev d0 : Prop := cynder_dark_past ∧ new_spyro_pg
theorem d0.holds : d0 := ⟨cynder_dark_past.holds, new_spyro_pg.holds⟩
/-- The new Spyro game is PG, by way of d0 -/
abbrev g2 : Prop := new_spyro_pg
theorem g2.holds : g2 := d0.holds.2

/-- An untracked lemma -/
theorem helper_lemma : HasDarkPast cynder := cynder_dark_past.holds
abbrev g3 : Prop := HasDarkPast cynder
theorem g3.holds : g3 := helper_lemma

theorem withSorry : GoodAddition cynder newSpyro := sorry

/-- A hidden assumption -/
axiom hidden : ∀ c : Character, HasDarkPast c
axiom c2 : Character
axiom P0 : Prop
axiom f : Character → Game

/-- dark past and PG -/
def darkAndPG (c : Character) (g : Game) : Prop := HasDarkPast c ∧ IsPG g
abbrev uses_def : Prop := darkAndPG cynder newSpyro

/-- A record with one field -/
structure Rec where
  /-- the past -/
  past : Prop

/-- A data instance -/
instance instInhabitedRec : Inhabited Rec := ⟨⟨True⟩⟩

private theorem secret_helper : True := trivial

end Spyro
