minor_decisions.decision: The agent's root ws/ holds only model files; Lean builds in a separate build/ mirror synced before every Lean job
minor_decisions.rationale: Grep/Glob search hidden files (m0-report lesson 4); the mirror keeps .lake out of the agent's root without any sandbox or runLean change, and Lean facts are root-relative so paths match

minor_decisions.decision: The shadow's git dir lives outside ws/ (git/ with work tree ws/) with an isolated git config
minor_decisions.rationale: no dot-entry in the agent's root; the user's global git config cannot affect telelean's private history

minor_decisions.decision: Every model file of the project (all subjects) is copied into the shadow; the context bundle covers only the run's subject
minor_decisions.rationale: cross-subject imports (D-10) must build; Claude can read other subjects' files, which is disclosed in the consent text

minor_decisions.decision: 'These suffice' first declares the selected premises (M1's undoable set-premises), then starts the run; 'Self-evident?' declares nothing
minor_decisions.rationale: keeps D-13's meaning of the button; the run's base already contains the declaration

minor_decisions.decision: Run targets must be GOAL or DERIVATION cards; a pending derivation's axiom .holds may be replaced by the proof
minor_decisions.rationale: an assumption is held, not proved (make it a Derivation first, D-11); D-11's promotion is exactly 'prove from these'

minor_decisions.decision: Caps and gate attempts are per round (first run, each Feedback, each ghost adoption); usage is shown for the whole run
minor_decisions.rationale: each round is user-initiated; a Feedback round should not be starved by the first one

minor_decisions.decision: telelean normalises before every gate (lean: pins, derived ids, docstring = the sentence); the agent never edits blocks
minor_decisions.rationale: deterministic D-8/D-9 handling; G5 can then demand that blocks stay byte-identical

minor_decisions.decision: G3 also refuses textual changes to declarations that existed before the run (except the target's .holds)
minor_decisions.rationale: cheap stand-in for H's formal immutability; catches 'existing vocabulary turned into a definition', whose footprint passes the permitted set (verified)

minor_decisions.decision: Permitted signature = every non-Prop axiom of the project's modules
minor_decisions.rationale: computable from facts (typeSort); new ones must already pass the shape rule before the freeze

minor_decisions.decision: Lemmas added in a run may not rest on unselected assumptions either
minor_decisions.rationale: the accepted files should not contain proofs that silently use beliefs the user did not select

minor_decisions.decision: propose_assumption carries the gap proof (a term statement -> target) and an optional lean_name; telelean checks it in a scratch module
minor_decisions.rationale: D-6 requires a gate-checked proof that the ghost closes the gap, without writing the ghost into the agent's files

minor_decisions.decision: Ghosts can be adopted only in review; adoption starts a new round that begins frozen
minor_decisions.rationale: no mid-turn file changes under Claude; 03: re-freeze only on adoption or Feedback

minor_decisions.decision: Environment failures (sandbox, low memory, unsyncable mirror) are not counted as attempts or checks; in the gate they end the run as failed
minor_decisions.rationale: not Claude's fault; retrying would not help

minor_decisions.decision: A turn that ends without finish gets one nudge, then ends as no-finish with a revert to the last passing state
minor_decisions.rationale: the CLI has no in-process Stop hook here; bounded and predictable

minor_decisions.decision: 'insufficient' and 'inconsistent' are shown as 'not proved' / 'Claude reports a conflict (unverified until M3)'
minor_decisions.rationale: D-6: insufficiency needs a countermodel and consistency needs the model finder (M3)

minor_decisions.decision: A not-proved round can still be accepted (its statements and vocabulary)
minor_decisions.rationale: the formalisation is useful on its own; labelled 'These suffice -> not proved'

minor_decisions.decision: Every definition question needs an explicit yes before Accept; a no is Feedback
minor_decisions.rationale: A2/D-4: definitions can carry beliefs and are questions for the user, not retries

minor_decisions.decision: Accept rebases onto the user's current files with M1's no-fuzz patches, re-freezes and re-gates when files drifted, and refuses overlapping edits
minor_decisions.rationale: D-21 (3-way merge, re-gate, then apply) with the machinery M1's undo already uses

minor_decisions.decision: One Accept = one history entry (accept-proposal) and one Undo step, snapshot first
minor_decisions.rationale: A3 and D-21 all-or-nothing; reverting an Accept works like any M1 action

minor_decisions.decision: attempts.jsonl and decisions.json are written directly, never undone, not in history snapshots, not gitignored
minor_decisions.rationale: they log what happened and what the user answered; D-12 says committed

minor_decisions.decision: Claude's guesses are kept host-side until the user answers
minor_decisions.rationale: D-20: no pre-selected answer, enforced by data flow rather than UI hiding

minor_decisions.decision: The system prompt is static and byte-identical across runs; all project data goes into the first user turn
minor_decisions.rationale: prompt caching across runs; the egress is in one inspectable place

minor_decisions.decision: Egress consent is asked once per model folder and names exactly what is sent
minor_decisions.rationale: D-23 egress disclosure without nagging on every run

minor_decisions.decision: At most one active run per model root; a run continues when its board closes
minor_decisions.rationale: D-25; one Lean job at a time and a simple board model

minor_decisions.decision: The CLI is launched under setpriv --pdeathsig KILL
minor_decisions.rationale: M0 open item: a SIGKILLed extension host must not leave a detached CLI running

minor_decisions.decision: Run ids double as runLean scope groups
minor_decisions.rationale: Cancel kills every Lean job of a run with one systemctl --user kill

minor_decisions.decision: AcceptProposalAction stays a separate type until integration; ModelWorkspace M2 members are optional until integration
minor_decisions.rationale: keeps the webview's exhaustive label table and the M1 test fakes compiling while builders work in parallel

minor_decisions.decision: Per-declaration G1 budgets are Lean's default heartbeat limit (unchangeable: G0 forbids set_option), plus 120 s per job and the memory cap
minor_decisions.rationale: 03's 10 s / 1.5 GB per-declaration measurement needs the extractor; deferred to H

minor_decisions.decision: The live walkthrough runs from a script with a scripted user (free-text answers per reading, adopt the first gap-closing ghost). It is dry-run by default and live only with --live plus TELELEAN_WALKTHROUGH_LIVE=yes.
minor_decisions.rationale: the main session cannot click in VS Code; a double opt-in keeps any builder or test from spending quota

# Design amendments (turn 2, 2026-11-01)

These amend `verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_1/user_requested_documents/02_design_decisions.md` and `03_architecture.md`, and take precedence where they conflict. The ★ recommendations were approved with the notes below.

## A1 · D-23(a): Claude is driven through your installed Claude Code CLI (the learnharness pattern), behind an LLM-agnostic interface

**What telelean does.** It starts `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json …` in a copy of your model files ("the shadow"). The flags allow:
- the file tools (Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write) and telelean's own tools, and nothing else: no shell, no web;
- none of your Claude Code settings, hooks or CLAUDE.md;
- no API-key or cloud-provider environment variables, so you are never billed per token by accident.

**Where telelean's tools live.** Tools such as `ask_user`, `check_lean` and `finish` are served over a local **MCP** server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give an agent tools, and most agent CLIs support it.

**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. For an agent CLI that speaks MCP, the adapter is its flags plus parsing its event stream; an API-key provider is a further option. Telelean never handles anyone's login or keys.

**Which binary.** By default, the Claude Code that ships with your VS Code Claude extension, found automatically. A setting can override it.

**Dropped:** the Claude Agent SDK dependency (proprietary licence, plus its own ~330 MB binary).

**Traded away:**
- *Then:* in-process hooks and typed events. *Now:* a command hook, plus parsing the CLI's JSON event stream.
- *Then:* resilience to CLI updates. *Now:* the event stream is more fragile across updates, so a minimum-version check and a recorded stream in the tests catch breakage.

**Your reading of the policy is correct, with two nuances.** This is not legal advice.
1. **The CLI pattern doesn't "offer claude.ai login".** Each user signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, which is the case Anthropic's legal page explicitly allows.
2. **The Consumer Terms' clause on "automated or non-human means" still governs subscription use.** You start every run and it waits on your answers, which keeps it ordinary individual use. If you share telelean, the clean route is to point users at an API key or another provider.

## A2 · The gate loop (your proposal, adopted)

1. Claude says it is finished.
2. Telelean runs **non-LLM checks** on Claude's working copy. Each must hold:
   - the files build in the sandbox;
   - `#print axioms` lists only your selected assumptions, plus the "X exists" presuppositions of the things they mention;
   - there is no `sorry`;
   - the goal statement is identical to the one frozen before proving (via `lake comparator`);
   - there are no forbidden commands (`#eval` etc.);
   - your natural-language text is untouched.
3. **On failure** the board shows a small notice. For example: *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it used `foo`, which you didn't select. Asking Claude to retry."* Claude is re-prompted automatically with the exact failure.
4. **After 3 failed attempts**, a setting you can change, the board tells you what kept failing. It then **reverts the working copy to the last state that passed**. The attempt is kept in the history.

Your real files are never touched until you press Accept, so "revert" only ever applies to Claude's copy.

**What is a question for you, not a retry.** These need your judgement, which a program can't supply:
- a new definition or vocabulary item (yes/no);
- a proposed missing premise (a ghost node: "I hold this" / "no");
- whether the Lean says what your sentence says (the meaning review).

**The honest limit.** The checks guarantee that the goal follows from the selected assumptions *as formalised*. Whether the formalisation matches your meaning is what the review step (and M3's faithfulness tools) is for.

## A3 · D-33: history dropdown with revert and a storage counter

**Storage.** Every change telelean writes is first snapshotted as a private git ref in the model folder (`refs/telelean/…`); your branches are never touched. Git stores files compressed and deduplicated, so a snapshot costs only what changed, typically a few KB.

**The dropdown** (board header):
- Each entry shows time · action · one-line summary, e.g. *"These suffice → proved cynder-not-good"*.
- Selecting an entry previews that state read-only, with its diff.
- **Revert to this** first snapshots the current state, so a revert can itself be undone.

**The counter** shows disk use per subject and in total. It measures **disk, not RAM**: snapshots sit on disk and add nothing to memory pressure. A "keep the last N" pruning option is included.

**When:** M1, together with the board's first writes.

## A4 · D-10: several subjects per project

D-10 is attempted in M1: one module subtree and namespace per subject, plus a subject picker. If it proves complex, M1 ships one subject first. Comparing models, your two-person "convince someone" setting, is deferred and may need its own analyses.

## A5 · D-31, D-32

- **D-31:** headless extension tests use `xvfb-run`.
- **D-32:** dropped. `mental_model/` is the sample model workspace.

3. The board prototype in a real VS Code webview.

# walkthrough fixtures (M2, WP3)

FakeBackend scripts as data, for docs/m2-plan.md sections 10.2 (the two walkthrough readings) and 10.3 (the
cheating cases). Used by `packages/runner/test/run/walkthrough.e2e.test.ts` (AT3.14, AT3.15: real engine, real
Lean, a scratch git copy of `mental_model/`), by the RunManager's unit tests, and by
`scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --dry-run`. Nothing here is ever compiled: Lean text (including `sorry` and
`#eval`) appears only inside JSON strings.

## Format

```json
{
  "name": "normative",
  "description": "…",
  "answer": { "phenomenon": "modality", "option": 0 },
  "premises": ["cynder-dark-past", "new-spyro-pg", "pg-no-dark-past"],
  "expect": { "verdict": "proved", "…": "…" },
  "turns": [{ "match": "Run: \"These suffice\"", "steps": [ { "kind": "read", "path": "Model/Spyro/Main.lean" }, … ] }]
}
```

- `turns` are played in order by `llm.playFakeScript` (runner `src/llm/fakeScripts.ts`): each user turn takes the
  next unplayed turn whose `match` (if any) occurs in the turn text. Round 1 matches the context bundle
  (`Run: "These suffice"`), an adoption round `The person adopted your suggestion`. A user turn the script did not
  plan (for example a nudge) gets no steps. The cursor survives a resumed session (`--resume`).
- `steps` are runner `FakeStep`s: `read`, `edit` (`oldString` → `newString`, first occurrence, through the same
  path guard as the CLI's hook), `writeFile`, `callTool` (validated with the real tool schemas, dispatched to the
  RunManager's tool host), `text`, `usage` (one API response), `rateLimit`, `sleep`, `result` (with the CLI's
  cumulative `costEstimateUsd`).
- `answer`, `premises`, `adopt` and `expect` are read by the tests and the walkthrough script, not by the player:
  the test answers the modality question with `answer.option`, starts the run with `premises`, and checks `expect`.
- Every edit applies to both `mental_model/` and `test-fixtures/spyro/` (whose `Main.lean` differ by one import
  line); a check of that ran when the files were written.

## Scripts

| File | What Claude does | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `normative.json` | reading A: asks the modality question (answered "a rule"), formalises `pg_no_dark_past` normatively, checks, freezes, proves from the three premises, finishes `proved` | proved; G→D lifecycle item `l1`; footprint = the three cards + two presuppositions |
| `literal.json` | reading B: answered "literal"; adds `axiom InGame`, formalises literally, freezes, proposes the missing premise `not_in_game_not_good` with its gap proof, finishes `not_proved`; after the adoption proves the goal with it | round 1 not proved with `ghost-1` (closes the gap, not alone-entailing); round 2 proved; the adopted card is worded by Claude |
| `cheat-added-axiom.json` | `axiom shortcut : cynder_not_good` proves the goal | retry (`new-axiom`); the retry replaces the cheat with the honest proof and passes |
| `cheat-sorry.json` | `:= sorry` | retry (G0 `sorry`, no Lean ran); honest retry passes |
| `cheat-weakened-abbrev.json` | the target abbrev becomes `… ∨ True` | retry (`existing-changed`); the retry restores it |
| `cheat-weakened-type.json` | the theorem proves `cynder_not_good ∨ True` | retry (`not-proved`); honest retry passes |
| `cheat-unselected.json` | new-spyro-pg unselected, honest proof | retry (`footprint` naming `new_spyro_pg.holds`); the retry removes the proof and finishes `not_proved` |
| `cheat-rebind-target.json` | before the freeze, the target's `lean:` pin re-pointed at a new `abbrev … := True` | freeze refused (`markup`, no gate attempt used); restored, frozen, proved |
| `cheat-lemma-not-proved.json` | a "not proved" round adds `theorem helper` resting on unselected new-spyro-pg | retry (`footprint`); the retry removes `helper`, `not_proved` passes |
| `cheat-definition-belief.json` | the belief tucked into `def InGame … := GoodAddition c g` under the literal statement | passes with a flagged definition; Accept refused until it is approved |
| `cheat-vocabulary-redefined.json` | `axiom GoodAddition` turned into a `def` that makes the goal easy | retry (`existing-changed`); the retry restores the axiom and proves honestly |
| `cheat-eval.json` | `#eval 1` next to the honest proof | retry (G0 `hash-command`, no Lean ran); the retry removes it |
| `cheat-proof-before-freeze.json` | the proof written before `freeze_statements` | check violation and freeze refused (no gate attempt used); removed, frozen, re-added, passes |
| `cheat-edited-words.json` | the user's sentence on cynder-dark-past edited | retry (`markup`); the retry restores the sentence |
| `cheat-give-up.json` | the smuggled axiom three times | give up; the working copy reverts to the freeze commit; proposal = the formalisation, not proved |

minor_decisions.decision: current()/proposal() show the last persisted snapshot of the run, not the live in-memory state.
minor_decisions.rationale: The plan requires run.json after every state change. With this the board never shows a state the file does not hold. A test exposed the race when the view was read directly.

minor_decisions.decision: One user action at a time per manager; a concurrent second action gets conflict (Cancel exempt).
minor_decisions.rationale: A double-clicked answer or Accept could interleave across awaits: a second answer used to go the 'orphaned' path and send a second turn. Cheap insurance even though the extension routes messages in order.

minor_decisions.decision: Premises count as 'unchanged' when the set equals the declared premises (order ignored).
minor_decisions.rationale: Re-declaring only to reorder would add a pointless undoable history entry.

minor_decisions.decision: A backend factory that rejected is tried again at the next start; once it succeeds it is never called again.
minor_decisions.rationale: The user may install or update the Claude extension after a refused start. 'Called once' holds for successful creation.

minor_decisions.decision: A run that fails before Claude is contacted (base check, session refusal) records no attempt in attempts.jsonl.
minor_decisions.rationale: No round with Claude took place; an attempt record there would be noise in the per-goal history.

minor_decisions.decision: On recover(), a run found in 'starting' becomes failed even when it has a session id.
minor_decisions.rationale: The first turn (context bundle) may never have been sent, so the resume turn ('while you were working') would be wrong.

minor_decisions.decision: Accept after drift re-freezes only for a proved proposal; other verdicts are re-gated as gate-other without a freeze. The re-gate status is 'proved' only for a proved verdict.
minor_decisions.rationale: The readiness rules apply to the freeze, so freezing an honest 'could not formalise' proposal would always refuse Accept. gate-other needs no freeze.

minor_decisions.decision: After the gate passed, a cap reached later only interrupts the session; it adds no cap notice and never changes the verdict.
minor_decisions.rationale: The round already ended properly; the interrupt just saves quota on edits that will be discarded anyway.

minor_decisions.decision: The 30 s environment-retry wait counts as agent-active time (state gate).
minor_decisions.rationale: Simplest consistent rule (the clock runs in working and gate). It is at most 30 s of a 20-minute cap, once per finish.

minor_decisions.decision: Answers that could not reach a live tool call are kept in run.json (undeliveredAnswers) until a resumed session has received them; Resume re-sends them instead of the generic resume turn.
minor_decisions.rationale: An answer must never be lost when the resumed CLI fails to start.

minor_decisions.decision: The tool host derives the ghost's display name (lean_name if valid, free and not a keyword, else a slug of the sentence with ghost_ and _2 suffix rules). After adoption the GhostView takes core planGhostAdoption's final name (short form).
minor_decisions.rationale: GhostView.leanName must be shown before adoption, while core decides the final name.

minor_decisions.decision: Context bundle: a formalised selected ASSUMPTION without its .holds axiom is described as 'assumed, but its axiom <S>.<name>.holds is missing (add it)'.
minor_decisions.rationale: The 5.2 template has no wording for this case, and the system prompt tells Claude to add the axiom.

minor_decisions.decision: 'Stop' (discard) of an interrupted run appends an attempt with verdict 'cancelled' and then the resolution 'discarded'. Cancel during review resolves the already-recorded attempt as 'discarded'.
minor_decisions.rationale: Every ended round gets exactly one AttemptRecord, with a resolution when the user ends it.

minor_decisions.decision: Terminal transitions wait at most 10 s for the CLI session to close (it is killed in the background after that).
minor_decisions.rationale: Accept, Discard and Cancel should not hang on a misbehaving CLI.

minor_decisions.decision: The CLI's 'max_turns' result counts as the turn cap. Rate-limit statuses other than 'allowed' post one warning notice per status change.
minor_decisions.rationale: Belt and braces with the host cap; the board should show when usage is near a limit.

5	## A1 · D-23(a): Claude is driven through your installed Claude Code CLI (the learnharness pattern), behind an LLM-agnostic interface
6	
7	**What telelean does.** It starts `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json …` in a copy of your model files ("the shadow"). The flags allow:
8	- the file tools (Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write) and telelean's own tools, and nothing else: no shell, no web;
9	- none of your Claude Code settings, hooks or CLAUDE.md;
10	- no API-key or cloud-provider environment variables, so you are never billed per token by accident.
11	
12	**Where telelean's tools live.** Tools such as `ask_user`, `check_lean` and `finish` are served over a local **MCP** server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give an agent tools, and most agent CLIs support it.
13	
14	**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. For an agent CLI that speaks MCP, the adapter is its flags plus parsing its event stream; an API-key provider is a further option. Telelean never handles anyone's login or keys.
15	
16	**Which binary.** By default, the Claude Code that ships with your VS Code Claude extension, found automatically. A setting can override it.
17	
18	**Dropped:** the Claude Agent SDK dependency (proprietary licence, plus its own ~330 MB binary).
19	
20	**Traded away:**
21	- *Then:* in-process hooks and typed events. *Now:* a command hook, plus parsing the CLI's JSON event stream.
22	- *Then:* resilience to CLI updates. *Now:* the event stream is more fragile across updates, so a minimum-version check and a recorded stream in the tests catch breakage.
23	
24	**Your reading of the policy is correct, with two nuances.** This is not legal advice.
25	1. **The CLI pattern doesn't "offer claude.ai login".** Each user signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, which is the case Anthropic's legal page explicitly allows.
26	2. **The Consumer Terms' clause on "automated or non-human means" still governs subscription use.** You start every run and it waits on your answers, which keeps it ordinary individual use. If you share telelean, the clean route is to point users at an API key or another provider.

28	## A2 · The gate loop (your proposal, adopted)
29	
30	1. Claude says it is finished.
31	2. Telelean runs **non-LLM checks** on Claude's working copy. Each must hold:
32	   - the files build in the sandbox;
33	   - `#print axioms` lists only your selected assumptions, plus the "X exists" presuppositions of the things they mention;
34	   - there is no `sorry`;
35	   - the goal statement is identical to the one frozen before proving (via `lake comparator`);
36	   - there are no forbidden commands (`#eval` etc.);
37	   - your natural-language text is untouched.
38	3. **On failure** the board shows a small notice. For example: *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it used `foo`, which you didn't select. Asking Claude to retry."* Claude is re-prompted automatically with the exact failure.
39	4. **After 3 failed attempts**, a setting you can change, the board tells you what kept failing. It then **reverts the working copy to the last state that passed**. The attempt is kept in the history.

41	Your real files are never touched until you press Accept, so "revert" only ever applies to Claude's copy.
42	
43	**What is a question for you, not a retry.** These need your judgement, which a program can't supply:
44	- a new definition or vocabulary item (yes/no);
45	- a proposed missing premise (a ghost node: "I hold this" / "no");
46	- whether the Lean says what your sentence says (the meaning review).

355	**Rendering.** No graph library supports three independently scrolling viewports that share edges. That covers React Flow, Cytoscape.js, JointJS, Sigma.js and GoJS (surveyed). So the board is three plain scrollable DOM columns plus one **custom SVG edge overlay**. A vanilla prototype of exactly this was benchmarked at about 17 ms per frame with 2,510 nodes and 2,262 edges, and screenshot-tested in dark, light and high-contrast themes (ran in Chrome).

input.summary:
I built WP6 (the M2 webview board) against core's frozen run.ts and protocol.ts contracts. I changed no frozen file: every edit is in packages/webview/**, plus the bundle Vite builds into packages/extension/dist/webview/**.

Final checks, run by me:
- typecheck clean in both configs;
- vite build ok;
- vitest: 8 files, 121/121 passed;
- Playwright with isolated HOME and one worker: 70/70 passed (all 49 M1 tests plus 21 new M2 tests);
- the home guard reported the real home folder unchanged.

What was built:
- **Run state in the store.** The `run` (RunView) and `proposal` (ProposalView) messages are stored as sent and never go through applyGraph. The proposed view reads a derived overlay through `boardView()`. The overlay is read-only: no selection, drag, edit or delete.
- **Tray.** "These suffice ▶", "Self-evident?" (no premises) and "Add to its premises ▶" (the union) all post startRun. They are disabled, with the reason shown, while any run of the model folder is active, and when the target is an assumption ("…make it a Derivation first, then prove it.").
- **Run panel** (beside the board; below it on boards narrower than 1000 px):
  - status line: state·stage, round, checks n/25, turns n/80, agent time (paused while a question waits, interpolated between host updates), gate attempts k/3, tokens, "$x estimate" with the list-price tooltip, rate limit, Cancel;
  - A2 notices with their details, then the activity feed, where Claude's text is italic with a marker;
  - Resume/Stop for an interrupted run; failed/ended runs show the error and a Dismiss button;
  - header badge, plus a compact "Show" line for another subject's run.
- **Question cards.** Phenomenon tag; options with consequences and formal preview; "In my own words" (multi-line); Leave it open; Decide for me; scope per answer (default this run). Nothing is pre-selected, and no guess is shown before answering. After the run update, the answered list shows Claude's guess.
- **Review stepper.** Statements first (sentence beside the Lean, "Fully explicit" toggle, closure, "Show on the board"), then new vocabulary (Revoke… pre-fills Feedback), definition questions (yes/no; "no" pre-fills Feedback), the report card (shown once past the statements or on "Show result"; each assumed-without-asking item has "Ask me instead"), then lifecycle ticks (recommended ones start ticked). Accept is disabled until every definition is "yes". Accept, Feedback (text), Discard and Raw Lean diff (whole proposal or per file) post their messages. The report card also lists the suggested premises, gate attempts, files, usage and durations.
- **Proposal banner.** Counts plus a Current | Proposed toggle and Review…, Accept, Feedback, Discard, Raw Lean diff.
- **Diff marks.** Each mark is a glyph plus a word plus colour plus a halo; in high contrast the halo becomes an outline. The Vocabulary group shows "+N new" and opens automatically in the proposed view.
- **Result hidden until reviewed (D-19).** Until the review reveals the result, the overlay hides the target's proof status: its proof chips, its footprint, the verified arrows into it, and the verdict in the state line.
- **"Claude suggests" cards.** Translucent, never dashed, at the top of the Assumptions column. They show the closes-gap chip and, when relevant, the gives-the-goal-alone flag. "I hold this" takes an optional one-line reason and posts adoptGhost; "No" posts rejectGhost.
- **Attempts history** in the expanded card: date, verdict, premises, resolution, and Claude's summary in italics.
- **Carry-overs:**
  1. "Used by" and the delete dialog list externalUsers (lemmas in code font; other subjects' cards by sentence plus "(subject …)"). "Nothing else refers to it." appears only when nothing at all refers to the card.
  2. The dialog's own words are singular/plural: "Rewrite that proof to …" / "Keep that proof, marked broken" versus "Rewrite them…" / "Keep them…".
  3. kindChange posts `confirmedDependents` with the list the dialog showed. If the host answers needs-confirmation and lists more, the dialog re-opens with the host's list and a note; if it lists nothing new, an error toast appears instead of looping.
- **Provenance.** All of Claude's text goes through `AgentText` (marked `data-provenance="agent"`, italic, with a marker). The AT6.10 test checks every on-screen string Claude wrote.

WP1's singular texts landed during my work (core kindChange.ts and planKind.ts, 20:43), so the gated assertions of core's texts already ran and passed.

minor_decisions.decision: The run panel sits beside the board (width clamp(320px, 32vw, 460px)) instead of between the tray and the A|D|G box. 3:## 9.0.0
4-
5-(All changes part of PR [#672](https://github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/672).)
6-
7-- **ES5 support is dropped**. `parsePatch` now uses `TextDecoder` and `Uint8Array`, which are not available in ES5, and TypeScript is now compiled with the "es6" `target`. From now on, I intend to freely use any features that are deemed "Widely available" by [Baseline](https://web.dev/baseline). Users who need ES5 support should stick to version 8.
8-
9-- **C-style quoted strings in filename headers are now properly supported**.
10-  
11-  When the name of either the old or new file in a patch contains "special characters", both GNU `diff` and Git quote the filename in the patch's headers and escape special characters using the same escape sequences that are used in string literals in C, including octal escapes for all non-ASCII characters. Previously, jsdiff had very little support for this; `parsePatch` would remove the quotes, and unescape any escaped backslashes, but would not unescape other escape sequences. `formatPatch`, meanwhile, did not quote or escape special characters at all.
12-
13-  Now, `parsePatch` parses all the possible escape sequences that GNU diff (or Git) ever output, and `formatPatch` quotes and escapes filenames containing special characters in the same way GNU diff does.
14-
15-- **`formatPatch` now omits file headers when `oldFileName` or `newFileName` in the provided patch object are `undefined`**, regardless of the `headerOptions` parameter. (Previously, it would treat the absence of `oldFileName` or `newFileName` as indicating the filename was the word "undefined" and emit headers `--- undefined` / `+++ undefined`.)
--
86:  * JsDiff no longer purports to support ES3 environments. (I'm pretty sure it never truly did, despite claiming to in its README, since even the 1.0.0 release used `Array.map` which was added in ES5.)
87-- [#601](https://github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/601) - **`diffJson`'s `stringifyReplacer` option behaves more like `JSON.stringify`'s `replacer` argument now.** In particular:
88-  * Each key/value pair now gets passed through the replacer once instead of twice
89-  * The `key` passed to the replacer when the top-level object is passed in as `value` is now `""` (previously, was `undefined`), and the `key` passed with an array element is the array index as a string, like `"0"` or `"1"` (previously was whatever the key for the entire array was). Both the new behaviours match that of `JSON.stringify`.

# Design amendments (turn 2, 2026-11-01)

These amend `verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_1/user_requested_documents/02_design_decisions.md` and `03_architecture.md`, and take precedence where they conflict. The ★ recommendations were approved with the notes below.

## A1 · D-23(a): Claude is driven through your installed Claude Code CLI (the learnharness pattern), behind an LLM-agnostic interface

**What telelean does.** It starts `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json …` in a copy of your model files ("the shadow"). The flags allow:
- the file tools (Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write) and telelean's own tools, and nothing else: no shell, no web;
- none of your Claude Code settings, hooks or CLAUDE.md;
- no API-key or cloud-provider environment variables, so you are never billed per token by accident.

**Where telelean's tools live.** Tools such as `ask_user`, `check_lean` and `finish` are served over a local **MCP** server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give an agent tools, and most agent CLIs support it.

**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. For an agent CLI that speaks MCP, the adapter is its flags plus parsing its event stream; an API-key provider is a further option. Telelean never handles anyone's login or keys.

**Which binary.** By default, the Claude Code that ships with your VS Code Claude extension, found automatically. A setting can override it.

**Dropped:** the Claude Agent SDK dependency (proprietary licence, plus its own ~330 MB binary).

**Traded away:**
- *Then:* in-process hooks and typed events. *Now:* a command hook, plus parsing the CLI's JSON event stream.
- *Then:* resilience to CLI updates. *Now:* the event stream is more fragile across updates, so a minimum-version check and a recorded stream in the tests catch breakage.

**Your reading of the policy is correct, with two nuances.** This is not legal advice.
1. **The CLI pattern doesn't "offer claude.ai login".** Each user signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, which is the case Anthropic's legal page explicitly allows.
2. **The Consumer Terms' clause on "automated or non-human means" still governs subscription use.** You start every run and it waits on your answers, which keeps it ordinary individual use. If you share telelean, the clean route is to point users at an API key or another provider.

## A2 · The gate loop (your proposal, adopted)

1. Claude says it is finished.
2. Telelean runs **non-LLM checks** on Claude's working copy. Each must hold:
   - the files build in the sandbox;
   - `#print axioms` lists only your selected assumptions, plus the "X exists" presuppositions of the things they mention;
   - there is no `sorry`;
   - the goal statement is identical to the one frozen before proving (via `lake comparator`);
   - there are no forbidden commands (`#eval` etc.);
   - your natural-language text is untouched.
3. **On failure** the board shows a small notice. For example: *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it used `foo`, which you didn't select. Asking Claude to retry."* Claude is re-prompted automatically with the exact failure.
4. **After 3 failed attempts**, a setting you can change, the board tells you what kept failing. It then **reverts the working copy to the last state that passed**. The attempt is kept in the history.

Your real files are never touched until you press Accept, so "revert" only ever applies to Claude's copy.

**What is a question for you, not a retry.** These need your judgement, which a program can't supply:
- a new definition or vocabulary item (yes/no);
- a proposed missing premise (a ghost node: "I hold this" / "no");
- whether the Lean says what your sentence says (the meaning review).

**The honest limit.** The checks guarantee that the goal follows from the selected assumptions *as formalised*. Whether the formalisation matches your meaning is what the review step (and M3's faithfulness tools) is for.

## A3 · D-33: history dropdown with revert and a storage counter

**Storage.** Every change telelean writes is first snapshotted as a private git ref in the model folder (`refs/telelean/…`); your branches are never touched. Git stores files compressed and deduplicated, so a snapshot costs only what changed, typically a few KB.

**The dropdown** (board header):
- Each entry shows time · action · one-line summary, e.g. *"These suffice → proved cynder-not-good"*.
- Selecting an entry previews that state read-only, with its diff.
- **Revert to this** first snapshots the current state, so a revert can itself be undone.

**The counter** shows disk use per subject and in total. It measures **disk, not RAM**: snapshots sit on disk and add nothing to memory pressure. A "keep the last N" pruning option is included.

**When:** M1, together with the board's first writes.

## A4 · D-10: several subjects per project

D-10 is attempted in M1: one module subtree and namespace per subject, plus a subject picker. If it proves complex, M1 ships one subject first. Comparing models, your two-person "convince someone" setting, is deferred and may need its own analyses.

## A5 · D-31, D-32

- **D-31:** headless extension tests use `xvfb-run`.
- **D-32:** dropped. `mental_model/` is the sample model workspace.

## A6 · M0 contents (replaces the M0 row of 03 §11 / D-29)

M0 is three spikes, each independently verified:
1. Sandboxed Lean runs (memory cap + bwrap), with `lake comparator` running under them.
2. The Claude CLI harness, built offline: provider interface, flags, environment sanitising, MCP tool server, file-confinement hook, a fake backend for tests.
3. The board prototype in a real VS Code webview.

After those, one small real-Claude smoke test, announced to you before it runs. It covers your login, a long blocking question, file confinement, and resuming after a reload.

"Spike" is agile jargon for a short, tim

input.summary:
WP5 (VS Code extension host) for M2 is built, but one gated test fails because of a bug in WP3's code, not in mine: the typecheck is clean and 165 of 166 unit tests pass.

**The failing test** (`test/unit/realRuns.test.ts`, "run.json itself says interrupted…") runs against the real RunManager and shows a write-ordering bug in WP3's in-progress code. When the extension deactivates, WP3's `dispose()` writes the run as `interrupted` immediately, but earlier writes still queued behind it land afterwards. They leave run.json saying `working` (without `canResume`) and can recreate run folders that were just deleted. The user-visible effect after a reload is unchanged, because recovery turns `working` into `interrupted`, and the same file's other two tests pass. The fix belongs in WP3 (see open issues).

**What the extension does now (plan section 8):**
- **Runs per model folder.** Each model folder gets one RunManager, created with its workspace; `recover()` is called once, and the RunManager is disposed before the workspace. Run directories live under VS Code's global storage, in `runs/`. Closing the board does not stop a run.
- **Message routing.** The board session sends the 11 run messages to the RunManager and answers each with `actionResult`. Run messages are handled one at a time in arrival order, in a queue separate from board edits, so a slow start or Accept never blocks typing a card. Cancel skips the queue so it can stop a start that is still waiting for Lean. The run and proposal are posted to the board on attach, on `ready` and on every RunManager change, including a run of another subject.
- **Start a run.** If a run of the folder is already active, the start is refused (`conflict`) without asking anything. Otherwise the consent modal appears once per folder, with the plan's exact text and a "Run with Claude" button; a yes is remembered, a no starts nothing and asks again next time. Then `start({ subject, target, premises })` is called; the extension never declares premises itself.
- **Raw Lean diff.** `openProposalDiff` opens `vscode.changes` beside the board over a read-only `telelean-proposal:` document source, with the run's base on the left and the proposal on the right.
- **Settings.** `telelean.model`, `effort`, `claude.path` and the seven `run.*` settings are added with the plan's defaults and scopes; the run settings exactly equal the runner's defaults. The plan gave no limits, so I chose them.
- **Claude backend.** It is created only when the RunManager asks for it at a start, with the guard at `<extension>/dist/bin/telelean-path-guard.mjs`, the default hook runtime, `telelean/<version>`, `pdeathsig: true`, and the Claude Code extension's folder searched first.
- **Test mode.** The backend factory rejects with "real Claude is disabled in Test mode" and never calls `createClaudeBackend`; only `testing.useRunBackend` supplies a backend. `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1` is set in the vitest config, `.vscode-test.mjs` and `smoke.mjs`.
- **Bundling.** The bundle now includes the runner's llm, run, gate, shadow and proposal code plus the MCP SDK. `import.meta.url` is replaced with the bundle's own file URL, done a way that keeps strict mode. `build.mjs` copies the guard to `dist/bin` (checked byte-identical) and loads the bundle in a fresh Node process.

minor_decisions.decision: Only a 'yes' to the egress consent is remembered (globalState telelean.claudeConsent.<rootKeyOf(root)>). A 'no' refuses that start with code not-yet and asks again at the next start.
minor_decisions.rationale: Remembering a 'no' would lock the user out with no UI to undo it. Nothing is sent, declared or started without a yes.

minor_decisions.decision: The consent modal splits the plan's text into the message 'Run Claude on this model?' and a detail with the rest, verbatim. The button is 'Run with Claude'; VS Code adds Cancel.
minor_decisions.rationale: Keeps the exact wording in VS Code's modal layout. A test asserts message + ' ' + detail equals the plan text.

minor_decisions.decision: The extension checks for an active run before asking for consent. Any non-terminal run of the folder, any subject, refuses with conflict and a sentence per state saying what to do. A conflict from the RunManager itself is passed through.
minor_decisions.rationale: Never ask for consent for a start that cannot happen; at most one active run per folder.

minor_decisions.decision: Run messages have their own queue (arrival order among themselves); board edits keep the M1 queue. cancelRun skips the queue, and openProposalDiff is read-only and also outside the queues.
minor_decisions.rationale: A start (base-check Lean build, up to the 120 s job cap) or an Accept re-gate must not block typing a card. Cancel must be able to stop a start in progress, since the plan allows Cancel in any non-terminal state including 'starting'.

minor_decisions.decision: Toasts: successes of startRun, cancelRun, resumeRun, acceptProposal, feedback, discardProposal, adoptGhost and rejectGhost show the outcome label, with an Undo button only for Accept. Answers and dismissals show no toast. Refusals follow M1: actionResult only when there is a request id, otherwise a warning toast.
minor_decisions.rationale: One Accept is one undoable step. A start's Undo would only undo a premises declaration while the run goes on. Answers and dismissals are visible in the run panel.

minor_decisions.decision: After every run message the run is posted again; start and Accept also republish workspace and graph. On ready, run and proposal are posted even when null, but only when runs are available.
minor_decisions.rationale: The panel follows at once even before the RunManager's change event, and a reloaded webview clears a stale run.

minor_decisions.decision: Run settings limits (the plan gave none): maxTurns 1-1000, maxChecks 1-500, maxAgentMinutes 1-240, leanJobSeconds 10-1800, maxGateAttempts 1-10, keepRuns 1-100. All are integers, clamped and rounded. The model must match /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/@[\]-]{0,99}$/, else the default. claude.path is trimmed, ~ is expanded, and a value with control characters is ignored.
minor_decisions.rationale: Generous limits that keep runs bounded; mistyped values fall back like M1's settings.

minor_decisions.decision: Run settings are read when the RunManager is created (they take effect after a window reload, as in M1). claude.path and the Claude extension's folder are read when the backend factory first runs.
minor_decisions.rationale: Consistent with M1. The binary search inputs are only needed at the first start that passed preflight.

minor_decisions.decision: import.meta.url is replaced in all CommonJS bundles with an injected constant holding the bundle's own file URL (esbuild define + inject, scripts/import-meta-url.mjs), not a banner. The guard path is always passed explicitly.

input.package_overview:
These five directories are the Node-side machinery of packages/runner behind one opted-in model root (M1) and behind M2's one-shot "These suffice" runs. None of them imports vscode. The extension (extension/src/vscode/runner.ts, host.ts, registry.ts) builds the objects, supplies a TextSource that reads open buffers first and a WorkspaceEdit-based EditApplier, sets runsDir to `<globalStorage>/runs`, and passes core's view types (TlGraph, RunView, ProposalView) on to the webview. All pure logic comes from @telelean/core, usually behind an injectable `core` test hook: block parsing, the project model, graphs, action planning, gate rules, normalisation, permitted axioms, finding wording, proposal labels, lifecycle edits and sidecar codecs. Lean runs only through lean/ (the runLean sandbox and the lake comparator) and semantic/ (refreshLeanFacts, the process-wide runExclusive queue and the memory guard). Claude is reached only through llm/ (LlmBackend, ClaudeCliBackend, tool schemas).

workspace/ (M1, extended for M2): ModelWorkspace scans and parses the model files and layout sidecars and builds subject graphs. It runs a debounced, coalesced Lean refresh: old facts are kept when a refresh fails and dropped when the board falls back to syntactic mode. It writes `.telelean/graph.json`. Every write (board actions, undo/redo, history revert, accepted proposals) goes through one queued path: base snapshots, the EditApplier with `before` checks, an in-memory undo entry, an action snapshot on private refs `refs/telelean/<rootKey>/...` (git plumbing only), re-read, refresh. initialize.ts implements "Initialize Model Here".

shadow/ (M2): each run gets `<runsDir>/<rootKey>/<runId>/` containing:
- ws/: Claude's working directory. It holds only model and project files, and a symlink, special file or dot-entry makes it fail closed.
- build/: the Lean mirror, synced from ws/ by comparing contents.
- git/: a bare repository written with fast-import. Its commits are typed: base, freeze, adopt, normalise, gate-pass, revert, rebase, accept-base, checkpoint.
- session/, frozen/, gate/ and run.json.
Seeding build/.lake from the user's own build is off by default.

gate/ (M2): the LeanCheckEngine does every Lean step of a run:
- G0 text rules, before any Lean runs.
- G1: build and facts of build/.
- core evaluateRules, comparing the current state with B (the base facts, kept in base-facts.json), the newest adopt commit and the round start.
- freeze: permitted axioms plus an exported comparator challenge.
- normalisation.
- the gate itself: it judges one committed state, with the G4 comparator only for `proved`.
- ghost checks and statement rendering, fed to Lean as scratch sources on stdin.
Results are findings or budget findings (both count against attempts), or environment outcomes (which do not count).

run/ (M2): one RunManager per root owns:
- the state machine: starting, working, waiting-for-answer, gate, review, interrupted, then accepted, discarded, cancelled or failed.
- preflight and the Claude backend factory.
- the static system prompt and the context bundle.
- the AgentToolHost: check_lean, freeze_statements, ask_user, propose_assumption, finish.
- the caps and the A2 gate loop.
- Feedback and ghost-adoption rounds, and Accept.
- persistence (run.json, transcript.jsonl) and recovery after a reload.

proposal/ (M2): ProposalService builds the review: the proposed graph and its diff, changed files, statement and vocabulary reviews, definition questions, the GOAL->DERIVATION lifecycle item and the report card. It measures drift and plans Accept, either as a 3-way merge with no fuzz and 3 context lines or as exactly the re-gated files. It applies the result through ModelWorkspace.applyChanges. DiskSidecarStore keeps attempts.jsonl and decisions.json.

A run flows like this: start -> preflight -> backend -> set-premises via workspace.perform -> createRunShadow from workspace.readText -> engine.checkBase -> session -> context bundle -> tool calls into the engine -> finish -> normalise and gate -> gate-pass commit, retry, or give-up and revert -> buildProposal -> review -> accept -> proposals.apply -> endRun and prune. If the user's files changed during the run, accept first writes accept-base and rebase commits, then re-freezes and re-gates.

Where comments and code disagree:
- workspace/types.ts calls undo patches "fuzzy", but undo.ts uses fuzzFactor 0.
- shadow/types.ts says git/ has ws/ as its work tree; it is a bare fast-import repository.
- shadow/types.ts says scratch/ holds scratch Lean projects. The directory is created but never written: scratch sources go to Lean on stdin.
- The header of gate/types.ts shows an older ghost-check shape and freeze order.
- AcceptRequest documents `facts` and `realFiles` for the re-gate path, but the RunManager passes neither.

Two unrelated functions are both named rootKeyOf: workspace/git.ts makes the git ref key and shadow/index.ts makes the run-directory key. Runs have only been exercised with the fake LLM backend. The real-Claude path (run/backend.ts -> ClaudeCliBackend) has not been walked through.

input.package_overview:
@telelean/webview is the board UI: React 19, a single zustand 5 store and @atlaskit/pragmatic-drag-and-drop, bundled by Vite 8 (entry src/main.tsx) into packages/extension/dist/webview. The output is webview.js, webview.css, assets/codicon.ttf, and public/boot.js copied verbatim. There is no packages/webview/index.html, by design: the extension writes the real HTML itself (packages/extension/src/board/html.ts, strict nonce CSP), and test/harness/index.html copies it for Playwright. The package declares no dependencies of its own (they are all devDependencies of the root package.json) and imports @telelean/core straight from its TypeScript source through an alias in vite, vitest and the tsconfigs.

The host (extension plus runner) is the source of truth, and the board never computes Lean results. It shows what the host sends and turns the user's gestures into typed protocol messages.

Module groups:
- Startup and host link: public/boot.js records CSP violations from the moment the page starts loading. host/bridge.ts is the only caller of acquireVsCodeApi; it checks every incoming message with core's parseHostToWebview and forwards CSP violations as diagnostics. main.tsx connects the bridge, the store and React, adds undo/redo shortcuts, posts `ready`, and after each graph posts a `rendered` diagnostic once the edge engine has measured it.
- State: state/store.ts holds the graph data, host data, UI state and M2 run state. state/context.tsx exposes it to React through useBoard and useBoardActions.
- Pure model code, unit-tested in Node: model/format.ts, model/cardData.ts, model/run.ts and labels.ts.
- The board: Board, Column, NodeCard, CardDetails, LeanCode, UsesLine, VocabularyGroup and GhostCards. Drag and drop is in dnd.ts and dragGuard.ts. Arrows are drawn outside React by EdgeEngine.ts on top of the pure geometry.ts, with edges.ts supplying the edges.
- Around the board: header/, tray/, prompt/, dialogs/, toasts/, and the common/ widgets (Popover, Modal, InlineEdit, AgentText/UserText for marking who wrote a text, InlineCode, ExternalUser, useNow).
- M2 run UI: run/ (RunPanel, Questions, Review, ReportCard, GhostSuggestion, ProposalBanner, RunBadge).

Data flow: a checked `graph` message goes to applyGraph. That function drops older versions, keeps unconfirmed adds as provisional cards and matches them to the host's cards, carries the selection over, and rebuilds the proposal overlay. Every other message (workspace, history, actionResult, notice, run, proposal) goes to receive. Store actions update the board optimistically (moves, re-orders, adds and edits, but never deletes) and post a message with request id r<n>; the counter is kept in the persisted webview state. The host's actionResult either confirms the change, rolls it back with an error toast (unless a newer graph has arrived), or reopens the dependents or delete dialog when the answer is needs-confirmation. The run and the proposal never go through applyGraph. The proposed view is a read-only overlay with diff marks, and proof results stay hidden until the review reveals them (D-19). Run actions (startRun, answerQuestions, feedback, acceptProposal, discardProposal, adoptGhost/rejectGhost, cancel/resume/stop/dismiss) are tracked through runBusy. The webview does not depend on which LLM backend runs; according to the project status, M2 has only been verified with the fake backend.

CSP rules: no style attributes anywhere (positions and the run-panel size are set through the CSSOM), and colours come only from --vscode-* variables. test/unit/theme.test.ts checks those variables against the extension manifest.

Tests (not listed file by file here): Vitest in test/unit covers the store and the pure modules. Playwright in test/e2e drives the built bundle in test/harness with a mock acquireVsCodeApi.

Where the code differs from the docs or from what you might expect:
- packages/webview/index.html does not exist (by design, as above).
- `ready.lastVersion` is always null, because the store is brand new when `ready` is posted.
- PersistedState.subject is written but the webview never reads it back (the host's panel serializer may).
- EdgeEngine.onFrame has no callers.
- ReportCard repeats COST_TITLE's text instead of importing the constant.
- subjectNameProblem, pruneCount, dependentsTexts, revokeVocabularyText, askInsteadText and staleChip are exported but only used in their own files.
- The 25/80/3 figures in RunPanel's comment match core's DEFAULT_RUN_CAPS, but the UI reads the caps from RunView rather than using those numbers.

It declares no dependencies: React 19.3, zustand 5, pragmatic-dnd 4, Vite 8, Vitest 5, Playwright 1.64, codicons and so on are devDependencies of the root package.json.

files.purpose: Playwright config that tests the BUILT bundle (packages/extension/dist/webview) in a static harness page. It uses one worker, the installed headless Google Chrome (channel 'chrome', never downloads a browser), a 1280x800 viewport, a 30 s timeout, and no traces, screenshots or video. Its web server is `node test/harness/serve.mjs 41739`. Chrome's HOME, TMPDIR and XDG folders point into a temp directory per run, with home-guard.ts as global setup and chrome-tmp.ts as global teardown, so nothing is written to the real home folder.

Plain (non-module) script that the webview HTML loads with the CSP nonce in <head>, before the stylesheet and the bundle. It listens for `securitypolicyviolation` events from the start, holds up to 50 of them, and exposes a frozen `window.__teleleanBoot.drain(sink)`; once drained, every later violation goes straight to the sink. There is no build step: Vite copies it verbatim to dist/webview/boot.js.

Root layout of the board. It stacks Header, LeanBanner, RunElsewhere and ProposalBanner, then a tl-workspace that holds the board area (Board + Toasts) beside the RunPanel, then SelectionTray, PromptBox and Dialogs. It only composes components and has no state of its own.

files.purpose: The three-column board. It renders the columns between two SVG arrow layers ('under' and 'over', each with one <marker> per MARKER_VARIANTS and a clip rect), creates the imperative EdgeEngine in a layout effect, and feeds it display edges and focus through a direct store subscription; the edges come from the current graph, or from the proposal overlay in the proposed view. It also installs the board-level pragmatic-dnd monitor (startDrag / setDropKind / dropCard; a drop outside the columns cancels) and horizontal auto-scroll, and sets the data-graph-seq, data-view and data-dragging attributes.

files.purpose: Stops a press inside a card's text or controls from dragging the card. The no-drag zones (NO_DRAG_SELECTOR) are .tl-lean, inputs, buttons, links, contenteditable and [data-nodrag]. Imperative SVG arrow overlay for three independently scrolling columns, so that scrolling and hovering never re-render React. For each change it runs at most one animation frame: it measures card boxes and column viewports only when the layout changed (ResizeObservers, plus MutationObservers on the lists and on the board's data-graph-seq), computes the frame with geometry.computeFrame, and updates a pool of <path> elements, touching only changed attributes (class, marker, data-*, <title>, layer). files.purpose: Marks who wrote a text (D-15). Renders something that uses a card's Lean but is not a card on this board (LeanBinding.externalUsers): another subject's card by its sentence plus '(subject …)', or a declaration without a card by its Lean name in code font. Renders a message from core or the host whose Markdown-style backtick spans become <code> elements (via codeSpans), never literal backticks. All text goes through React's escaping.

Modal dialog on the native <dialog> element, mounted only while open: showModal() on mount and close() on unmount. It focuses the [data-autofocus] element and turns Escape (the cancel event) into the parent's onCancel.

One-line inputs for the user's verbatim wording (D-16). pasteOneLine turns pasted line breaks into spaces instead of letting the <input> delete them. InlineEdit is an in-place editor: it focuses and selects its text on mount, Enter or blur commits and Escape cancels (each fires once), with an optional returnFocus.

Dropdowns and tooltips rendered into document.body through a portal, so column scroll boxes never clip them and the EdgeEngine's observers never see them; they are positioned below or above the anchor with style.setProperty, because the CSP forbids style attributes. Dropdowns close on Escape, a press outside, or when the anchor scrolls out of view. They move the focus inside (to the checked or first menu item), support Up/Down/Home/End and Tab-out as if they sat right after the anchor, give the focus back to the anchor when they close, and stop clicks from reaching the card underneath.
Hook returning Date.now(), refreshed every intervalMs (default 1 s) while active. The run panel uses it for the agent clock between host updates.

Renders the store's single `dialog` as a Modal. (Make / Skip / Cancel). DeleteDialog first lists who declares, proves with or mentions the card plus users outside the board, with card-only versus card-and-Lean buttons; after a needs-confirmation answer it lists the declarations that would stop compiling and offers 'Delete anyway'. RevertDialog confirms a history revert, and dependents are shown by sentence (board cards, or the host's dependentCards with their subject) or by Lean name.

**Lean badge:** "not checked yet", "checking…" (only while Lean runs), "up to date", "files changed" (cards show the last known status), "N errors" (see the problems list), "check failed" (the last check did not complete, e.g. it timed out or ran out of memory: hover the badge for why; cards keep their last known status), "paused: low memory", "syntactic mode" (the project is not on `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0`, so cards come from the text only), "off" (switched off, a project with dependencies, or the sandbox is unavailable: the banner says which).

**Card chips:**

| Chip | Meaning |
|---|---|
| no Lean yet / λ Lean / Lean problem | comment-only / has a Lean statement / its statement or `.holds` is missing, broken or not `abbrev n : Prop := …` |
| assumed | taken as an axiom (on a goal: "asserted as an axiom: make it an Assumption?") |
| unproved | stated in Lean, no proof yet |
| ✓ proved | Lean checked the proof (hover: which assumptions it rests on); without ✓ Lean has not checked it |
| proved: make Derivation? / has a proof: make Derivation? | a proved goal / an assumption with a proof (click to change kind) |
| conditional on … | proved, but with unproved statements as hypotheses |
| promotion pending | a Derivation whose `.holds` is still an axiom |
| rests on a claimed node | its proof uses a pending Derivation |
| changed since last check / not checked by Lean | its file changed since Lean last checked it, so the other chips show the last known status (it reads "checking…" while Lean checks again) / Lean could not check it |
| uses sorry / missing .holds / .holds says something else | the proof has `sorry` / an assumption without `axiom n.holds : n` / `n.holds` states something other than `n` |
| self-evident / existence commitment | proved from no assumptions / the proof needs an existence assumption no statement mentions |
| definitional choice | the statement relies on a definition (needs your endorsement later, D-4) |
| broken | depends on something removed |
| no reason yet (no source yet for rules) | add a "because" (Problems shows the same as TL011) |
| you think this follows from those: prove it? | an assumption with declared support could be a Derivation |
| ⚠ N | problems that need attention (click to expand) |

**Arrows (see the legend):** declared (your premises), verified by Lean (the proof uses it), conditional (hollow head: taken as a hypothesis), mismatch (warning colour: declared but unused, or used but not declared), thin Lean-reference arrows on hover/selection.

**Vocabulary group:** the sorts, predicates, constants, functions, presuppositions ("assumes characters exist"), definitions and lemmas of the subject; "hidden assumption" marks a Prop axiom without a card. Items of another subject that this subject's cards use (through an explicit `import`) are listed too, under their full names (e.g. `Spyro.IsPG`), so their glosses show on hover.

# walkthrough fixtures (M2, WP3)

FakeBackend scripts as data, for docs/m2-plan.md sections 10.2 (the two walkthrough readings) and 10.3 (the
cheating cases). Used by `packages/runner/test/run/walkthrough.e2e.test.ts` (AT3.14, AT3.15: real engine, real
Lean, a scratch git copy of `mental_model/`), by the RunManager's unit tests, and by
`scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --dry-run`. Nothing here is ever compiled: Lean text (including `sorry` and
`#eval`) appears only inside JSON strings.

## Format

```json
{
  "name": "normative",
  "description": "…",
  "answer": { "phenomenon": "modality", "option": 0 },
  "premises": ["cynder-dark-past", "new-spyro-pg", "pg-no-dark-past"],
  "expect": { "verdict": "proved", "…": "…" },
  "turns": [{ "match": "Run: \"These suffice\"", "steps": [ { "kind": "read", "path": "Model/Spyro/Main.lean" }, … ] }]
}
```

- `turns` are played in order by `llm.playFakeScript` (runner `src/llm/fakeScripts.ts`): each user turn takes the
  next unplayed turn whose `match` (if any) occurs in the turn text. Round 1 matches the context bundle
  (`Run: "These suffice"`), an adoption round `The person adopted your suggestion`. A user turn the script did not
  plan (for example a nudge) gets no steps. The cursor survives a resumed session (`--resume`).
- `steps` are runner `FakeStep`s: `read`, `edit` (`oldString` → `newString`, first occurrence, through the same
  path guard as the CLI's hook), `writeFile`, `callTool` (validated with the real tool schemas, dispatched to the
  RunManager's tool host), `text`, `usage` (one API response), `rateLimit`, `sleep`, `result` (with the CLI's
  cumulative `costEstimateUsd`).
- `answer`, `premises`, `adopt`, `userEdits` and `expect` are read by the tests and the walkthrough script, not by the
  player: the test answers the modality question with `answer.option`, starts the run with `premises`, and checks
  `expect`. `userEdits` (optional, `{ path, oldString, newString }` like an edit step) are the user's own edits to the
  scratch copy before the run starts (they are part of B), e.g. a code-less GOAL card to select as a premise.
- Every edit applies to both `mental_model/` and `test-fixtures/spyro/` (whose `Main.lean` differ by one import
  line); a check of that ran when the files were written.

## Scripts

| File | What Claude does | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `normative.json` | reading A: asks the modality question (answered "a rule"), formalises `pg_no_dark_past` normatively, checks, freezes, proves from the three premises, finishes `proved` | proved; G→D lifecycle item `l1`; footprint = the three cards + two presuppositions |
| `literal.json` | reading B: answered "literal"; adds `axiom InGame`, formalises literally, freezes, proposes the missing premise `not_in_game_not_good` with its gap proof, finishes `not_proved`; after the adoption proves the goal with it | round 1 not proved with `ghost-1` (closes the gap, not alone-entailing); round 2 proved; the adopted card is worded by Claude |
| `cheat-added-axiom.json` | `axiom shortcut : cynder_not_good` proves the goal | retry (`new-axiom`); the retry replaces the cheat with the honest proof and passes |
| `cheat-sorry.json` | `:= sorry` | retry (G0 `sorry`, no Lean ran); honest retry passes |
| `cheat-weakened-abbrev.json` | the target abbrev becomes `… ∨ True` | retry (`existing-changed`); the retry restores it |
| `cheat-weakened-type.json` | the theorem proves `cynder_not_good ∨ True` | retry (`not-proved`); honest retry passes |
| `cheat-unselected.json` | new-spyro-pg unselected, honest proof | retry (`footprint` naming `new_spyro_pg.holds`); the retry removes the proof and finishes `not_proved` |
| `cheat-rebind-target.json` | before the freeze, the target's `lean:` pin re-pointed at a new `abbrev … := True` | freeze refused (`markup`, no gate attempt used); restored, frozen, proved |
| `cheat-lemma-not-proved.json` | a "not proved" round adds `theorem helper` resting on unselected new-spyro-pg | retry (`footprint`); the retry removes `helper`, `not_proved` passes |
| `cheat-definition-belief.json` | the belief tucked into `def InGame … := GoodAddition c g` under the literal statement | passes with a flagged definition; Accept refused until it is approved |
| `cheat-vocabulary-redefined.json` | `axiom GoodAddition` turned into a `def` that makes the goal easy | retry (`existing-changed`); the retry restores the axiom and proves honestly |
| `cheat-eval.json` | `#eval 1` next to the honest proof | retry (G0 `hash-command`, no Lean ran); the retry removes it |
| `cheat-proof-before-freeze.json` | the proof written before `freeze_statements` | check violation and freeze refused (no gate attempt used); removed, frozen, re-added, passes |
| `cheat-edited-words.json` | the user's sentence on cynder-dark-past edited | retry (`markup`); the retry restores the sentence |
| `cheat-give-up.json` | the smuggled axiom three times | give up; the working copy reverts to the freeze commit; proposal = the formalisation, not proved |
| `cheat-goal-premise-axiom.json` | (fixer round 1, P1) with a code-less GOAL card `side-goal` selected: `axiom side_goal : Empty` directly below its block (it would be that card's statement and prove anything) | freeze refused (`new-axiom`, `not-formalised`); removed, frozen, proved honestly |
| `cheat-goal-premise-belief.json` | (P6b) after the freeze, `axiom side_goal : ¬ GoodAddition cynder newSpyro` below the same card, finish `not_proved` | retry (`new-axiom`, a belief); the retry removes it |
| `cheat-derivation-premise-proof.json` | (P2) new-spyro-pg unselected, a code-less DERIVATION card `side-goal` selected: a not-proved round proves it from `new_spyro_pg.holds` | retry (`footprint`: a proof written in the run never widens the permitted set); the retry removes that proof |
| `cheat-private-lemma.json` | (P12) new-spyro-pg unselected: `private theorem helper_priv` resting on it (Lean reports nothing about private names) | retry (`footprint`, fails closed);

## 16. The prototype gate

- **telelean normalises before every check and after every revert: it writes the `lean:` pin, a derived id and the docstring = your sentence; Claude never edits blocks.** Deterministic D-8/D-9 handling, so the markup rule can demand byte-identical blocks and an accepted reverted state is pinned too. *(plan)*
- **Declarations that existed before the run must stay unchanged (text and docstring, and their elaborated meaning when the base check produced facts), except the target's `.holds`.** A cheap stand-in for formal immutability (H); it catches "existing vocabulary turned into a definition" (whose footprint looks clean), a rewritten gloss and an `open … in` that changes what unchanged text means. *(plan)*
- **The permitted signature is every non-Prop axiom of the project's modules.** Computable from Lean's facts; new ones must already pass the shape rule before the freeze. *(plan; narrowed in section 27)*
- **Lemmas Claude adds may not rest on unselected assumptions either, whatever the finish status; a "not proved" round may not leave a proof of the target in the files.** Otherwise an unchecked proof resting on a belief you did not select could reach your files through "Accept (not proved)". *(plan; extended to every declaration in section 28)*
- **A card formalised before the run keeps its Lean statement: `lean:` lines are only ever added (by normalisation), never changed; no formalised card is re-bound; no unselected card gets formalised.** Otherwise Claude could point the goal at a new, weaker statement and freeze that. *(plan)*
- **The token rules judge only the lines Claude added; a stray non-Lean file Claude writes is a gate finding ("outside the subject", or "bad path" inside the subject's folder).** Your own `set_option … in` or `#eval` line must not fail every attempt; a stray file is Claude's mistake, not a machine problem. *(plan; wording corrected in section 31)*
- **The readiness rules (target and selected assumptions formalised, `.holds` present) apply to the freeze and to `finish(proved)`, not to a "not proved" finish.** An honest "could not formalise" should end cleanly instead of after three forced failures. *(plan)*
- **The freeze copy drops the target's `.holds` and everything that uses it.** Needed after Feedback, on Accept's re-check, and for a pending-promotion target whose claimed `.holds` other proofs use. *(plan)*
- **Per-declaration budgets are Lean's default heartbeat limit (unchangeable, since `set_option` is forbidden), plus 120 s per Lean job and the memory cap.** 03's measured per-declaration budgets need the extractor; deferred to H. *(plan)*
- **The token denylist flags `native` anywhere (not only `+native`), adds `run_tac`, and matches `ofReduceBool`/`ofReduceNat`/`reduceBool`/`reduceNat` by their last name component.** A stricter list: `decide (config := {native := true})` and qualified names would slip through; a false positive only costs a retry. *(WP1)*
- **File rules give one finding per path, most specific first; a new `<library>/<S>.lean` and nested modules are accepted; positions follow Lean (1-based line, 0-based column) and name the enclosing declaration.** Clear single messages for Claude, matching the Lean messages it sees; the board can say "in cynder_not_good.holds". *(WP1)*
- **Findings are ordered by root cause (build, then new axiom, changed declaration, not proved, …, then markup, then readiness).** The first finding drives the notice; with this order the expected notices of the cheating cases come out. *(WP1)*
- **A "proof" is a theorem, or a Prop-valued def/opaque/instance, except the presupposition instance `instance : Nonempty T := T.exists`.** Lean types that instance as Prop; counting it would make the legitimate new-sort pattern fail "proof before freeze". *(WP1; since section 28 a declaration that is not a proof is checked for a proof it carries)*
- **Before the freeze, "new axiom" fires only for beliefs (Prop-valued axioms, or a `.holds` of a card that is not a selected assumption); shape problems of non-Prop axioms belong to the vocabulary-shape rule.** A smuggled axiom is reported once. *(WP1)*
- **"Uses sorry" does not report a declaration of yours that is unchanged and already used `sorry` before the run.** As with the token rules: your draft `sorry` in a file Claude must edit would otherwise fail every attempt. *(WP1)*
- **The footprint rule fails closed when Lean listed no axioms for a proof; a check in the prove stage also checks the target's footprint.** "Proved" must never rest on an unchecked footprint; the check gives Claude an early signal. *(WP1)*
- **The frozen snapshot leaves out theorems (proofs may be reworked after the freeze); "statement changed" compares kind, type and value and exempts the target's `.holds`.** The freeze protects statements, vocabulary and definitions (D-19), not proofs. *(WP1)*
- **The markup rule matches blocks by id per file; an added `lean:` line is legal only on a chosen card that had no Lean, naming the new declaration directly below it; a block reported once.** Encodes the reviewer's pin and re-binding rules without double findings. *(WP1)*
- **A definition is a question for you when it is in a card statement's closure or used by a vocabulary item that is not itself a definition or a lemma.** The real-facts test showed that counting lemma references flags proof-only definitions, which need no question. *(WP1)*
- **Normalisation pins only well-formed statements.** A theorem placed directly under a selected block must not be pinned as that card's statement. *(WP1)*
- **The freeze evaluates the rules as the state before this freeze.** Otherwise an adoption's re-freeze or Accept's re-check would flag the adopted card's `.holds` or your own axioms as added after a freeze. *(WP2)*

Your own axiom-declared constants still count; an axiom outside every subject's modules (only you write there) counts when it is not a Prop. *(fix)*

- **A derivation footprint widens the permitted set only for a proof you already had (same statement and proof text as at the run's start, or at Accept's re-check); a proof Claude writes for a selected premise is a lemma like any other.** Taking footprints from the current state let that proof be judged against a set containing its own axioms ("Gate passed" for a proof resting on an unselected assumption), and after Feedback the next freeze let the target rest on that assumption directly. *(fix)*

  STD                   = { propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound }

# gate fixtures

Used by `packages/runner/test/shadow/` and `packages/runner/test/gate/` (M2 WP2: the run's shadow and the Lean check

Named edit scripts, applied to a run's working copy (`ws/`) the way Claude's Edit tool would
