Each has **Show card** (when it belongs to a card) and a `file:line` button that opens the file. ### 2.2.7 Subjects - **Picker.** "subject: [Spyro ▾]" lists the model's subjects with their card counts. - **New subject.** **New subject…** takes a capitalised identifier of at most 64 characters, not already taken. It writes `Model/.lean` and `Model//{Vocabulary,Inbox,Main}.lean`, adds `import Model.` to `Model.lean`, and switches the board to the new subject. - **Rules.** - A board shows one subject at a time. - Card ids are unique across subjects. - Undo and History work per subject. - If the shown subject disappears (an Undo of its creation, a revert), the board switches to the first remaining one and says so. - The subject is remembered across reloads. ### 2.2.8 Selection and the tray - **Selecting.** A click selects one card, replacing the selection. Ctrl/Cmd+click, or Space on a focused card, toggles a card in the selection. - **The tray** shows "N selected", the premise chips, a turnstile ⊢ and a target slot. - **Target.** The card chosen with ⊢ on a premise chip; without that, the single selected Goal. - **Chips.** Each has ⊢ ("Make this the target") and × ("remove"). - **Presuppositions.** "+ presupposes:" chips show the existence presuppositions of the selected statements; clicking one highlights it. - **Buttons.** **Clear** and the run buttons (2.4.1). - **Proposed view.** In the read-only proposed view, clicks never change the selection. ### 2.2.9 Keyboard | Where | Keys | |---|---| | Anywhere | Tab moves between cards and buttons. Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes (not while typing in a field or while a dialog is open) | | Focused card | Enter expands or collapses it, Space selects or deselects it, F2 edits the sentence, Delete opens the delete dialog, Alt+Up/Down moves it one place in its column | | Dropdowns (subject, History, Problems, "uses:") | opening one moves the focus into it; Up, Down, Home and End move between items; Escape or choosing an item returns the focus to the button that opened it | | Dialogs | native modal dialogs: the focus is trapped, Escape cancels, and Cancel has the initial focus on every destructive dialog | | A\|D\|G switch | Left and Right move between Assumption, Derivation and Goal | ### 2.2.10 Toasts, provenance and theming - **Toasts.** - At most three at a time, at the bottom of the board area. - Info toasts stay 6 s, warnings 10 s, errors 15 s; a toast with Undo stays at least 10 s. - **Undo** appears only on the newest undoable toast, and only while Undo would revert exactly that action. - Identical messages are merged. - **Provenance.** Everything Claude wrote appears in italics with a "Claude" marker ("(Claude's words)", "(Claude's wording)"), never in the style of your own words. That covers its messages, questions and options, suggestions, summaries, and the glosses of new vocabulary. - **Theme colours.** Six colours can be overridden through `workbench.colorCustomizations`, with defaults for dark, light and both high-contrast themes: - `telelean.kindAssumption` - `telelean.kindDerivation` - `telelean.kindGoal` - `telelean.formalizedAura` - `telelean.vocabulary` - `telelean.highlight` The board follows VS Code's reduced-motion preference. ## 2.3 Editing the model without AI (M1) ### 2.3.1 Every board action | Action | Gesture | What is written | Undo / History entry | |---|---|---|---| | Add a card | A\|D\|G box | a comment block in `Model//Inbox.lean` | yes / "add" | | Edit the sentence | **Edit** or F2 (Enter saves, Esc cancels) | `natural_name:`. A docstring equal to the old sentence follows it; a formalised card gets its `lean:` pin | yes / "edit" | | Edit the reason | **Add why / Edit why**, or the "no reason yet" chip; empty removes it | `rationale:` | yes / "edit" | | Stance, source | chips in the expanded card | `stance:` / `source:` | yes / "edit" | | Re-order | drag within a column, or Alt+Up/Down | `.telelean/subjects//layout.json` only | yes / no entry of its own (rides along with the next snapshot) | | Change kind | drag to another column, **Make …**, or a "make Derivation?" chip | `type:` plus the D-11 Lean change (2.3.4) | yes / "kind" | | Delete | **Delete**, or the Delete key | the block, and its Lean unless kept; theorem proofs go to `.telelean/subjects//attic/.lean`; the id leaves other cards' `premises:` | yes / "delete" | | New subject | subject picker | the subject's files and an import in `Model.lean` | yes / "new subject" | | Undo / Redo | header buttons, keys, or a toast's Undo | the previous file contents | – / "undo", "redo" | | Revert to a history entry | History → **Revert to this** → **Revert** | the subject's files as they were then | yes / "revert" | | Refresh Lean | badge or command | `.lake/`, `.telelean/graph.json` | no | - **Saving and conflicts.** Edits are saved at once, including any unsaved typing in the same file. telelean checks each file's current text against what it planned. If the file changed meanwhile, the edit is refused: "… changed since telelean planned "…"; nothing was applied". - **Optimistic display.** The board shows adds, moves and edits at once, and rolls them back with an error toast when the host refuses them. ### 2.3.2 Adding cards: the A|D|G box 1. **Kind.** Pick Assumption, Derivation or Goal. 2. **Sentence.** Type one sentence. Pasted line breaks are folded into one line. 3. **Optional second row:** - stance chips (Assumption only); - a "why" field, whose prompt follows the kind and stance: "Why do you believe it?", "Where does the rule come from?", "What are you exploring?", "Why do you think it follows?" or "Why do you care?"; - source chips (Assumption and Derivation). 4. **Add.** Press Enter or **Add assumption/derivation/goal**. **What is written.** A comment-only block (your words, trimmed, no Lean), with an id derived from the sentence and `asserted:` set to today. If `Inbox.lean` is missing, telelean creates it and adds its import. **During a run.** The box keeps working. Its second row folds while the run panel shows, and adding a card switches the board back to Current. ### 2.3.3 Editing and deleting - **Editing.** - The sentence and the reason are edited in place; the focus returns to the card. - Stance and source change with one click. - Ids never change with the sentence. - **Deleting, first dialog.** It lists what refers to the card: declared as a premise by, used by the proofs of, mentioned in the statements of, lemmas without a card, and other subjects' cards. It says "Nothing else refers to it." only when nothing does. The buttons: - **Delete card and its Lean code**, or **Delete card** for a comment-only card; - **Delete card only, keep Lean**. This leaves `axiom …holds` as an unmarked axiom, which the Vocabulary group flags as a hidden assumption; - **Cancel**, which has the focus. - **Deleting, second dialog.** If deleting the Lean code would break other declarations (the host knows this from Lean's facts), nothing is deleted yet. The dialog reopens as "Delete its Lean code too?" and lists those declarations: cards by sentence, another subject's card with "(subject …)", anything else by its Lean name. The buttons: - **Delete anyway**: the listed declarations stop compiling until changed, and Undo brings the code back; - **Delete card only, keep Lean**; - **Cancel**. ### 2.3.4 Changing kind (D-11) Kind changes never rename a statement. Part 3.5 gives the logic. | Change | Lean effect | |---|---| | comment-only card, any change | only `type:` | | Goal → Derivation | none now; the card counts as derived once `theorem n.holds` exists | | Goal or Derivation → Assumption | adds `axiom n.holds : n`, or turns the theorem into that axiom (the proof is archived in the attic). Without a reason, an optional "Why do you hold it?" dialog appears (Skip is fine) | | Assumption → Derivation | the axiom stays; the card shows **promotion pending** until you replace the axiom with a proof | | → Goal | removes `n.holds`. If proofs use it, a dialog offers **Rewrite them to take it as a hypothesis** `(h_n : n)` (needs fresh Lean facts; refused when a user is not a theorem), **Keep them, marked broken**, or **Cancel** | | → Assumption, when `n.holds` takes hypotheses | proofs that pass it arguments must change: "Rewrite them to use it directly" or "Keep them, marked broken" | **How the board previews and confirms:** - **Drop zones.** During a drag, the other columns become labelled drop zones showing the impact, for example "Make Derivation: promotion pending until proved". That text comes from the board's own cards only ("No card on this board uses it"). - **Re-planning with Lean.** The host re-plans the change with Lean's facts across the project. If it finds more dependents (lemmas without a card, other subjects' proofs), it asks again with its own list and says it found more. Your choice then applies to exactly the listed dependents. - **Cancelling a drag.** Dropping a card outside every column cancels it. ### 2.3.5 Declaring premises - **The only gesture.** The only board gesture that writes `premises:` is the tray's **These suffice ▶** or **Add to its premises ▶**, and both start a Claude run (2.4). - **How it is written.** The declaration is written after preflight, as an ordinary undoable action labelled "These suffice: … ← N premises". - **What it refuses.** Premises from another subject, a card supporting itself, and cycles. - **Without Claude.** Edit `premises:` by hand. The host would accept a declare-only message, but the board never sends one. ### 2.3.6 Undo, Redo and History **Undo and Redo.** - 100 steps per subject, kept in memory. They survive closing the board, but not a window reload. - Tooltips name the action ("Undo: Add assumption: …"). - If you edited a file by hand since, Undo reverses only telelean's change, and refuses when that no longer applies ("changed since; use History to revert"). **History** needs git (amendment A3). Each telelean change becomes a commit on private refs: `refs/telelean//subjects/` per subject, and `…/project` for the project files. - **Never touched:** your branches, index, HEAD, remotes and hooks. Nothing is pushed. - **When snapshots are taken:** "Initial state" when a board first loads. Hand edits are snapshotted as "Manual edits" before telelean's next change. - **What a subject's snapshots cover:** its `.lean` files, its `layout.json` and its attic. `attempts.jsonl` and `decisions.json` are not covered. **The History dropdown.** - **Storage line:** "This subject: X · All subjects: Y". This is disk use, not memory. - **Entries:** "time · action · label", 50 at a time, with **Show older entries**. - **Preview** opens a read-only multi-file diff beside the board, titled `History:

I assembled the main report from the six package overviews, the features draft and the theory draft. All 21 fact-check corrections (C1–C21) and the 11 'missing' items (M1–M11) are applied in Part 3. I only read files: nothing was written to the repo or scratch, nothing published, no Lean run. Where to save it: docs/project-report-files.md already exists and calls itself the 'Appendix to docs/project-report.md' (2026-11-02), so the main report should be saved as docs/project-report.md. Part 1 ends with the requested pointer line.

Structure:
- Status summary.
- Part 1: architecture (new). Processes, packages, data flows (refresh, edit/undo/history, a run, Accept), storage table, trust boundaries, departures from the 02/03 design.
- Part 2: features, tightened. Old 2.7/2.8 moved into Appendix A, docs-vs-code consolidated into Appendix B.
- Part 3: Lean system, corrected.
- Appendices A (limitations/open items), B (docs vs code, from all surveys), C (glossary), D (how checked).

Features-draft errors I found by spot-checking the code and fixed:
- Root `npm run build` only type-checks the runner (`noEmit`). Core compiles to an unused `dist/`.
- The run's `scratch/` folder is created but never used; ghost checks are scratch files on Lean's stdin, not 'scratch projects'.
- The check file also uses `type_of%` and runs via `lake env lean --stdin --json`.
- A toast with Undo stays at least 10 s.
- The vocabulary flag 'new' and the 'broken' chip's flag are never set by core.
- The graph.json schema file is named 1.0 while the format is 1.1.
- Accept without drift runs no Lean check.
- After a revert, the proposal is the last passing commit plus normalisation. The re-check does not block.
- Only definition approvals gate Accept. 'Show the proof result now' exists.
- At most one freeze per round, and the check budget is enforced.
- The extension is registered in place (confirmed in ~/.vscode/extensions/extensions.json).

Integrated beyond the theory draft: the last verifier's reuseLeanBuild finding (m2close-verify-2). Lake can trust a compiled module built from another version after a save during an outside build followed by Undo. Per the verifier, this also exposes the board's own facts (an M1 matter). I put it in 3.7 item 5, A.2 item 1 and §2.3.7.

The gate gaps found by the fact-check are now listed as known issues A.2 items 4–6:
- T.holds deletion/conversion;
- the pre-freeze instance blind spot, which also affects the user's own statements;
- freeze discipline holding only per round.

Not verified by me: the test counts (quoted from the verifier); the user-guide 'trash' claim; the theory writer's and fact-checker's Lean outputs (quoted as theirs). Appendix D carries the `p2.lean` process note: the fact-checker confirmed the file is gone.

cheating cases). Used by `packages/runner/test/run/walkthrough.e2e.test.ts` (AT3.14, AT3.15: real engine, real
Lean, a scratch git copy of `mental_model/`), by the RunManager's unit tests, and by
`scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --dry-run`. Nothing here is ever compiled: Lean text (including `sorry` and
`#eval`) appears only inside JSON strings.

## Format

```json
{
  "name": "normative",
  "description": "…",
  "answer": { "phenomenon": "modality", "option": 0 },
  "premises": ["cynder-dark-past", "new-spyro-pg", "pg-no-dark-past"],
  "expect": { "verdict": "proved", "…": "…" },
  "turns": [{ "match": "Run: \"These suffice\"", "steps": [ { "kind": "read", "path": "Model/Spyro/Main.lean" }, … ] }]
}
```

- `turns` are played in order by `llm.playFakeScript` (runner `src/llm/fakeScripts.ts`): each user turn takes the
  next unplayed turn whose `match` (if any) occurs in the turn text. Round 1 matches the context bundle
  (`Run: "These suffice"`), an adoption round `The person adopted your suggestion`. A user turn the script did not
  plan (for example a nudge) gets no steps. The cursor survives a resumed session (`--resume`).
- `steps` are runner `FakeStep`s: `read`, `edit` (`oldString` → `newString`, first occurrence, through the same
  path guard as the CLI's hook), `writeFile`, `callTool` (validated with the real tool schemas, dispatched to the
  RunManager's tool host), `text`, `usage` (one API response), `rateLimit`, `sleep`, `result` (with the CLI's
  cumulative `costEstimateUsd`).
- `answer`, `premises`, `adopt`, `userEdits` and `expect` are read by the tests and the walkthrough script, not by the
  player: the test answers the modality question with `answer.option`, starts the run with `premises`, and checks
  `expect`. `userEdits` (optional, `{ path, oldString, newString }` like an edit step) are the user's own edits to the
  scratch copy before the run starts (they are part of B), e.g. a code-less GOAL card to select as a premise.
- Every edit applies to both `mental_model/` and `test-fixtures/spyro/` (whose `Main.lean` differ by one import
  line); a check of that ran when the files were written.

## Scripts

| File | What Claude does | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `normative.json` | reading A: asks the modality question (answered "a rule"), formalises `pg_no_dark_past` normatively, checks, freezes, proves from the three premises, finishes `proved` | proved; G→D lifecycle item `l1`; footprint = the three cards + two presuppositions |
| `literal.json` | reading B: answered "literal"; adds `axiom InGame`, formalises literally, freezes, proposes the missing premise `not_in_game_not_good` with its gap proof, finishes `not_proved`; after the adoption proves the goal with it | round 1 not proved with `ghost-1` (closes the gap, not alone-entailing); round 2 proved; the adopted card is worded by Claude |
| `cheat-added-axiom.json` | `axiom shortcut : cynder_not_good` proves the goal | retry (`new-axiom`); the retry replaces the cheat with the honest proof and passes |
| `cheat-sorry.json` | `:= sorry` | retry (G0 `sorry`, no Lean ran); honest retry passes |
| `cheat-weakened-abbrev.json` | the target abbrev becomes `… ∨ True` | retry (`existing-changed`); the retry restores it |
| `cheat-weakened-type.json` | the theorem proves `cynder_not_good ∨ True` | retry (`not-proved`); honest retry passes |
| `cheat-unselected.json` | new-spyro-pg unselected, honest proof | retry (`footprint` naming `new_spyro_pg.holds`); the retry removes the proof and finishes `not_proved` |
| `cheat-rebind-target.json` | before the freeze, the target's `lean:` pin re-pointed at a new `abbrev … := True` | freeze refused (`markup`, no gate attempt used); restored, frozen, proved |
| `cheat-lemma-not-proved.json` | a "not proved" round adds `theorem helper` resting on unselected new-spyro-pg | retry (`footprint`); the retry removes `helper`, `not_proved` passes |
| `cheat-definition-belief.json` | the belief tucked into `def InGame … := GoodAddition c g` under the literal statement | passes with a flagged definition; Accept refused until it is approved |
| `cheat-vocabulary-redefined.json` | `axiom GoodAddition` turned into a `def` that makes the goal easy | retry (`existing-changed`); the retry restores the axiom and proves honestly |
| `cheat-eval.json` | `#eval 1` next to the honest proof | retry (G0 `hash-command`, no Lean ran); the retry removes it |
| `cheat-proof-before-freeze.json` | the proof written before `freeze_statements` | check violation and freeze refused (no gate attempt used); removed, frozen, re-added, passes |
| `cheat-edited-words.json` | the user's sentence on cynder-dark-past edited | retry (`markup`); the retry restores the sentence |

# runner-lean fixtures

Used by `packages/runner/test/lean/` (the M0 sandboxed-Lean spike). Base project: `../spyro`.

## `overlays/<stage>/`

Files copied over a fresh shadow of `../spyro` to reproduce a run's stages. Each is a complete
replacement of `Model/Spyro/Main.lean`, so the differences are easy to read with `diff`.

| Stage | What a run would have left | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `formalised` | Phase A done: the normative reading of `pg-no-dark-past` formalised (`abbrev pg_no_dark_past` + `axiom pg_no_dark_past.holds`); the goal has no proof | the frozen snapshot (comparator challenge) |
| `proved` | `formalised` + the honest proof `theorem cynder_not_good.holds` (the same proof as `../spyro/Check/Normative.lean`) | footprint test; comparator case (a), and case (c) with `new-spyro-pg` unselected |
| `weakened` | the goal abbrev itself weakened to `… ∨ True` (same name), then "proved" by `Or.inr trivial` | comparator case (b): caught by the closure comparison |
| `weakened-type` | the goal abbrev untouched, but the theorem stated as `cynder_not_good ∨ True` | comparator case (b'): caught by the statement comparison |
| `smuggled` | a new `axiom shortcut : cynder_not_good` used as the proof | comparator extra case (smuggled axiom) |
| `noisy-build-error` | `proved`, but the proof replaced by a type error, after an `#eval` whose output imitates comparator's own lines (`bwrap: Can't mkdir /root: …`, `Resolving dependencies`) | comparator: a failing build stays "rejected: build-failed", never "could not start" (the `#eval` only prints) |

If `../spyro/Model/Spyro/Main.lean` changes, regenerate these from it (only the lines shown by
`diff ../spyro/Model/Spyro/Main.lean overlays/formalised/Model/Spyro/Main.lean` are telelean's additions).

## `probes/*.lean.txt`

Deliberate sandbox probes (`#eval` code that writes into `$HOME`, lists `$HOME` and `/run`, and tries
DNS, TCP, the D-Bus socket and the abstract X11 socket). They are stored **inert** as `.lean.txt`:
never rename them to `.lean` here and never open them with a Lean server. The tests copy each one
into a sandboxed shadow as `Probe.lean` and elaborate it with `lake env lean` under `runLean`.

### 10.2 The walkthrough scripts (FakeBackend; exact edits, all verified to build, section 0)

Edits use `{ kind: 'edit', path, oldString, newString }` so they apply to both `mental_model/` and `test-fixtures/spyro` (whose Main.lean differ by one import line). The test answers questions through `RunManager.answer` when the `run` event shows them.

**Reading A (normative)**, round 1:
1. `read Model/Spyro/Main.lean`
2. `ask_user` `{ questions: [{ phenomenon: 'modality', question: 'Does "cannot have" state a rule about what PG games should not include (normative), or that a PG game is unable to contain such a character (literal)?', options: [{ label: 'A rule (normative)', consequence: 'A PG game with such a character breaks the rule; it says nothing about what the game contains.' }, { label: 'Impossible (literal)', consequence: 'No PG game contains a character with a dark past at all.' }], claudesGuess: { option: 0 }, affectedNodes: ['pg-no-dark-past'] }] }` → the test answers `{ question: 0, choice: { kind: 'option', option: 0 }, scope: 'run' }`
3. edit Main.lean: old `stance: rule\nasserted: 2026-11-01\n-/\n\n` → new `stance: rule\nasserted: 2026-11-01\n-/\n/-- PG games cannot have characters with dark pasts -/\nabbrev pg_no_dark_past : Prop := ∀ (g : Game) (c : Character), IsPG g → HasDarkPast c → ¬ GoodAddition c g\naxiom pg_no_dark_past.holds : pg_no_dark_past\n\n`
4. `check_lean {}` → ok; 5. `freeze_statements { targets: ['cynder-not-good'] }` → frozen
6. edit Main.lean: old `abbrev cynder_not_good : Prop := ¬ GoodAddition cynder newSpyro\n` → new the same line + `theorem cynder_not_good.holds : cynder_not_good :=\n  pg_no_dark_past.holds newSpyro cynder new_spyro_pg.holds cynder_dark_past.holds\n`
7. `check_lean {}`; 8. `finish { status: 'proved', summary: 'Proved from the three premises under the normative reading.', assumed_without_asking: [] }`; 9. `result`.

**Reading B (literal)**, round 1: steps 1–2 as above, answered with option 1; then
3. edit Vocabulary.lean: old `/-- Cynder -/` → new `/-- is in -/\naxiom InGame : Character → Game → Prop\n/-- Cynder -/`
4. edit Main.lean as A.3 with `¬ InGame c g` instead of `¬ GoodAddition c g`
5. `check_lean`; 6. `freeze_statements`
7. `propose_assumption { natural_name: 'A character who cannot be in a game would not be a good addition to it', lean_statement: '∀ (c : Character) (g : Game), ¬ InGame c g → ¬ GoodAddition c g', why_needed: 'The literal reading only says Cynder cannot be in the game; nothing links being in a game to being a good addition to it.', proof: 'fun h => h cynder newSpyro (pg_no_dark_past.holds newSpyro cynder new_spyro_pg.holds cynder_dark_past.holds)', lean_name: 'not_in_game_not_good' }` → recorded as `ghost-1`
8. `finish { status: 'not_proved', summary: 'Under the literal reading the goal does not follow.', gap: 'Nothing connects being unable to appear in a game with being a good addition to it.', assumed_without_asking: [] }`; `result`.

Expected: gate (gate-other) passes; proposal verdict not-proved, `InGame` in the vocabulary review, ghost-1 `closesGap`, not `aloneEntails`. The test sends `adoptGhost(ghost-1, 'it seems obvious to me')`; round 2 (stage prove, frozen with the ghost selected):

10. `check_lean`; 11. `finish { status: 'proved', … }`; `result`.

### 10.4 Isolation

As M1 section 10: `$TELELEAN_TEST_TMP`, git in scratch repos with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, `ulimit -c 0` where Lean, Chrome or VS Code start, vitest `fileParallelism: false`, runs dirs under scratch. The VS Code smoke uses its isolated user-data dir (so `globalStorage/runs` is inside it) and the FakeBackend: the real ClaudeCliBackend is never constructed in tests except with M0's `fake-claude.mjs` double.

**Quota tripwires (reviewer addition; three independent layers, so one forgotten fake cannot spend quota):**
1. `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1` in every test environment: `packages/runner/vitest.config.ts` (already set), the extension's vitest config and `.vscode-test.mjs` (WP5), and `scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs` and `scripts/smoke-claude.mjs` set it for themselves in dry-run mode. Under it `createClaudeBackend` throws before resolving any binary (unless the test passes `settings.resolve` with fake binaries) and `ClaudeCliBackend.startSession` throws before spawning unless its launcher is `process.execPath` (M0's node double) (WP3, AT3.13). Fixer round 1: any non-empty value other than `0`/`false` arms it; `createClaudeBackend`'s exemption needs both `resolve.home` and `resolve.pathEnv` (a bare `resolve: {}` would scan the real home and PATH); `startSession`'s exemption needs the binary to be a `.mjs`/`.js` test double inside a `test/**/fixtures/` folder as well (`isTestDoubleLaunch`; a JavaScript Claude Code CLI launched with node would otherwise start); runner `test/llm/binary.test.ts`'s check of the user's real binary (`--version` only) runs only with `TELELEAN_ALLOW_REAL_CLAUDE_VERSION=1`. Fixer round 2: `scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs` refuses `--live` at once under every arming value (it refused only `1`), with the rule in `scripts/quota-tripwire.mjs`, which runner `test/run/quotaTripwire.test.ts` keeps equal to `realClaudeDisabled`.
2. The extension in Test mode never calls `createClaudeBackend`: its default backend factory rejects; only `testing.useRunBackend` can supply a backend (WP5, AT5.4).
3. No default anywhere starts a session: `RunServices.backend` has no default, the backend is created lazily at a start, `recover()` never resumes a session by itself (a restored question waits for the user's answer, an interrupted run for "Resume"), the walkthrough script is live only with `--live` plus `TELELEAN_WALKTHROUGH_LIVE=yes`, and (fixer round 1) M0's smoke script `scripts/smoke-claude.mjs` is dry by default and live only with `--live` plus `TELELEAN_SMOKE_LIVE=yes` (either alone refuses before any module is loaded or binary resolved; runner `test/run/smokeScript.test.ts`).
The integrator greps the test sources for `createClaudeBackend(` and `new ClaudeCliBackend(` and checks every hit is a fake-binary or double test.

## 10. Test isolation and resource rules

- **Temp dirs**: tests create scratch trees under `$TELELEAN_TEST_TMP` (runner helper `makeTempRoot`); builders set it to their scratch dir. When it is unset, tests use a fresh `mkdtemp` under `os.tmpdir()`, never anything under the real `$HOME`. Never build inside `mental_model/` or `test-fixtures/` (copy first).
- **Chrome (Playwright, WP6)**: `launchOptions.env` gets `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` pointing into the run's short temp dir (the one `chrome-tmp.ts` already makes for `TMPDIR`), plus `--disable-crash-reporter --disable-breakpad --no-first-run`; the npm script runs `sh -c 'ulimit -c 0; playwright test'`. One worker.
- **VS Code (WP5)**: a pretest script makes `$TELELEAN_TEST_TMP/vscode-<pid>/{home,xdg-config,xdg-cache,xdg-data,user-data,extensions,ws}` (passing the path to `.vscode-test.mjs` through an environment variable), copies `mental_model/` to `ws/mental_model` (until WP4 has written it: `test-fixtures/spyro` plus a generated `.telelean/config.json` and empty layout, in the copy only), and writes `user-data/User/settings.json` with `"chat.disableAIFeatures": true`, `"telemetry.telemetryLevel": "off"`, `"update.mode": "none"`, `"extensions.autoUpdate": false`, `"extensions.autoCheckUpdates": false`, `"workbench.enableExperiments": false`, `"security.workspace.trust.enabled": false`. `.vscode-test.mjs` passes `--user-data-dir`, `--extensions-dir` (test-electron adds its own `.vscode-test/user-data` only when these are absent: verified in `@vscode/test-electron` 3.1.0 `util.js`), `--disable-extensions`, `--disable-telemetry`, `--disable-workspace-trust`, and env `HOME`/`XDG_*` to those dirs, `ELAN_HOME=/home/zhengyew/.elan` (read-only use by runLean), `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`; `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` stay (systemd-run --user needs them). Script: `sh -c 'ulimit -c 0; env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE xvfb-run -a npx vscode-test'`. Afterwards assert that the isolated `user-data` dir was used (files appeared in it) and that nothing new appeared in the real `~/.copilot`, `~/.config/Code`, `~/.config/google-chrome` (compare listings before/after in the test script).
- **Git in tests** (WP4/WP5): only in scratch repositories; `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=$TELELEAN_TEST_TMP` (discovery never leaves the scratch tree), the safe `-c` flags, explicit author.
- **RAM**: `free -m` before heavy steps; one heavy process at a time (one `lake build`, one VS Code instance, one browser); vitest `fileParallelism: false`; `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4`; every Lean process under runLean's memory cap; `ulimit -c 0` in every test script that starts Lean, Chrome or VS Code.

input.package_overview:
Four independent suites, one per package, all deliberately sequential (vitest fileParallelism: false, one Playwright worker, one VS Code instance at a time) because of the RAM rule. File headers cite acceptance-test ids from docs/m1-plan.md or docs/m2-plan.md; the two plans reuse AT1.x-AT6.x for different work packages (M1: markup, model/planner, semantic, workspace, extension, webview; M2: gate rules, engine/shadow, RunManager, proposals, extension, webview).

core (pure TS; `cd packages/core && npm test` = tsc -p tsconfig.test.json, then vitest run). Unit tests of markup (lexer, parser, serializer, values, edits, Lean ops; ported research cases, property, robustness and scale tests), the project model (statuses, edges, vocabulary, stale facts, subjects, diagnostics), the planner (D-11, delete, conditional proofs, carry-overs), graph.json and its committed schema, the protocol, and the M2 gate rules (G0, permitted set/freeze, evaluateRules incl. cheats, carriers, notices, normalisation, ghost adoption) plus proposal codecs/diff. Lean facts are hand-written JSON (test/fixtures/project), derived from text (project/helpers/fakeFacts.ts) or recorded from real Lean 4.35 (gate/realFacts). Fixtures are read through Vite `?raw` (core has no Node types).

runner (Node; `cd packages/runner && npm test` = vitest run with TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1 and 180 s timeouts; `npm run typecheck` checks src and tests). Three layers. (1) Parsers on recorded Lean/Lake output and pure helpers (semantic/*, gate/pure, llm/streamJson, llm/argvEnv, lean/profile-shadow). (2) Real-Lean integration under runLean (systemd-run --user scope, bwrap, MemoryMax, toolchain v4.35.0 from ~/.elan, LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4) on scratch copies of test-fixtures/ or mental_model/, git only in scratch repos: lean/*, semantic/refresh, gate/engine and gate/rules (Claude played by test-fixtures/gate/edits.json), shadow, workspace, proposal/build, integration/*, and run/walkthrough.e2e, where the FakeBackend plays test-fixtures/walkthrough/*.json: both readings plus a 20-script cheat catalogue (added axiom, sorry, weakened abbrev/type, unselected premise, rebind-target, helper lemma, definition-belief, redefined vocabulary, #eval, proof before freeze, edited words, give-up, goal-premise axiom/belief, derivation-premise proof, private lemma, two carrier cases, example). These assert that no telelean-<runId>-* systemd unit is left; several skip below 12 GB MemAvailable. (3) Fakes: run/manager.* via run/helpers (FakeEngine, FakeShadow, fake services, TrackingBackend, fake timers); llm/* against the FakeBackend, the CLI double fixtures/fake-claude.mjs with a real loopback MCP server, and the path-guard hook. Knobs: TELELEAN_TEST_TMP, TELELEAN_KEEP_TMP=1, TELELEAN_ALLOW_REAL_CLAUDE_VERSION=1.

extension: `npm run test:unit` (vitest; `vscode` aliased to test/unit/vscodeStub.ts) covers host logic, the edit applier, manifest/settings, the bundle, host restore and run wiring. `npm run build:all && npm run test:smoke`: scripts/smoke.mjs makes an isolated profile under $TELELEAN_TEST_TMP/vscode-<pid> (HOME, XDG_*, user-data, extensions, a ws with model copies) and runs `xvfb-run npx vscode-test` (VS Code 1.140.0, mocha tdd) as two instances: smoke (activation, board, boards with a fake workspace via testing.useRunner, model with the real workspace and Lean, runs with a FakeBackend) and e2e (e2e.test.ts, e2e-runs.test.ts driving the real board over CDP). Afterwards it fails on changes in the real ~/.config/Code, ~/.copilot, Chrome dirs or trash and on leftover processes or units. TELELEAN_SMOKE_GREP filters; `npm test` runs typecheck, build, unit and smoke.

webview: `npm run test:unit` (DOM-free store, run model, geometry, edges, formatting, card data, theme CSS); `npm run build && npm run test:e2e` runs Playwright (installed Chrome, headless, one worker) on the built bundle served at 127.0.0.1:41739 with a mock acquireVsCodeApi and the real CSP. Every spec fails on console, page or CSP errors; home-guard and chrome-tmp keep Chrome out of the real home. Root `npm test` runs every package's script.

Quota tripwires (plan 10.4): (1) TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1 in both vitest configs, .vscode-test.mjs and smoke.mjs: createClaudeBackend refuses without a scratch resolve, and ClaudeCliBackend.startSession launches only node plus a test-fixture double (llm/tripwire, run/backend). (2) The Test-mode extension never builds the real backend; only testing.useRunBackend installs one (unit/runBackend, hostRuns, realRuns). (3) The live scripts are dry by default and refuse half-armed or tripwired runs (run/smokeScript, walkthroughScript, quotaTripwire). No test runs real Claude.

Docs vs code: core edit/conditional.test.ts cites a missing runner integration/conditional.test.ts (its real-Lean counterpart is integration/fixes.test.ts); helper headers (fakeMarkup, scenarios, parseFixture, gate/helpers, run/helpers/*, proposal/helpers, m2-carryover.spec) still describe stubs and gated blocks, but nothing is gated now; no test reads llm/fixtures/recorded-cli-2.1.314 although docs/m2-plan.md says tests use it; the walkthrough README says the RunManager unit tests use its scripts, but they script inline.

input.package_overview:
@telelean/core is the pure-TypeScript heart of telelean. The runner (Node), the extension host and the React webview all share it. tsconfig.json limits it to lib ES2023 with no DOM or Node typings, so it does no I/O: every function takes texts, parsed files or models and returns data. It holds no LLM code: the gate rules here are the non-LLM judge of Claude's work. Other packages do not use dist/; their tsconfig/vite/vitest configs alias `@telelean/core` to src/index.ts. The only runtime dependency, zod, is used solely by export/schema.ts. index.ts deliberately does not re-export that file, which keeps the webview bundle free of zod. The package has 48 vitest files under test/; this survey does not cover them.

Module groups:
- Contracts (marked FROZEN, additive changes only): model.ts (TlNode/TlEdge/TlGraph, D-15 derived statuses, vocabulary, Lean-check state); facts.ts (the LeanFacts the runner's sandboxed `lake build` plus check file produce); actions.ts (BoardAction -> EditPlan -> FileChange, ActionError, history/undo types); run.ts (M2 run, proposal and sidecar record types); protocol.ts (versioned host<->webview messages with hand-written validators); paths.ts and layout.ts (folder and sidecar conventions).
- markup/: a lexer faithful to Lean 4.35, a declaration-header scanner, and the `@@ telelean v1` block parser. The parser reports TL0xx diagnostics and binds blocks (a pinned `lean:` beats adjacency). The group also has the serializer, byte-preserving field/block edits, and LeanOps (D-11 rewrites, D-9 docstring mirror).
- project/: buildProjectModel merges parsed files, file hashes and LeanFacts (FactsIndex: fresh, stale-by-name, unchecked) into a ProjectModel. That covers ids, bindings, declaration ownership, D-3 vocabulary classification, statement closures, proof statuses with footprints, status flags, TL1xx diagnostics and D-13 edges. Verified edges come from `.ilean` references, not from footprints. subjectGraph cuts out one subject's TlGraph and adds foreign vocabulary and the M2 externalUsers.
- edit/ plus kindChange.ts: planAction plans BoardActions through EditSession, which re-parses between steps, keeps other cards' bindings and yields whole-file changes plus layout/attic data. planKind applies the D-11 table using the facts (mark-broken, or a mechanical hypothesis rewrite, with confirmedDependents). kindChange.ts is the graph-only preview the webview shows during a drag.
- export/: graph.json format 1.1, plus its zod schema and the JSON Schema generated from it.
- gate/ (M2): the prototype gate's pure rules. These are the G0 token and file rules, the ghost single-term rule, the D-5 permitted set and freeze snapshot, and evaluateRules (G1 errors read from facts, G3, G5 and the stage/readiness rules over the B/A/S models). Also here: pre-gate normalisation, ghost adoption, lifecycle edits, and plain-language sentences for findings. The sandboxed build itself and G4 (the comparator) run in the runner.
- proposal/ (M2): board diff, accepted-proposal label, codecs for attempts.jsonl and decisions.json.
- samples/ and graph.ts: the frozen Spyro sample, a generated large graph, and M0 helpers that the webview still uses (slugId, createUserNode, columnOrder).

Data flow: the runner parses every model file (parseLeanFile) and builds the model with the latest facts. It publishes subjectGraph boards (attaching attempts itself) and writes toGraphJson output to .telelean/graph.json. The extension posts each board as a `graph` message, which the webview checks with parseHostToWebview. Webview messages go through parseWebviewToHost in the extension and become BoardActions. The runner plans them with planAction and applies them as FileChanges plus sidecars. In M2 the runner builds models of the user's base, the shadow and the adoption commits. At each gate it runs checkFileChanges, evaluateRules and the permitted-set code, phrases failures with attemptNotice, and builds ProposalViews with diffGraphs and the sidecar codecs.

Places where code and docs disagree:
- package.json's description still says the package holds only types, the protocol and samples.
- add-node's `preferredId` is documented as used, but nothing reads it; ids are always derived from the sentence.
- graph.json `attempts` is always []. Its comment says it is filled from M2 on, but neither core nor the runner fills it.
- The schema file is named 1.0, but the format is 1.1; the schema accepts any 1.x.
- The comments in gate/types.ts and gate/index.ts list fewer G0 tokens and ghost keywords than g0.ts checks. docs/m2-plan.md section 3.1 matches the code.

12	
13	Opening the board builds the model with Lean in place: `mental_model/.lake/` and `.telelean/graph.json` appear (both gitignored).
14	
15	## 2. Make a new model: `telelean: Initialize Model Here`
16	
17	Run it from the Command Palette, or right-click a folder in the Explorer.
18	
19	- **Empty folder:** it asks for the first subject's name (a Lean namespace such as `Spyro`; the default comes from the folder name) and writes the Lake project (`lakefile.toml` with `autoImplicit = false`, toolchain `v4.35.0`), `Model.lean`, `Model/<Subject>.lean`, `Model/<Subject>/{Vocabulary,Inbox,Main}.lean`, `.telelean/` and `.gitignore`.
20	- **Existing Lake project without dependencies:** it asks first, then only adds `.telelean/` and the missing `.gitignore` lines. Your Lean files are not changed.
21	- **Refused:** projects with Lake dependencies (Mathlib: M4), `lakefile.lean`-only projects (convert with `lake translate-config toml`), folders with other files but no lakefile.
22	- Then, if the folder is not inside a git repository, it offers `git init` for history (say no and history stays off; you can still accept later from the board).
23	- **A model folder that is already inside a git repository** (yours) gets history without being asked: opening its board writes "Initial state" snapshots there, as commits under private refs (`refs/telelean/…`; never a branch, never your staging area, never pushed). Section 9 says how to remove them.
24	
25	## 3. The board
26	
27	From top to bottom: the header (subject picker, History, Undo/Redo, Lean badge, Problems, legend), three columns (Assumptions, Derivations, Goals; each scrolls on its own), the selection tray, and the A|D|G box. The **Vocabulary group** is the first item of the Assumptions column, collapsed by default (click its heading to open it). **Problems** in the header lists the diagnostics of this subject. On a narrow board the columns keep a readable width and the board scrolls sideways.
28	
29	**Keyboard.** Tab moves between cards and buttons; on a focused card, Enter expands it, Space adds it to the selection (or takes it out), F2 edits its sentence, Delete opens the delete dialog and **Alt+Up / Alt+Down** moves it up or down in its column. Opening a dropdown (subject picker, History, Problems, "uses:") moves the focus into it: Up/Down/Home/End move between its items, Escape or choosing an item gives the focus back to its button. Saving or cancelling an in-place edit gives the focus back to the card.
30	
31	**Cards.** The face shows your sentence, "because: …" (your reason), the kind glyph **A**/**D**/**G**, status chips, and for formalised cards a "uses:" line. A glow (aura) means the card has a Lean statement. The chevron (or Enter on a focused card) expands it.
32	
33	**Expanded card.** Lean code with **Copy** (puts exactly that code on the clipboard) and **Open in editor** (opens the file beside the board, never over it); problems; "Rests on" (the assumptions its proof uses) and "Presupposes" chips; "Depends on / Used by"; stance and source chips; **Make Assumption / Make Derivation / Make Goal**; **Edit**, **Add why / Edit why**, **Delete**.
34	
35	**In the Lean code:** press and drag to select text (it never drags the card); hover an identifier for its gloss (or the card's sentence); click it to highlight the item in the Vocabulary group (or to reveal that card). Ctrl/Cmd+click is reserved for later.
36	
37	**"uses:" line.** The vocabulary the card's statement uses, from Lean, two names inline ("HasDarkPast, cynder, …"); **▾ N** lists all of them with kinds and glosses, and picking one highlights it.

# Decisions log (M1 and M2)

Sections 1–13 are M1 ("the map without AI"); sections 14–26 are M2 (one-shot "These suffice" with Claude), further down; section 27 lists the fixes after M2's verification (round 1, core, runner and docs), section 28 those of round 2 (core, runner, scripts and docs), section 29 those of round 3 (core, runner and docs), section 30 M2's closing fixes (runner, webview, extension and docs), section 31 those of the second closing round (docs, code comments and one new test). Decisions that wait for you are listed first, right below.

Every smaller decision taken while planning, building and integrating M1, grouped by topic. One line each: **the decision**, then why. Sources: plan = `docs/m1-plan.md` section 13.1 (architect and review); WP1–WP6 = the builders; int = the integrator; fix = the fixers after the verification (section 10 lists the core and runner ones, section 11 the extension and webview ones, sections 12 and 13 the two closing rounds). None of these needed your approval to proceed, and all of them can be reversed. If you disagree with one, say which and it can be changed.

Contract changes (new exports, optional fields) are listed separately in `docs/m1-plan.md` section 14.

## Decisions awaiting you

- **Where should "Raw Lean diff…" open: beside the board (the current default) or as a tab in the board's own group?** Beside the board, VS Code opens the diff in an editor group next to it; when the board is the only group the window splits, so the board shrinks to half its width while the diff is open (the board stays usable at that width). As a tab in the board's group, the diff opens over the board: the board keeps its full width but is hidden until you switch back to its tab. Nothing changes until you choose (sections 28, 29 and 30).


- **`AcceptProposalAction` stayed a separate type and the ModelWorkspace's M2 members stayed optional until integration.** The webview's exhaustive label table and the M1 test fakes kept compiling while the builders worked in parallel. *(plan)*
- **The runner's factories take core test hooks; cross-package tests were marked [gated] and ran at integration.** Each work package could test its own logic while the others were stubs. *(plan)*
- **The walkthrough fixtures carry test metadata (answer, premises, adopt, expected outcome) beside the playable turns, and turns are matched by their text.** A script stays in step across reminders and resumed sessions, and the tests and the dry-run script share the files. *(WP3)*
- **The VS Code run suite uses its own pristine model copy and inlines the normative script.** Another suite changes `ws/mental_model`; independent of the fixture format. *(WP5)*

## 26. Integration (int)

- **`HistoryActionKind` now includes `accept-proposal`, and the ModelWorkspace's M2 members are required; every builder gate (`isImplemented` and the webview's carry-over gate) is gone.** Plan 11 step 2; every test of the plan now runs. *(int)*
- **`RunManager.dispose()` writes run.json at once and returns a promise that resolves after the writes queued before it, with the final "interrupted" state written last (`RunFiles.close`).** Queued writes used to land after the synchronous one and leave run.json saying "working" (WP5's AT5.9). *(int)*
- **M1's integration tests confirm exactly the dependents the planner lists (both the derivation and the goal that uses it, for the "rewrite" of a change to Goal).** Carry-over 3 refuses a choice that does not cover every dependent. *(int)*
- **The VS Code run suite waits for a dismissed run to leave the board instead of for a reply.** `dismissRun` carries no request id (plan 6.3), so no reply comes; the old wait timed out after 240 s. *(int)*
- **A new end-to-end suite (`e2e-runs.test.ts`) drives "These suffice" through the real board over the DevTools protocol in the e2e instance, on its own model copy (`runs-e2e/runs_e2e_model`); the smoke instance's file pattern excludes `e2e*`.** Only trusted clicks in the real webview show that the question card, the overlay, the review, the ghost card and Accept work end to end. *(int)*
- **That suite installs one backend that switches FakeBackend scripts per test (WP5's run suite now does the same for its hanging backend).** The RunManager keeps the backend its factory returned, so a script per run needs a switch rather than a new factory; WP5's suite only worked when an earlier test had happened to reload the window. *(int)*
- **After each test that suite ends any run the test left (Discard or Cancel, then Dismiss) and restores the copy's files.** One failed assertion used to leave the board in review and fail every later test too. *(int)*
- **A runner integration test (`test/integration/m2flow.test.ts`) runs the plan's 11.4 flows in a user's repository layout: Accept/Undo/Redo/History revert, literal adoption, Accept after drift (merge and conflict), the premises declaration and a refused start, recovery with a pending question.** The plan's integrator test; it also checks that HEAD, index, branches, config, hooks and status outside the model never change. *(int)*
- **The root build's npm debug logs go to the integrator's scratch folder (`npm_config_logs_dir`), never `logs-max=0`.** npm would otherwise write into and prune the real `~/.npm/_logs`. *(int)*
- **`RunView.updatedAt` is left as it is: it is already stamped at the same moment as Claude's working time.** The board's clock interpolation (WP6) needed exactly that; no change was required. *(int)*
- **A refused re-freeze after an adoption leaves its `adopt` commit in the working copy's history; left as it is.** The rules consult that reference only for adopted cards, whose text it holds unchanged; no wrong verdict follows (checked by analysis and the end-to-end tests). *(int)*
- **`.telelean/graph.json` still lists no attempts (`attempts: []`); only the board's graphs carry them.** graph.json's export takes no attempts; left for later (WP4 note). *(int)*

# Design amendments (turn 2, 2026-11-01)

These amend `verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_1/user_requested_documents/02_design_decisions.md` and `03_architecture.md`, and take precedence where they conflict. The ★ recommendations were approved with the notes below.

## A1 · D-23(a): Claude is driven through your installed Claude Code CLI (the learnharness pattern), behind an LLM-agnostic interface

**What telelean does.** It starts `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json …` in a copy of your model files ("the shadow"). The flags allow:
- the file tools (Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write) and telelean's own tools, and nothing else: no shell, no web;
- none of your Claude Code settings, hooks or CLAUDE.md;
- no API-key or cloud-provider environment variables, so you are never billed per token by accident.

**Where telelean's tools live.** Tools such as `ask_user`, `check_lean` and `finish` are served over a local **MCP** server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give an agent tools, and most agent CLIs support it.

**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. For an agent CLI that speaks MCP, the adapter is its flags plus parsing its event stream; an API-key provider is a further option. Telelean never handles anyone's login or keys.

**Which binary.** By default, the Claude Code that ships with your VS Code Claude extension, found automatically. A setting can override it.

**Dropped:** the Claude Agent SDK dependency (proprietary licence, plus its own ~330 MB binary).

**Traded away:**
- *Then:* in-process hooks and typed events. *Now:* a command hook, plus parsing the CLI's JSON event stream.
- *Then:* resilience to CLI updates. *Now:* the event stream is more fragile across updates, so a minimum-version check and a recorded stream in the tests catch breakage.

**Your reading of the policy is correct, with two nuances.** This is not legal advice.
1. **The CLI pattern doesn't "offer claude.ai login".** Each user signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, which is the case Anthropic's legal page explicitly allows.
2. **The Consumer Terms' clause on "automated or non-human means" still governs subscription use.** You start every run and it waits on your answers, which keeps it ordinary individual use. If you share telelean, the clean route is to point users at an API key or another provider.

## A2 · The gate loop (your proposal, adopted)

1. Claude says it is finished.
2. Telelean runs **non-LLM checks** on Claude's working copy. Each must hold:
   - the files build in the sandbox;
   - `#print axioms` lists only your selected assumptions, plus the "X exists" presuppositions of the things they mention;
   - there is no `sorry`;
   - the goal statement is identical to the one frozen before proving (via `lake comparator`);
   - there are no forbidden commands (`#eval` etc.);
   - your natural-language text is untouched.
3. **On failure** the board shows a small notice. For example: *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it used `foo`, which you didn't select. Asking Claude to retry."* Claude is re-prompted automatically with the exact failure.
4. **After 3 failed attempts**, a setting you can change, the board tells you what kept failing. It then **reverts the working copy to the last state that passed**. The attempt is kept in the history.

Your real files are never touched until you press Accept, so "revert" only ever applies to Claude's copy.

**What is a question for you, not a retry.** These need your judgement, which a program can't supply:
- a new definition or vocabulary item (yes/no);
- a proposed missing premise (a ghost node: "I hold this" / "no");
- whether the Lean says what your sentence says (the meaning review).

**The honest limit.** The checks guarantee that the goal follows from the selected assumptions *as formalised*. Whether the formalisation matches your meaning is what the review step (and M3's faithfulness tools) is for.

## A3 · D-33: history dropdown with revert and a storage counter

**Storage.** Every change telelean writes is first snapshotted as a private git ref in the model folder (`refs/telelean/…`); your branches are never touched. Git stores files compressed and deduplicated, so a snapshot costs only what changed, typically a few KB.

**The dropdown** (board header):
- Each entry shows time · action · one-line summary, e.g. *"These suffice → proved cynder-not-good"*.
- Selecting an entry previews that state read-only, with its diff.
- **Revert to this** first snapshots the current state, so a revert can itself be undone.

**The counter** shows disk use per subject and in total. It measures **disk, not RAM**: snapshots sit on disk and add nothing to memory pressure. A "keep the last N" pruning option is included.

**When:** M1, together with the board's first writes.

## A4 · D-10: several subjects per project

D-10 is attempted in M1: one module subtree and namespace per subject, plus a subject picker. If it proves complex, M1 ships one subject first. Comparing models, your two-person "convince someone" setting, is deferred and may need its own analyses.

## A5 · D-31, D-32

- **D-31:** headless extension tests use `xvfb-run`.
- **D-32:** dropped. `mental_model/` is the sample model workspace.

## A6 · M0 contents (replaces the M0 row of 03 §11 / D-29)

M0 is three spikes, each independently verified:
1. Sandboxed Lean runs (memory cap + bwrap), with `lake comparator` running under them.
2. The Claude CLI harness, built offline: provider interface, flags, environment sanitising, MCP tool server, file-confinement hook, a fake backend for tests.
3. The board prototype in a real VS Code webview.

After those, one small real-Claude smoke test, announced to you before it runs. It covers your login, a long blocking question, file confinement, and resuming after a reload.

/**
 * The Lean check engine (contracts in ./types.ts; docs/m2-plan.md sections 3, 4.3 and 7.1).
 *
 *   checkBase  sync the mirror to the base, build (no G0: the user's own text); errors -> problems naming file:line;
 *              otherwise B's facts are kept in `<runDir>/base-facts.json`
 *   check      G0 (core checkFileChanges on B vs ws/) -> only if clean: sync the mirror, build + facts (one Lean job)
 *              -> core project models (B with B's facts, A = the newest `adopt` commit, the round start, S with the
 *              fresh facts) -> core evaluateRules
 *   freeze     check (purpose freeze) -> core permitted set + frozen snapshot -> lake's challenge in a copy of the
 *              mirror without the target's `.holds` and its transitive users -> commit `freeze`
 *   normalise  core normalisationChanges for the selection's statements new since B -> commit `normalise`
 *   gate       judge one committed state: G0, G1, G3, G5 via check (purpose gate-*), then G4 for `proved` only
 *   checkGhost single-term rule (no Lean) -> a clean check of ws/ -> the pinned scratch check (fact 7)
 *   render     `#print` default and explicit forms from a scratch check file
 *
 * Every Lean job runs through semantic.runExclusive under runLean with the run id as scope group (so
 * `lean.cancelRun(runId)` stops it); the memory guard is applied right before each spawn. Lean and sandbox failures
 * never throw: `timeout`/`oom` are `budget` findings (counted), everything else telelean could not do is an
 * `environment` outcome (not counted). Only invalid arguments throw TypeError.
 */
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { mkdir, readdir, readFile, rename, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks';

import {
  ActionError,
  buildProjectModel,
  checkFileChanges,
  computePermittedAxioms,
  evaluateRules,
  frozenSnapshot,
  ghostTextProblems,
  holdsName,
  normalisationChanges,
  parseLeanFile,
  scanForbidden,
  SORRY_AXIOM,
  type FileChange,
  type FrozenSnapshot,
  type GateFinding,
  type LeanFacts,
  type ProjectModel,
  type RulePurpose,
} from '@telelean/core';

import { freezeChallenge, holdsTarget, runComparator, type ComparatorVerdict, type FreezeResult } from '../lean/comparator.js';
import { parseLeanJsonMessages } from '../lean/footprint.js';

## 12. The real-Claude walkthrough (main session only, after integration)

### 12.1 The script (built by WP3)

`node scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs [--dry-run] [--live] [--reading normative|literal|both] [--model claude-opus-5-5] [--effort high] [--work-dir DIR] [--max-turns 80] [--max-checks 25] [--max-agent-minutes 20] [--binary PATH] [--approve-definitions]`. It bundles the runner into the work dir, copies `mental_model/` to `<work>/model-<reading>/`, initialises git there (isolated config), runs one Lean refresh, and drives the RunManager like a user: answers a question whose phenomenon is `modality` or whose text mentions "cannot" with free text (normative: "I mean it as a rule: PG games should not include characters with dark pasts. I do not mean it is impossible for a PG game to contain one."; literal: "I mean it literally: a PG game cannot contain a character with a dark past at all."), answers any other question with "Decide for me", adopts the first ghost with `closesGap` in the literal reading, accepts proved proposals with the recommended lifecycle items (definition questions only with `--approve-definitions`; otherwise it stops and reports them), then refreshes the copy and records the final statuses. Dry run = FakeBackend scripts of section 10.2 (contacts nothing; the script sets `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1` for itself; `--dry-run --binary-check` additionally runs only `claude --version` through `llm.resolveClaudeBinary` and builds the argv with `ClaudeCliBackend.prepare`, which spawns nothing, then prints the resolved binary, argv, sanitised environment names, settings, MCP config without the token, and the system prompt; it never calls `startSession`). Live = ClaudeCliBackend, only with `--live` and `TELELEAN_WALKTHROUGH_LIVE=yes` (either alone refuses before any binary is resolved). The live run stops (cancels) at the first `rate_limit` event whose status is not `allowed`.

### 12.2 Procedure

1. Preconditions: integration done, all suites green, `--dry-run` passes for both readings, `free -m` shows ≥ 12 GB available, no other heavy process running, and `TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE` not set in the shell that runs the live command (with it set the live run refuses at once: safe, but it would look like a failure).
2. `node scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --dry-run --binary-check` → note the binary (expected: the VS Code Claude extension's `resources/native-binary/claude`, version ≥ 2.1.295, e.g. 2.1.314) and confirm the argv has no `--bare` and the environment strips `CLAUDE*`/`ANTHROPIC_*`.
3. Tell the user before spending quota: two live runs on the default model, roughly the numbers in 12.3.
4. Normative: `TELELEAN_WALKTHROUGH_LIVE=yes node scripts/walkthrough-claude.mjs --live --reading normative --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --work-dir <scratch>/m2-walkthrough`. Pass: subscription auth verified before the first prompt; Claude asks about the modality (or formalises the normative reading directly and lists it under assumed_without_asking); freeze; gate passes with verdict proved (gate attempts ≤ 3); lifecycle G→D offered and applied; after Accept the copy's refresh shows `cynder-not-good` proved, DERIVATION, footprint = the three premises + two presuppositions.
5. Literal: the same with `--reading literal`. Pass: round 1 verdict not-proved with at least one ghost that closes the gap; after adoption round 2 is proved; the adopted card carries `worded_by: agent`; the copy refreshes to proved.
6. If a reading fails: record everything, do not loop; at most one retry per reading, and only after reading the transcript (a different but faithful formalisation is acceptable; a cheat that the gate caught is a pass of the gate, not of the walkthrough).
7. Record, per reading: `summary.json` (verdict per round, gate attempts with failures, notices, questions asked and the answers given, ghosts, flagged definitions, the final diff of the copy, final statuses), `transcript.jsonl`, usage (requests, input / output / cache-read / cache-write tokens, the CLI's cost estimate, rate-limit events), durations (wall, agent-active), CLI and model versions, the guard log (denials, if any). Save them into the prompt log's bundle as the walkthrough report. Also report the effects outside the scratch dir: the CLI itself stores each session's transcript under `~/.claude/projects/<its encoding of the shadow's ws/ path>/<session id>.jsonl` (that is how `--resume` works; telelean never reads it, and the main session reports the directory names, not contents); `~/.elan/known-projects` line count before and after (expected unchanged); no `telelean-*` systemd unit left.
8. Optional, with the user: the same flow in VS Code (Extension Development Host on a copy of `mental_model/`), pressing These suffice on the board.

### 12.3 Expected cost (an estimate, not a measurement)

Per reading, about 10–20 model requests (normative) and 20–35 over two rounds (literal); each request carries the cached system prompt, tool schemas and conversation (~10–30k input tokens, mostly cache reads), so both readings together ≈ 0.5–1.5 M cache-read tokens, 50–150 k cache-write tokens, a few thousand uncached input tokens, and 20–60 k output tokens at effort high. Wall time ≈ 5–15 minutes per reading. The CLI reports its own cost estimate at API list prices (M0's smoke test: 8 Haiku requests ≈ $0.003); a subscription is not billed per token, but this is ordinary quota use, so the main session announces it first and stops at any rate-limit warning.

# Part 2: Functionality and features

This part covers what a user can do with telelean today and what happens when they do it. It was checked against the code as of 2026-11-02:

- the extension manifest and host (`packages/extension`);
- the React board (`packages/webview`);
- the runner (`packages/runner`);
- the pure core (`packages/core`).

It was also compared with `docs/user-guide.md` and with the last verifier report (`verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_9/subagent_reports/m2c_workflow/agents/m2close-verify-2.md`). The built bundles in `packages/extension/dist/` are newer than every source file, so an installed extension runs exactly this code. Where the user guide and the code disagree, the text says **Docs vs code**; section 2.7.3 lists all of these places.

**Status in brief.**
- **M1, the board without AI, is complete.**
- **M2, one-shot "These suffice" with Claude, is implemented and integrated.** Every M2 flow has been run with a scripted fake Claude (the FakeBackend), including real clicks through the board in a VS Code test instance.
- **Real Claude has never driven the M2 code.** The only contact with real Claude so far was M0's eight-request smoke test of the command-line harness.
- **The last verification round ended "needs-work", with minor issues only** (section 2.7.2).

---

## 2.1 Setting up and running

### 2.1.1 What the machine needs

- **Linux with the sandbox tools.** Lean checks need four things:
  - bubblewrap (`bwrap`);
  - a reachable systemd user manager (`systemd-run --user`, `systemctl --user`);
  - cgroup v2 with the memory controller;
  - util-linux `setpriv`.

  All four are in `/usr/bin` on this machine. Without them, checks fail closed: the board shows "Lean: off" with "sandbox unavailable: …".
- **Lean `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0` under `~/.elan`** (or `$ELAN_HOME`). telelean calls `~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.35.0/bin/lake` and `lean` directly, never elan's proxies, so it never writes `~/.elan/known-projects`. That toolchain is installed here.
- **git**, for history. It is optional; the setting `telelean.git.path` chooses the executable.
- **For M2: Claude Code 2.1.295 or newer, logged in with a claude.ai subscription.** By default telelean uses the binary inside the VS Code Claude Code extension. Here that is `~/.vscode/extensions/anthropic.claude-code-2.1.314-linux-x64/resources/native-binary/claude`.
- **VS Code 1.140 or newer.** Building needs Node 24.22.2 (`.node-version`).

### 2.1.2 Build, install, reload

- **There is no VSIX package.** Packaging is an optional M4 item. The extension runs from its folder.
- **Building, only after a source change.** Run `npm run build` at the repository root. It does four things:
  - builds core with `tsc`;
  - bundles the extension host with esbuild, which also copies the Claude path-guard hook to `packages/extension/dist/bin/telelean-path-guard.mjs`;
  - builds the runner with `tsc`;
  - builds the webview with Vite into `packages/extension/dist/webview/`.

  `npm --prefix packages/extension run build:all` rebuilds only the webview and the extension bundle. At the moment nothing needs rebuilding.
- **Installing, once.** Run **Developer: Install Extension from Location…** and pick `/home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/extension`. The user guide says this was done in M0; the M0 report offered it as optional. VS Code registers the folder, so after a rebuild **Developer: Reload Window** loads the new `dist/`.
- **Trust.** The manifest declares untrusted workspaces unsupported, because building a model with Lean can run code. VS Code therefore disables the extension in Restricted Mode and in virtual workspaces.

### 2.1.3 Commands and activation

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **telelean: Open Board** (`telelean.openBoard`) | Command Palette | Opens, or reveals, the board of a model folder (2.1.5). |
| **telelean: Initialize Model Here** (`telelean.initializeModel`) | Command Palette; Explorer right-click on a folder | Turns a folder into a model (2.1.4). |
| **telelean: Refresh Lean Check** (`telelean.refresh`) | Command Palette | Re-checks the focused board, or the only open board. With several open and none focused it asks which; with none open it runs Open Board. |

- **Keybindings and menus.** No keybindings are contributed. Apart from the Explorer entry, no menu items are contributed.
- **Activation.** The extension activates by itself in windows that contain `**/.telelean/config.json`, when VS Code restores a board tab, and when one of its commands runs. Activation reads no model file, runs no Lean and looks for no Claude binary until a board opens.
- **Log.** Its log is **View → Output → telelean**.

### 2.1.4 Initialize Model Here

1. **Folder.** It uses the folder you right-clicked. Otherwise it shows a quick pick of the window's folders plus "Choose another folder…".
2. **Inspection.** telelean inspects the folder and acts on what it finds.

   - **Already a model.** It says so and opens the board.

   - **Empty folder** (no visible entries). It asks for the first subject's name: a capitalised Lean identifier of at most 64 characters, suggested from the folder name (for example `mental_model` → `MentalModel`). Then it writes:
     - `lakefile.toml`, with `autoImplicit = false`, `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` and one `[[lean_lib]] Model`;
     - `lean-toolchain`, set to `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0`;
     - `lake-manifest.json`, with no packages;
     - the missing `.gitignore` lines: `/.lake/`, `/.telelean/graph.json`, `/.telelean/frozen/`, `/.telelean/sessions/`, `/.telelean/*.tmp`;
     - `Model.lean` and `Model/<S>.lean`;
     - `Model/<S>/{Vocabulary,Inbox,Main}.lean`, each `namespace <S> … end <S>` with a one-line comment;
     - `.telelean/config.json`;
     - `.telelean/subjects/<S>/layout.json`.

   - **Lake project without dependencies.** It asks first, in a modal: "Add telelean to the Lake project …?". Then it writes only `.telelean/config.json` (with the project's library name), a layout file per subject it found, and the missing `.gitignore` lines. It does not change any Lean file.

   - **Refused, with the reason.** It refuses in these cases:
     - Lake dependencies (Mathlib comes in M4);
     - a project configured only by `lakefile.lean` (Lake can convert it with `lake translate-config toml`);
     - both lakefiles at once;
     - no `[[lean_lib]]`, or a library name that is not a plain identifier;
     - a missing or invalid `lake-manifest.json`;
     - a folder that has files but no `lakefile.toml`.

3. **git offer.** If the folder is not inside a git repository, a modal offers `git init` for history. Saying no leaves history off; the board can still initialise git later. A folder already inside a repository gets history without being asked.
4. **Board.** telelean opens the board. Every file it writes goes through VS Code (one `WorkspaceEdit`) and is saved.

**Docs vs code (minor).** The user guide's file list leaves out `lake-manifest.json` and the layout file. It also does not say that an existing Lake project needs a `lake-manifest.json`.

### 2.1.5 Open Board

- **Finding models.** telelean searches the window's folders up to depth 6 for `.telelean/config.json`. It skips `node_modules`, `.lake`, `.git`, `verbatim_prompt_log` and `test-fixtures`. In this repository it finds only `mental_model/`, so opening `/home/zhengyew/telelean` opens that model directly.
- **Choosing.** One model opens directly. Several give a quick pick ("Which model?"). None gives an information message with **Initialize Model Here…**.
- **The tab.** There is one board per model folder, an ordinary editor tab titled `telelean: <folder>`. The parent folder is added to the title when two models share a name. Running the command again reveals the existing tab.
- **Restoring.** The tab survives a window reload: VS Code restores it, and the extension maps it back to its model and the subject it showed.
- **Loading errors.** If the model cannot be loaded, the tab says why. Fix the problem and run Open Board again; no reload is needed.
- **First check.** Opening the board starts a Lean check (2.3.9).
